items.title: Author Correction: Cretaceous bird from Brazil informs the evolution of the avian skull and brain
items.summary: This paper is an author correction notice addressing an error in a previously published study on a Cretaceous bird from Brazil and avian skull and brain evolution. The original analysis of the enantiornithine bird *Navaornis hestiae* contained misplaced anatomical landmarks on its endocranial model, caused by a sharp corner in the three-dimensional reconstruction that displaced semilandmarks to an incorrect surface. The authors corrected the landmark positions using updated software and reanalyzed the dataset, producing a revised principal components analysis of endocranial shape variation. The core finding that *Navaornis* occupies an intermediate morphological position between stem birds and crown birds along the primary axis of shape variation is unchanged, though the corrected data now place *Navaornis* within crown bird variation along a secondary axis rather than just outside it. Additional shape distance analyses confirm that *Navaornis* shares endocranial similarities with a mix of stem and crown bird taxa, reinforcing the original interpretation of its mosaic of plesiomorphic and crown bird-like brain features.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it concerns a Cretaceous-era bird fossil from Brazil that provides new insights into how the avian skull and brain evolved, representing a significant paleontological find relevant to understanding early bird evolution.
items.citation: Luis M. Chiappe, Guillermo Navalón, Agustín G. Martinelli et al.. Author Correction: Cretaceous bird from Brazil informs the evolution of the avian skull and brain. Nature. 2026

items.title: Temporal uncoupling of radial glia lineage progression in cortical organoids
items.summary: This paper investigated how radial glial progenitors progress through their lineage to generate the full diversity of excitatory cortical neurons, comparing this process between living animals and laboratory-grown brain organoids. The researchers adapted a mosaic genetic labeling technique, originally developed for in vivo use, to work in mouse embryonic stem cells, enabling precise clonal tracking of progenitor cells within self-organizing cortical organoids. They found that, unlike the strictly timed and stereotyped lineage progression observed in the developing cortex in vivo, radial glial progenitors in organoids display a high degree of plasticity in their proliferative behavior and show increased lineage restriction, resulting in diminished cell-type diversity within individual clones. Notably, these differences in clonal output occurred despite organoid progenitors displaying transcriptional profiles and lineage trajectories indistinguishable from their in vivo counterparts at the single-cell level. The authors conclude that non-cell-autonomous signals absent from self-organizing systems, likely provided by the native stem cell niche, are essential for the faithful temporal coordination of progenitor lineage progression and the generation of diverse cortical neuron subtypes within a clone.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that cortical organoids fail to faithfully recapitulate the timed progression of radial glia progenitor lineages, producing reduced clonal neuronal diversity due to the absence of external niche signals that normally regulate this process. The findings highlight a fundamental limitation of organoid models and point to non-cell-autonomous cues as essential regulators of cortical development.
items.citation: Melissa Stouffer, Osvaldo A. Miranda, Florian M. Pauler et al.. Temporal uncoupling of radial glia lineage progression in cortical organoids. Nature. 2026

items.title: Shared principles of human and bacterial antiviral immunity
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals that the fundamental mechanisms by which humans and bacteria defend against viruses are deeply conserved, suggesting universal rules governing host–virus conflict across vastly different forms of life. By identifying shared principles of pathogen sensing, signalling, and effector function, it offers a unifying framework for understanding antiviral immunity.
items.citation: Philip J. Kranzusch. Shared principles of human and bacterial antiviral immunity. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343
items.summary: This paper investigated the characteristics and causes of extreme historical flooding across Europe during the early fourteenth century, a period previously understood only partially. Using a new documentary dataset, the researchers identified sixteen major flood events occurring across much of Europe between late 1341 and 1343, four of which had return periods of five hundred to one thousand years. Rather than the previously recognized single extreme event, the Magdalena Flood of 1342, this work reveals that event was part of a prolonged and cascading sequence that made 1342 the year with the greatest number of extreme floods in the past seven centuries. The flood sequence carried substantial socio-economic consequences, including a paradigm shift in European flood mitigation practices. Volcanic eruptions and multi-annual Arctic sea ice retreat are proposed as plausible drivers of this unusual clustering, and the findings argue that risk management frameworks must account for the possibility of cascading extreme flood events occurring within short timeframes.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reconstructs a sequence of massive medieval floods that cascaded across an entire continent, revealing that modern flood management systems are not equipped to handle such chained extreme events. The findings underscore an urgent gap in current risk strategies by demonstrating that unusually clustered, large-scale floods are a real historical—and therefore future—possibility.
items.citation: Andrea Kiss, Alberto Viglione, Mariano Barriendos et al.. Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343. Nature. 2026

items.title: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
items.summary: The retinoblastoma protein Rb is a well-established tumour suppressor that represses E2F transcription factors to halt cell cycle progression, and CDK4/6 inhibitors exploit this function in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer by keeping Rb in its active, hypophosphorylated state. This study investigated how pharmacologically activated Rb reshapes chromatin and gene expression beyond simply arresting the cell cycle. Using breast cancer cell lines, patient-derived xenografts, and clinical samples, the researchers found that CDK4/6 inhibition drives Rb to redistribute across the genome, where it not only represses cell cycle gene promoters as expected but also integrates into oestrogen receptor transcriptional hubs to unexpectedly enhance oestrogen-responsive gene expression in an Rb-dependent manner, a process partly mediated through interaction with the chromatin regulator KDM5A. Many of the genes activated through this Rb-driven programme are pro-proliferative, and while anti-oestrogen therapy can neutralise this effect in endocrine-sensitive tumours—explaining the known synergy between CDK4/6 inhibitors and endocrine therapy—the programme persists in endocrine-resistant contexts such as those harbouring ESR1 mutations, limiting therapeutic efficacy. These findings recast Rb as a dual-function transcriptional regulator whose tumour-suppressive cell cycle arrest activity is partially counteracted by its own capacity to activate pro-proliferative transcriptional programmes.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals an unexpected self-limiting mechanism in a widely used cancer therapy: when CDK4/6 inhibitors activate Rb, the protein simultaneously drives transcription of oestrogen-responsive genes that undermine the very cell-cycle arrest the treatment is meant to sustain.
items.citation: April C. Watt, Antonio Ahn, Catherine Blyth et al.. Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer. Nature. 2026

items.title: Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders
items.summary: This paper investigated how parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons (PV INs) in the hippocampus regulate memory formation and how their dysfunction contributes to neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, and schizophrenia. The researchers designed an input-specific translatome screen to identify genes that regulate experience-dependent PV IN plasticity in the CA3/CA2 hippocampal subregion, finding that many of these genes are haploinsufficient in neurodevelopmental disorders, suggesting a shared mechanistic vulnerability. As a proof-of-concept, they targeted upregulation of one candidate gene, the homeobox transcription factor Meis2, specifically in CA3/CA2 PV INs of an adult neurodevelopmental disorder mouse model. This targeted intervention was sufficient to restore experience-dependent PV IN plasticity, improve hippocampal network properties including sharp-wave ripple activity, enhance cognition, and suppress seizures. The findings establish experience-dependent PV IN plasticity as a convergent mechanism across neurodevelopmental disorder risk genes and demonstrate that developmental circuit deficits can be reversed through targeted molecular intervention in adulthood.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a molecular target in a specific interneuron population whose manipulation can simultaneously rescue multiple debilitating features of neurodevelopmental disorders—including memory deficits, disrupted network function, and seizures—in an adult animal model, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue even after development is complete.
items.citation: Yu‐Tzu Shih, Jason Bondoc Alipio, Zin‐Juan Klaft et al.. Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders. Nature. 2026

items.title: A gas-enshrouded and gas-reddened black hole at cosmic dawn
items.summary: This paper investigates the formation mechanisms of supermassive black holes in the very early universe, a longstanding theoretical puzzle. Using observations of a source existing only around 660 million years after the Big Bang, the researchers identified extraordinary spectral features including an exceptionally large hydrogen Balmer break, broad multi-peaked emission, and Balmer line absorption. They model the source as a supermassive black hole surrounded by an extremely dense, turbulent, dust-free gas envelope, which accounts for the unusual spectral signatures. This configuration is consistent with theoretical models proposing that dense gas cocoons enable rapid black hole growth through super-Eddington accretion, potentially explaining how billion-solar-mass black holes emerged so early in cosmic history. Critically, the findings suggest that the redness of such objects, including the recently discovered class known as "little red dots," is caused by gas rather than dust, and that scattering rather than kinematics drives their complex spectral line shapes, implying that black hole mass estimates for these sources may be overestimated by orders of magnitude.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it offers direct observational evidence for how supermassive black holes grew so rapidly in the early universe—by accreting mass while shrouded in gas. The findings also suggest that this enshrouded state may explain the mysterious "little red dots" seen at cosmic dawn.
items.citation: Rohan P. Naidu, Jorryt Matthee, Harley Katz et al.. A gas-enshrouded and gas-reddened black hole at cosmic dawn. Nature. 2026

items.title: Towards an equitable future of global photovoltaic waste recycling
items.summary: The study examined the growing global crisis of photovoltaic waste, assessing how different recycling strategies—local versus outsourced—compare in terms of economic and climate outcomes across diverse regions and technologies over time. The researchers developed a comprehensive analytical framework that accounts for supply-side material constraints, regional heterogeneity, and anticipated technological progress. They found that global photovoltaic waste will accumulate to hundreds of millions of tonnes by mid-century, with middle-income regions becoming dominant contributors after roughly two decades, and that the break-even point for economically viable recycling remains more than a decade away. A combination of region-specific and outsourced recycling strategies was found to maximize global net benefits, substantially reducing greenhouse gas emissions and generating large cumulative economic returns, though outsourced recycling risks deepening inequality for low-income regions. The authors conclude that a declining-subsidy scheme alongside international cooperation focused on technology transfer and recycling capacity building in low-income regions represents the most equitable and scalable path toward photovoltaic waste circularity.
items.why_notable: The work draws attention by quantifying the massive scale of photovoltaic waste expected by mid-century and arguing that without regionally tailored recycling approaches and international collaboration, the burden of managing that waste will fall inequitably across the globe.
items.citation: Chen Wang, Jian Zuo, Xinyu Chen et al.. Towards an equitable future of global photovoltaic waste recycling. Nature. 2026

items.title: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
items.summary: This paper developed a new super-resolution microscopy framework that bypasses the need for external laser or light excitation by instead exploiting reaction-excited luminescence, including electrochemiluminescence, chemiluminescence, and bioluminescence. The central challenge addressed was that conventional reaction-based luminescent imaging is constrained to poor spatiotemporal resolution due to limited photon output. The authors created a combined experimental and computational approach called RIED, which uses a spatiotemporal recording strategy paired with entropy-weighted correlation and deconvolution to reconstruct super-resolution images from the sparse photon statistics characteristic of reaction-driven emission. Applying this framework, they achieved approximately one-hundred nanometer resolution imaging of intracellular organelles across all three luminescence modalities, demonstrated highly sensitive detection of surface proteins, and performed ultralong-term continuous live-cell super-resolution imaging of mitochondrial transfer dynamics spanning over forty hours. The work establishes a laser-free class of super-resolution microscopy with expanded potential for biological imaging where light excitation is problematic.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it introduces a chemistry-driven super-resolution imaging approach that simultaneously achieves three-dimensional, laser-free, highly sensitive, and ultralong-term live-cell imaging — capabilities that collectively overcome the spatiotemporal resolution barriers that have constrained existing reaction-based imaging methods.
items.citation: Wenxin Zhu, Chi Zhang, Jiahui Gui et al.. Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging. Nature. 2026

items.title: Degree-of-polarization modulation for high-dimensional optical computing
items.summary: This paper investigates the spatial modulation of the degree of polarization as a new controllable degree of freedom for optical information processing. The researchers engineered polarization statistics at the micrometre scale using a phase-only spatial light modulator, enabling fully programmable control over both the state of polarization and the degree of polarization across more than a thousand spatial modes. By mapping the red–green–blue colour space onto the full volume of the Poincaré sphere, they encoded colour images into a single-wavelength laser beam, a concept they term "polarization colours." This expanded dimensionality was applied to demonstrate fully parallel photonic classification of colour images using a high-dimensional photonic neural network and high-security multidimensional optical encryption. The work establishes degree-of-polarization modulation as a practical resource for advancing optical computing, photonic information processing, and cryptography.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates that engineering light statistics at the micrometre scale allows both the state and degree of polarization to be spatially programmed simultaneously, opening a new high-dimensional space for encoding and processing optical information.
items.citation: Claudio Conti, Claudio Conti, Davide Pierangeli. Degree-of-polarization modulation for high-dimensional optical computing. Nature. 2026

items.title: Neural basis of compositional control
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies distinct roles for specific brain regions in how humans flexibly combine and switch between goal-directed behavioral strategies. The findings challenge simpler accounts of decision-making by showing that value signals contextualize rather than continuously update control policies, with the hippocampus, anterior cingulate cortex, and orbitofrontal cortex each contributing differently to this compositional process.
items.citation: Assia Chericoni, Justin M. Fine, TAHA S. ISMAIL et al.. Neural basis of compositional control. Nature. 2026

items.title: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination
items.summary: Bridge recombinases from the IS110 transposon family use a bridge RNA to direct programmable recombination between donor and target DNA sequences, but the mechanism by which these elements excise from host genomes to form the circular intermediates needed for transposition had not been characterized. This study investigated the excision reaction of the IS621 recombinase–bridge RNA complex, finding that bridge RNA is weakly expressed from genomic loci and that excision proceeds less efficiently than insertion. Using cryo-electron microscopy, the researchers solved structures of the recombinase–bridge RNA complex bound to excision DNA substrates and compared these to previously determined insertion complex structures. While the insertion complex bends donor and target DNAs into a U-shaped configuration, the excision substrates adopt linear conformations that bind across both bridge RNA loops to form an X-shaped architecture, a geometry that reduces top-strand exchange efficiency and explains the natural bias toward insertion. The study also identifies specific dinucleotide interactions called handshake guides that similarly modulate both reactions, together providing a structural framework for the full IS110 transposition cycle and informing the rational design of programmable gene-editing tools.
items.why_notable: The work is attracting attention because cryo-electron microscopy structures reveal the precise structural basis by which a bridge recombinase controls the directional preference for DNA insertion over excision. This mechanistic insight is considered significant for its potential to guide the rational design of programmable gene-editing tools based on bridge recombination.
items.citation: Masahiro Hiraizumi, Januka S. Athukoralage, Nicholas T. Perry et al.. Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination. Nature. 2026

items.title: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that variation *within* species—not just the replacement of one species by another—plays a substantial role in shaping how tropical forests resist drought, with drier forests showing coordinated shifts toward greater embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins.
items.citation: Chris Smith-Martin, Robert Muscarella, Timothy Brodribb et al.. Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance. Nature. 2026

items.title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
items.why_notable: The work is drawing attention because newly detected bow shocks in the outer regions of the Helix Nebula offer direct observational evidence that fragmented stellar ejecta are being recycled back into the surrounding interstellar gas. This finding sheds light on a poorly understood process by which material shed by dying stars is reintegrated into the broader galactic environment.
items.citation: Pieter van Dokkum, Roberto Abraham, W. Paul Bowman et al.. Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula. Nature. 2026

items.title: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health
items.summary: This study investigated how maternal and early-life factors shape the infant gut microbiome, a topic whose determinants have remained poorly understood. Researchers conducted metagenomic sequencing of a large longitudinal collection of fecal samples from mother-infant pairs in a Dutch birth cohort, integrating these data with hundreds of clinical and exposure variables alongside sequencing of breast milk and vaginal microbiomes. They found that the maternal gut microbiome undergoes only subtle changes during pregnancy and postpartum, yet serves as a primary reservoir for infant gut strains, with transmission being time-dependent and influenced by maternal species abundance. Mode of delivery and feeding mode emerged as the dominant shapers of the infant gut microbiome and its functional profiles, while home versus hospital delivery was only moderately associated with infant gut microbiome composition. Notably, the maternal gut microbiome was identified as a predictor of infant eczema, underscoring the broader role of maternal microbial communities in shaping early infant health outcomes.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it identifies the maternal gut microbiome as a predictor of eczema in infants, suggesting that a mother's microbial composition influences her child's health outcomes beyond direct transmission.
items.citation: Trishla Sinha, Siobhan Brushett, Asier Fernández-Pato et al.. Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health. Nature. 2026

items.title: Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way
items.summary: This paper investigates the dark matter content of ultra-diffuse galaxies using stellar streams as a diagnostic tool. The researchers identified evidence for the first known extragalactic globular cluster stellar stream in deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1. The stream's morphology, color, and association with a compact source were used to support a globular cluster progenitor interpretation, and simulated globular cluster stellar populations successfully reproduced the observed surface brightness. Using generative stream modeling that fits dynamical models directly to the stream's morphology, the authors constrained both the mass of the progenitor system and the properties of the host dark matter halo, finding evidence for a massive dark matter halo around this ultra-diffuse galaxy. The work demonstrates that globular cluster stream analysis can be extended beyond the Milky Way, opening a new approach to studying dark matter in external galaxies.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it presents the first evidence of a globular cluster stellar stream discovered outside the Milky Way, extending a phenomenon previously known only in our own galaxy to an extragalactic setting. Beyond this observational milestone, the stream also serves as a probe of the dark matter content of its ultra-diffuse host galaxy.
items.citation: Julie Kiel Holm, Sarah Pearson, Jacob Nibauer et al.. Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way. Nature. 2026

items.title: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that the climate drivers of tropical-forest carbon storage differ across major regions, challenging simpler assumptions and highlighting that accurate predictions of how climate change will alter forest biomass require accounting for complex interactions among climate, topography, and soils.
items.citation: Matheus Henrique Nunes, Helene C. Muller‐Landau, Eric Bastos Görgens et al.. Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass. Nature. 2026

items.title: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO2 plane
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because researchers successfully fabricated a high-quality pristine monolayer cuprate superconductor containing just a single CuO₂ plane, an extreme structural limit for this class of materials. Using this platform, they were able to identify two distinct quantum critical phenomena arising in the transition region between the Mott insulating and superconducting phases.

items.title: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours

items.title: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
items.summary: This study investigated biomarkers associated with clinical benefit from perioperative nivolumab treatment in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, using data from the CheckMate 77T trial. Researchers analyzed circulating tumor DNA, molecular residual disease, genomic alterations in specific driver genes, and pathologic complete response in a subset of randomized patients receiving either nivolumab or placebo. Circulating tumor DNA clearance before surgery occurred more frequently in the nivolumab group than the placebo group and was associated with higher rates of pathologic complete response, while post-surgical molecular residual disease conversion to positive status predicted disease recurrence in both groups. Patients harboring alterations in genes including KEAP1, STK11, CDKN2A, and SMARCA4 appeared to derive prolonged event-free survival benefit from nivolumab compared with placebo. A machine-learning model further identified pre-surgical circulating tumor DNA clearance, tumor histology, disease stage, pathologic complete response, and nivolumab treatment as top predictors of prolonged event-free survival, collectively offering insight into potential predictive biomarkers for perioperative immunotherapy in resectable lung cancer.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it identifies potential predictive biomarkers that could help determine which non-small cell lung cancer patients are most likely to benefit from perioperative immunotherapy, addressing a critical gap in personalizing treatment decisions. The findings are grounded in data from a major clinical trial, lending them particular clinical relevance.
items.citation: Tina Cascone, Mark M. Awad, Jonathan Spicer et al.. Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer. Nature. 2026

items.title: How the human brain can pursue two goals at the same time
items.summary: This paper investigated how the human brain enables simultaneous pursuit of multiple goals, a capacity seen broadly in natural behavior. Using control theory, an engineering framework, the researchers inferred participants' goals while they played a simple video game that required balancing competing objectives. Neuronal recordings from three brain regions revealed how these areas work together, encoding a specific "goal-blending" variable that represents the weighted combination of multiple targets. The findings provide a mechanistic account of how the brain implements flexible, multi-goal behavior through coordinated activity across distinct neural circuits.
items.why_notable: This research draws attention by revealing the neural mechanism behind a fundamental cognitive ability — pursuing multiple goals simultaneously — showing how three brain regions coordinate to blend strategies, an insight derived by applying an engineering framework to human behavior.
items.citation: How the human brain can pursue two goals at the same time. Nature. 2026

items.title: Human brain stimulation engages different gene programs in different cell types
items.summary: This paper investigated the cellular and molecular responses to electrical brain stimulation as a potential therapeutic strategy for cognitive decline. The researchers examined the human temporal cortex to identify gene expression programs activated in different cell types during neuronal network stimulation. They found that electrical stimulation engages distinct, cell-type-specific genetic programs, and that these genetic signatures coincide with the strengthening of cell assemblies in human brain tissue, suggesting a molecular basis for stimulation-induced neural plasticity that could inform therapeutic development.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals that electrical brain stimulation triggers distinct gene programs depending on the specific cell type involved, offering new molecular insight into how this therapeutic approach works. These findings could help guide the development of more targeted stimulation-based treatments for cognitive decline.
items.citation: Human brain stimulation engages different gene programs in different cell types. Nature. 2026

items.title: Ultrafast temporal engineering of optical properties using terahertz light
items.summary: The paper studied photonic time crystals, which are optical systems whose properties such as refractive index are modulated strongly and rapidly in time. The researchers created such a crystal by directing an intense terahertz light wave onto a specially microstructured material that supports plasmonic excitations — collective oscillations of electrons. This all-optical approach achieved the rapid and strong temporal modulation of optical properties required for a photonic time crystal operating at high frequencies.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates a way to create a photonic time crystal entirely through light, using an intense terahertz pulse to rapidly and strongly modulate the optical properties of a structured material via its plasmons. The achievement opens new possibilities for controlling light propagation through time-varying optical systems without requiring conventional electronic or mechanical modulation.
items.citation: Ultrafast temporal engineering of optical properties using terahertz light. Nature. 2026

items.title: Bow shocks reveal how a dying star returns matter to interstellar space
items.summary: Deep imaging of ionized gas in the Helix Nebula was used to study the process by which a dying Sun-like star returns its material to the surrounding interstellar medium. The observations revealed numerous curved shock waves, called bow shocks, formed as ejected shells of stellar material fragment and accelerate outward from the star. The changing morphology of these bow shocks indicates that the shell fragments are progressively stripped, shredded, and mixed into the interstellar gas. This process is estimated to unfold over roughly ten thousand years, providing direct observational insight into how planetary nebulae recycle stellar matter back into space.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it provides direct observational evidence of the detailed physical process by which a dying Sun-like star returns its material to interstellar space, revealed through newly imaged bow shocks in the Helix Nebula. The findings show that ejected shell fragments are progressively stripped and mixed into surrounding interstellar gas on a timescale of roughly ten thousand years, offering a clearer picture of stellar mass-loss and galactic chemical enrichment.
items.citation: Bow shocks reveal how a dying star returns matter to interstellar space. Nature. 2026
