items.title: Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026
items.summary: The paper examined the emergence and spread of SARS-CoV-2 variant BA.3.2, a strain first identified in South Africa in late 2024 that carries a notably large number of mutations in the spike protein relative to the antigens used in current vaccines. Using a multimodal genomic surveillance strategy that integrated traveler-based screening, clinical specimen testing, and wastewater monitoring, public health authorities tracked the variant's introduction and domestic spread within the United States and internationally. BA.3.2 was first detected in the United States through a traveler arriving from the Netherlands, with subsequent detections in clinical patients, airplane wastewater, and community wastewater samples spanning a substantial number of states. The variant had also been reported across more than two dozen countries by the surveillance period's end. The authors conclude that the extent of spike protein divergence in BA.3.2 raises concern for reduced protection from prior infection or vaccination, underscoring the need for continued genomic surveillance to assess its public health impact.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Mila Shakya, Kevin C. Ma, Laura J. Hughes et al.. Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.
items.summary: This study examined the global research landscape at the intersection of wastewater metagenomics, antimicrobial resistance, and pathogen surveillance using bibliometric methods. The authors retrieved over a thousand publications from a major scientific database and applied network analysis tools to map publication trends, international collaborations, keyword evolution, and literature co-citation patterns across a fifteen-year period. They found that the field experienced dramatic growth, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic, with research themes shifting from basic detection of antibiotic resistance genes in activated sludge toward broader One Health and public health surveillance frameworks. Despite high output from certain countries, analysis revealed that integration between environmental monitoring and public health literature remains limited, indicating that translating metagenomic surveillance data into actionable health risk assessments is still nascent. The authors conclude by identifying key priorities for the field, including standardizing analytical methods, incorporating artificial intelligence for resistome analysis, broadening participation from underrepresented regions, and operationalizing One Health surveillance approaches.
items.citation: Zheng Y, Ma N, Zhao B et al.. Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.
items.summary: The study investigated whether a quantitative PCR assay originally developed for clinical *Candida auris* colonization screening could be adapted for detecting this multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen in wastewater. Given that *C. auris* skin colonization and shedding contribute to its environmental persistence and transmission in healthcare settings, the researchers validated the qPCR workflow using a wastewater matrix to assess its performance characteristics. The assay demonstrated high amplification efficiency, strong reproducibility, and a low limit of detection, indicating it can sensitively and reliably identify *C. auris* in wastewater samples. The authors conclude that this approach offers a cost-effective alternative or complement to direct patient screening, enabling broader surveillance of *C. auris* prevalence across entire healthcare systems, including facilities where routine clinical screening is not yet in place.
items.citation: Rodríguez Stewart RM, Litvintseva AP, Chavez J et al.. Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the use of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for detecting gastrointestinal and respiratory pathogens in Africa, with particular attention to the context of Rwanda as a rapidly urbanizing, low- and middle-income country with limited traditional surveillance capacity. The authors conducted a narrative systematic review by searching multiple databases for peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and surveillance studies published over more than two decades, ultimately including a substantial subset of records after screening for pathogen-specific wastewater data and public health relevance. The review found that WBE offers a non-invasive and cost-effective means of capturing both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections at the community level, providing real-time epidemiological intelligence that clinical surveillance systems frequently miss due to underreporting. Key challenges identified include variability in wastewater sampling methods, environmental factors that promote viral decay, and inconsistencies in laboratory workflows across settings. The authors conclude that integrating WBE into existing public health surveillance systems, particularly in resource-limited settings like Rwanda, could substantially strengthen epidemic preparedness, guide resource allocation, and improve outbreak response, provided that investment in laboratory infrastructure, standardized protocols, and multisectoral collaboration is sustained.
items.citation: Bambara S, Isingizwe MC, Adegboyega TT et al.. A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the role of wastewater surveillance as an early warning tool for infectious disease outbreaks, with a focus on its integration within a One Health framework that links human, animal, and environmental health. The authors systematically searched multiple major databases, screened the retrieved studies through a structured review process, and synthesized findings from studies that met their inclusion criteria. The evidence showed a positive association between pathogen detection in wastewater and clinical case counts in communities, with respiratory and gastrointestinal pathogens being most commonly identified and demonstrating season-specific surges in circulation. Sampling frequency and duration in socially vulnerable areas were particularly valuable for providing early outbreak warnings. The review concluded that while wastewater surveillance holds strong promise as a complementary public health tool, standardization of methods remains lacking and explicit application of One Health frameworks is rare, pointing to a need for more integrated surveillance systems across human, animal, and environmental domains.
items.citation: Panigrahi S, Pattnaik M, Pradhan R et al.. Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament
items.summary: This study examined whether multi-pathogen wastewater-based surveillance could serve as a practical public health tool during a major mass gathering in a low- and middle-income country. During a football tournament held in Uganda, researchers deployed Moore swabs across dozens of manholes at a national stadium on multiple match days, concentrating pathogens from collected wastewater samples and analyzing them for a broad range of enteric, respiratory, and other pathogens using quantitative PCR. The vast majority of samples tested positive for at least one pathogen, with enteric pathogens such as Shigella, Rotavirus A, and Enterovirus detected most frequently, while mpox virus was also identified at a notable proportion of sites, and respiratory pathogens including SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza B appeared at lower rates. Pathogen diversity fluctuated across sampling days, with multiple pathogens co-detected in most positive samples, and surveillance findings directly informed real-time public health responses including sanitation improvements, hygiene promotion, environmental disinfection, and strengthened on-site clinical triage. The authors conclude that integrating multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance into mass-gathering preparedness frameworks is operationally feasible in low-resource settings and can provide actionable, population-level epidemiological intelligence to support outbreak detection and response.
items.citation: Nsawotebba A, Morunyanga I, Nakintu V et al.. Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament. 2026

items.title: Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.
items.summary: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a powerful surveillance approach that captures population-level infectious disease data beyond what traditional clinical reporting systems can detect. This review examines how WBE identifies underreported, novel, and emerging pathogens—including enteric, respiratory, and neglected agents—that are routinely missed by healthcare systems, thereby revealing the true hidden burden of infection in communities. Sequencing-based studies conducted through this approach have uncovered extensive diversity within the human virome, including numerous novel and divergent viruses, while also demonstrating that co-detection of multiple viral taxa may influence viral evolution and disease dynamics. WBE has shown the capacity to detect both known and novel pathogens before they gain clinical recognition, though challenges in quantification and biological validation remain. The review anticipates that advances in long-read sequencing, bioinformatics, and global data integration will further establish WBE as a foundational component of early-warning and One Health surveillance systems worldwide.
items.citation: Greaves JC, Rodriguez RA. Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.. Environmental monitoring and assessment. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of different SARS-CoV-2 variants circulating simultaneously. The authors developed a statistical method that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts and genetic sequencing data to infer variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies, going beyond approaches that rely on sequence proportions alone. The method also allows structured relationships between reproduction numbers to be estimated across time series, enabling the inference of fixed growth advantages for specific variants across different geographic locations. Applying this framework to data from United States states over a period spanning from early 2021 to early 2022, the authors estimated effective reproduction numbers for multiple variants of concern and interest and identified consistent growth advantages of particular variants across locations. The work demonstrates that combining case and sequencing data provides richer epidemiological insight into variant dynamics than sequencing data alone.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race
items.summary: This review paper examined the co-evolutionary arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages, focusing on the diverse defense mechanisms bacteria have developed to resist phage infection and the counter-adaptations phages employ in response. The authors systematically surveyed bacterial defenses operating at multiple stages of the phage infection cycle, including surface-level strategies such as receptor modification, capsule production, and biofilm formation, as well as intracellular mechanisms like restriction-modification systems, abortive infection, and CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity. Phages were found to counter these defenses through means such as anti-CRISPR proteins, receptor mimicry, and enzymatic degradation of capsules and biofilms. The review concludes that these dynamic interactions shape broader microbial ecosystems and have practical implications for developing novel antimicrobial strategies, including engineered phages and combination therapies. The authors argue that a deeper understanding of bacterial-phage dynamics is essential for advancing phage therapy as a viable tool against multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.citation: Rafwana Ibrahim, Jesil Mathew Aranjani. Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance with a focus on the bacterial pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms driving resistance in these pathogens, encompassing reduced membrane permeability, efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic drug inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic therapies and traditional drug discovery pipelines have proven insufficient, and assesses a range of emerging therapeutic strategies including artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds, while addressing their translational and regulatory challenges. The authors also emphasize the importance of antimicrobial stewardship, global surveillance, and a One Health framework that integrates human, animal, and environmental health sectors to slow resistance emergence. The overall conclusion is that combating priority-resistant pathogens will require coordinated, multidisciplinary approaches spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical practice, and public health policy.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture
items.summary: This review examines the problem of pesticide persistence in agricultural environments and evaluates microbial strategies for their degradation as sustainable alternatives to conventional physical and chemical remediation. The paper synthesizes current understanding of how pesticides affect crop physiology and metabolism, and surveys the diversity of microorganism-mediated breakdown pathways, with particular emphasis on enzymatic mechanisms and the metabolic versatility of microbes that exploit pesticides as carbon, sulphur, and electron sources. A central focus is placed on microbial consortia, which leverage functional diversity and synergistic interactions to achieve enhanced degradation efficiency, and on microbiome engineering approaches that enable targeted manipulation of microbial communities for improved specificity and performance. The review also covers genetic modification strategies, including protoplast fusion and rhizosphere engineering with plant growth–promoting microorganisms, which have shown potential to simultaneously accelerate pesticide breakdown and improve crop productivity. The authors conclude that integrative, consortia-based, and engineered microbial systems represent a viable and sustainable pathway toward resilient agroecosystems, and they highlight emerging technologies, environmental and economic benefits, and recent patentable innovations in this field.
items.citation: S. Sangeeta Srivastava Srivastava, Rakeeb Ahmad Mir, Sofi Javed Hussain et al.. Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update
items.summary: This study evaluated the effectiveness of national antimicrobial resistance (AMR) action plans across all United Nations member states over a multi-year period, using a newly developed One Health governance index constructed through expert consultation and integrating hundreds of policy documents alongside multinational survey and surveillance data. The researchers applied difference-in-differences and joinpoint regression methods to assess how governance quality relates to antimicrobial use, AMR prevalence, and AMR-related mortality. Overall governance scores improved meaningfully across the study period, but implementation and monitoring consistently trailed behind policy design, particularly in animal and environmental sectors. A notable finding was that measurable reductions in AMR prevalence did not emerge until approximately five years after countries adopted national action plans, highlighting a substantial delay between policy adoption and observable impact. Multisector engagement and antimicrobial use surveillance were identified as the factors most strongly associated with improved AMR outcomes, leading the authors to call for sustained financing and stronger environmental and agricultural integration as the next Global Action Plan is developed.
items.citation: Weiye Chen, Yige Zeng, Jinxin Zheng et al.. Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the IceCube neutrino detector can be used to search for dark matter particles that have been accelerated to relativistic speeds by proton jets from blazars. The researchers modeled a fermionic dark matter scenario with a massive vector mediator coupling to quarks, computing the diffuse dark matter flux from a large sample of blazars whose proton spectra were inferred from multiwavelength observations, while accounting for dark matter spike profiles around supermassive black holes and Earth attenuation effects. The dark matter–nucleon scattering cross section was calculated by including elastic, resonant single pion production, and deep inelastic scattering contributions to smoothly bridge different interaction regimes. Using IceCube data, the authors derived constraints on the model's parameter space and found that this blazar-boosting strategy can exceed the sensitivity of conventional direct-detection experiments for dark matter masses below approximately one GeV. The signal is found to be dominated by deep inelastic scattering, making it most sensitive to heavier mediators, while resonant processes reduce event rates by up to roughly nine percent near the detection threshold.
items.citation: Alberto M. Gago, Jaime Hoefken Zink, Joel Jones-Pérez et al.. Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters
items.summary: This paper investigates young massive stellar clusters as potential Galactic sources capable of accelerating cosmic rays to petaelectronvolt energies, focusing on how diffusion physics shapes the very high energy gamma-ray emission observed around such systems. The authors developed a theoretical framework showing that mirror diffusion combined with pitch-angle scattering in turbulent magnetic fields naturally produces an energy-dependent diffusion coefficient scaling as the cube root of energy, then coupled three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a young massive stellar cluster with Monte Carlo cosmic ray propagation calculations to model the multi-wavelength environment realistically. Using the stellar cluster W43 as a benchmark, they tested two cosmic ray injection geometries—a central point source and a spherical shell at the collective wind shock—and compared predicted gamma-ray spectra against observations from Fermi and LHAASO. They found that the suppressed mirror-plus-scattering diffusion regime, combined with a standard injection spectrum, successfully reproduces the observed gamma-ray data, whereas stronger energy-dependent diffusion requires an unusually hard injection spectrum to match observations. A key conclusion is that the observed gamma-ray emission is governed primarily by the diffusive propagation regime rather than by where exactly within the cluster the cosmic rays are injected.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
items.citation: Lucas Barreto-Mota, Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino, Gaetano Di Marco et al.. Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots
items.summary: This paper investigated the properties of Lyman-alpha emission in little red dots, a population of compact high-redshift objects detected by JWST, using spectroscopic observations spanning redshifts from three to nine. The researchers assembled a sample of little red dots observed with both ground-based VLT/MUSE and space-based JWST/NIRSpec instruments, detecting Lyman-alpha emission in roughly half of the objects examined. The study found that broad Lyman-alpha emission, indicative of powerful outflows or active galactic nucleus activity, is present in only two sources, while the majority of Lyman-alpha emitters among little red dots show narrow line widths comparable to those of typical high-redshift star-forming galaxies. Although the fraction of broad Lyman-alpha emitters is elevated compared to ordinary star-forming galaxies, stacking analyses of the larger sample reveal no ubiquitous broad component once the two individually detected cases are excluded. The authors conclude that broad Lyman-alpha emission characterizes only a rare subset of little red dots, possibly representing a distinct evolutionary phase tied to unusually strong outflows or other exceptional physical conditions.
items.citation: Yuta Kageura, Masami Ouchi, Hiroto Yanagisawa et al.. ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting software vulnerabilities through static analysis, arguing that traditional rule-based approaches rely too heavily on syntactic patterns while ignoring the semantic meaning embedded in code. The authors propose SETYPE, a semantics-aware type system that derives type information directly from the natural language meanings of symbols and expressions in source code, using large language models to perform both type inference and type checking. A failed type check in this framework signals a potential vulnerability, eliminating the need for security experts to manually encode insecure coding patterns. The approach was prototyped for Python web applications and evaluated on real-world software, achieving high detection precision and accuracy. The system also discovered numerous previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities, a substantial fraction of which were subsequently confirmed by developers.
items.citation: Ruizhe Wang, Meng Xu, N. Asokan. Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
items.summary: Marionette is a world model for interactive games featuring articulated characters that addresses the problem of error accumulation in long-horizon video generation by explicitly separating world state prediction, geometric rendering, and appearance synthesis. Rather than autoregressing directly in pixel or latent space, the system first predicts an interpretable high-dimensional three-dimensional world state encoding multi-entity articulated skeletons and trajectories, then converts this state into structured pose-control videos using a fixed zero-parameter renderer that computes geometry and occlusion analytically, and finally synthesizes photorealistic observations using a video diffusion model conditioned on these structured controls. This decomposition makes the world state directly controllable, as demonstrated by experiments showing that injecting mismatched action streams measurably alters joint error. Critically, long-horizon failures such as character drift and ground penetration can be corrected by applying simple geometric rules directly to the explicit state without modifying the appearance model, substantially reducing ground penetration and maintaining plausible character proximity. The approach achieves video fidelity comparable to generation conditioned on recorded pose, confirming that routing appearance through the predicted state incurs no detectable quality cost.
items.citation: Zian Meng, Zhen Li, Chuanhao Li et al.. Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX
items.summary: This study characterizes the physical properties of NGC 2437, one of the most extended star clusters within the near-infrared footprint of the VVV Extended Survey, using a combination of optical data from Gaia DR3 and near-infrared data from the VVVX survey. Proper motions from Gaia were used to identify cluster members, enabling the construction of optical and near-infrared color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, including the deepest near-infrared color-magnitude diagram yet produced for this cluster. The analysis yielded well-constrained physical parameters including distance, reddening, extinction, structural properties, and a mean cluster age estimated using solar-metallicity isochrones, along with a binary fraction measurement. The improved depth achieved through VVVX deep stack imaging substantially increased the number of detected point sources compared to shallower observations, demonstrating the value of this approach for studying stellar populations in the southern Galactic plane. The revised cluster parameters were also used to reassess the relationship of NGC 2437 to several nearby objects, including an adjacent open cluster, a planetary nebula, and an evolved stellar source in the same field.
items.citation: Tali Palma, Matías Gómez, Dante Minniti et al.. The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future prospects of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for neglected infectious diseases, with particular attention to antimicrobial resistance. The authors survey a range of emerging technologies, including isothermal nucleic acid amplification, rapid polymerase chain reaction, CRISPR-based detection, nanomaterial biosensors, and microfluidic platforms capable of delivering near-laboratory accuracy within clinically relevant timeframes without dependence on centralized infrastructure. The integration of artificial intelligence and cloud-based digital health systems is highlighted as a means of automating result interpretation and enabling real-time resistance surveillance and antimicrobial stewardship. Next-generation platforms are shown to offer mechanistic insights into drug resistance in diseases such as tuberculosis, malaria, and bacterial infections, though barriers including clinical validation, cost, scalability, and equitable access remain significant. The authors argue that the convergence of molecular diagnostics, nanotechnology, and AI-driven analytics creates transformative opportunities for precision therapy, resistance monitoring, and infectious disease preparedness in low-resource settings.
items.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
items.citation: Qi Zhang, Xiajun Zhang, Jie Yang et al.. Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infections in freshwater snail intermediate hosts, which is a critical component of schistosomiasis surveillance and control. The researchers developed a loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimizing it for a simple, rapid reaction at a fixed temperature. The assay's performance was evaluated against conventional parasitological methods, standard PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two endemic African countries. The new assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity in laboratory conditions, and in field settings it detected more infected snails than conventional PCR, while microscopy failed to detect any positive cases at all. The authors conclude that this assay represents a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early warning of shifts in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addressed the problem of subjective and error-prone visual interpretation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification results, which can lead to false positives and negatives in molecular diagnostics. The researchers developed a machine-learning pipeline using the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm to automatically locate reaction tubes in digital images and classify them as positive or negative for DNA amplification. The model was trained and evaluated on a test set, achieving high overall accuracy along with strong precision and recall metrics for both positive and negative classifications. The findings demonstrate that this automated approach is suitable for real-time LAMP diagnostics, offering rapid, objective, and reliable result interpretation with minimal operational complexity.
items.citation: Mezgebo B, Chaffee R, Castellanos LR et al.. You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated nucleic acid amplification across a wide temperature range as an alternative to conventional methods that require precise thermal control. The researchers developed a LAMP-based amplification approach using a Bst polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability, enabling DNA synthesis across a temperature spectrum from below typical LAMP conditions up to temperatures approaching those used in PCR. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at both high and low starting temperatures and sustained under dynamically changing temperature profiles, rather than requiring a fixed isothermal condition. The system was validated for detection of SARS-CoV-2 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic targets, confirming its diagnostic applicability. The authors propose this broad-temperature amplification platform as a promising solution for point-of-care and field diagnostics where maintaining strict thermal regulation is impractical.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a novel protein detection method called DISCO-LAMP, which combines proximity ligation assay technology with loop-mediated isothermal amplification to enable wash-free antigen detection without the need for temperature cycling equipment. The central challenge addressed was achieving strong amplification of ligated full-length DNA products while suppressing background amplification from unligated individual DNA fragments, which was overcome through extensive template and primer design optimization. The optimized assay achieved a detection limit in the femtomolar range for target DNA, and when paired with specific affinity reagents, successfully detected Shiga toxin 2 as well as both Wuhan-1 and Omicron variants of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein using a newly engineered binding protein targeting a conserved epitope. The authors conclude that DISCO-LAMP is a versatile, isothermal platform that can be adapted to detect a wide range of protein targets through the proximity ligation framework.
items.citation: Thomas BM, Simeon RA, Yan KL et al.. DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.. Sensors & diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.
items.summary: This review examines isothermal amplification technologies as diagnostic tools for detecting pathogens in both livestock and companion animals. The authors synthesize recent advances in these methods, which amplify nucleic acids at a constant temperature and therefore do not require the thermocycling equipment central to conventional PCR-based approaches. The review covers innovations in assay design, improvements in analytical performance, and the integration of these techniques into portable platforms suited for field and resource-limited settings. The authors highlight how isothermal methods offer rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly alternatives that overcome the infrastructure, equipment, and personnel barriers associated with traditional molecular and conventional diagnostics. The review also addresses remaining challenges and outlines future directions for deploying these technologies in routine veterinary diagnostics and broader animal disease surveillance programs.
items.citation: Tooryan F, Enyertornye B, Choudhury FJ et al.. Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only a report identifier and repository link without any description of the study's content, methods, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future direction of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to represent serious global public health threats. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, analyzing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor platforms, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transform conventional systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically evaluates biosensor design principles, signal transduction mechanisms, and performance validation across diverse food environments, while identifying persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization. The authors propose mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics, and offer a forward-looking perspective encompassing self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panels, and blockchain-integrated validation pipelines for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control
items.summary: This review examines antimicrobial resistance as a global public health threat transmitted through the food chain, connecting animals, the environment, and humans under a One Health framework. The authors analyzed the key drivers of AMR spread across animal agriculture, aquaculture, and food processing, while evaluating detection methodologies ranging from traditional culture-based phenotypic testing to advanced molecular approaches including whole genome sequencing, metagenomics, and CRISPR-based diagnostics. Although molecular tools offer greater speed and resolution than conventional methods, the review identifies persistent challenges such as matrix interference, the viable but non-culturable bacterial state, and the disconnect between genotype and phenotype. The paper also describes integrated mitigation strategies encompassing on-farm antimicrobial stewardship, biofilm control, and consumer hygiene practices. The authors conclude that bridging technical and regulatory gaps in AMR surveillance is essential for developing effective interventions and ensuring food system safety.
items.citation: Emílio Gomes, Tomás Gonçalves Mesquita, Patrícia Serra et al.. Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes
items.summary: Neurocysticercosis, caused by the tapeworm *Taenia solium*, is the most prevalent helminthic infection of the human central nervous system and presents with highly variable clinical manifestations. The paper is a comprehensive review synthesizing current knowledge on the epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment, and control of this disease, addressing both endemic regions and industrialized countries where it is increasingly seen in immigrant populations. Over the past decade, notable advances have emerged in anti-parasitic combination therapies, strategies to mitigate treatment-associated inflammation, novel surgical approaches, and more sensitive and specific immunological and neuroimaging diagnostic tools. Despite these advances, diagnostic difficulties remain and treatment strategies can vary depending on the form of the disease, creating ongoing challenges for clinical practice. The review aims to serve as a practical reference for clinicians by clarifying the variability in disease expression and guiding optimal diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making across different epidemiological settings.
authors: for The Cysticercosis Working Group in Peru (CWGP)
items.citation: Javier A. Bustos, Christina M. Coyle, Kiran T. Thakur et al.. Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Varicella Zoster Virus Infection: Clinical Features, Molecular Pathogenesis, Treatment, and Prevention
items.summary: This review examines varicella zoster virus, a human herpesvirus that establishes lifelong latency and reactivates to cause herpes zoster, a condition whose incidence rises markedly with age and immune compromise. The authors synthesize current understanding of the virus's epidemiology, structure, and life cycle alongside the molecular mechanisms underlying latency, reactivation, neuronal injury, and immune evasion. The clinical burden of herpes zoster is described as extending well beyond skin disease to encompass postherpetic neuralgia, neurological complications, and systemic involvement. The review also surveys advances in diagnostic technologies, antiviral and anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategies, management of long-term sequelae, and preventive approaches including vaccination. The authors identify a gap between molecular insights and comprehensive clinical implementation, and propose an integrative framework intended to guide translation of fundamental discoveries into more effective prevention and treatment strategies.
items.citation: Lei Peng, Honghao Song, Tianying Li et al.. Varicella Zoster Virus Infection: Clinical Features, Molecular Pathogenesis, Treatment, and Prevention. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: This paper examines a fundamental design flaw in systems that use language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources: the common practice of concatenating all sources into a single prompt conflates two operationally distinct tasks, namely interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a decision. The authors propose separating these tasks and introduce a four-field evidence tuple as a structured interface between them. They identify a failure mode they term count-scale drift, wherein summing unnormalized weights produces a decision threshold that shifts with the number of sources consulted, and show that pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios resolves both this drift and ordering inconsistencies that arise when source reliabilities differ. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in two temporal settings, where the separation improves performance at different levels of granularity, and a combination of a small sequence encoder with a tree ensemble handling censored survival loss substantially outperforms a hand-crafted baseline on a clinical prediction metric. The authors also specify falsifiable predictions, acknowledged negative results, and confounded comparisons, framing the contribution as applicable beyond language models to any additive multi-signal decision system.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: No Reduction of Tropical Convection with Warming Expected from Theory or Models
items.summary: The paper investigates a longstanding apparent contradiction between theoretical predictions of weakening tropical convection under surface warming and the behavior seen in convection-resolving models. The authors examine two major theoretical arguments that have long been used to anticipate reduced convective mass transport as temperatures rise. They demonstrate that both arguments actually describe a redistribution of convective motions rather than an overall reduction, with weakening at certain altitudes being offset by strengthening higher up as the troposphere expands, and apparent mass flux reductions at fixed pressure levels reflecting decreasing air density rather than diminished convective activity. Convective motions and transported water are found to be highly invariant to warming when tracked along isotherms rather than fixed altitudes or pressure levels. These findings reconcile theory with model results and provide a simplified framework for understanding how tropical atmospheric circulation responds to a warming climate.
items.citation: Zachary McGraw, Blaž Gasparini. No Reduction of Tropical Convection with Warming Expected from Theory or Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of embedding constrained optimization solvers into end-to-end learning pipelines, where fixed-depth unrolling forces difficult trade-offs between solution quality, feasibility, and computational cost. The authors propose Residual-Controlled Douglas–Rachford Splitting (RCDRS), a differentiable solver layer for conic linear programs that treats the unrolled solver as a feedback-controlled dynamical system, with a causal controller adaptively tuning relaxation and objective-drive parameters while preserving the projection-splitting structure. Theoretically, they establish that each admissible block remains an averaged relaxed operator with finite-step fixed-point residual bounds, and they analyze time-varying rollouts as summable perturbations of a limiting averaged operator to recover primal-dual diagnostics. Experiments on mixed-cone benchmarks and engineering applications demonstrate that RCDRS improves solution quality, feasibility, and downstream decision performance compared to fixed unrolling approaches.
items.citation: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu. Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well self-evolving AI agents can adapt code-based designs when the underlying physics of a simulation environment changes. The benchmark comprises adaptation pairs spanning six physics domains, where each pair presents a source environment and a mutated target environment sharing the same goal and interface, requiring agents to iteratively revise a solution that worked in the source but fails in the target. Ten self-evolving methods from four paradigms were compared using diagnostic sandbox feedback within a limited attempt budget. The benchmark proves far from solved, with the best-performing method succeeding on only a fraction of pairs, and even providing agents with exact information about the physical changes does not substantially raise performance. The results indicate that simulator-grounded reflection outperforms unverified self-revision, that memory mechanisms anchor agents to early designs, and that the core bottleneck is mechanism redesign rather than parameter inference.
items.citation: Yuhao Zhan, Bingxiang He, Zecong Tang et al.. PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of autoformalization, which involves translating natural-language mathematical statements into machine-verifiable formal languages like Lean 4. The authors developed MathForm, a framework that combines retrieval-augmented generation with iterative, verification-guided refinement to overcome the limitations of approaches that rely solely on a model's parametric memory or single-pass filtering pipelines. Their system uses a retrieval planner to fetch relevant definitions and existing formalizations from the Mathlib library before generation, then revises outputs using compiler diagnostics and semantic-consistency feedback. Using this framework, they constructed a large verified dataset of Lean 4 examples spanning diverse mathematical domains, which was used to train a model through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. The resulting model achieves strong performance across multiple benchmarks, outperforming larger specialized models of greater size on both syntactic and semantic consistency metrics.
items.citation: Lushi Pu, Weiming Zhang, Xinheng Xie et al.. MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement. arXiv. 2026

items.title: APTER: Adaptive Post-Training with Expert-Grounded Rubrics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of adapting large language models to professional domains where responses must satisfy structured domain constraints, incorporate critical evidence, and demonstrate complete reasoning. The authors propose APTER, a framework that grounds post-training evaluation in expert-constructed criteria frameworks, where stable professional capabilities are instantiated into query-specific rubrics without requiring reference answers. Unlike prior approaches that generate rubrics independently per query or rely on holistic preferences, APTER links rubric verdicts back to their source criteria, enabling diagnosis of persistent capability deficiencies across samples. These diagnostic signals trigger targeted supervised fine-tuning updates within a reinforcement learning loop, allowing the framework to adaptively repair identified weaknesses. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and medical question answering demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple model generations in both domains.
items.citation: Xukai Wang, Liangqi Li, Zhiyue Xu et al.. APTER: Adaptive Post-Training with Expert-Grounded Rubrics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of cystatin C (CysC) for the early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. The researchers systematically searched electronic databases, assessed study quality using the QUADAS-2 tool, and applied a random-effects meta-analysis alongside summary receiver operating characteristic curve analysis across studies meeting their inclusion criteria. Cystatin C demonstrated good overall diagnostic performance for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, with strong values for sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve. Subgroup analyses revealed that studies using Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria showed higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with less heterogeneity, and combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further improved diagnostic accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising biomarker for early clinical identification of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, though heterogeneity among included studies warrants cautious interpretation.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the utility of pancreatic stone protein as a biomarker for detecting and risk-stratifying sepsis in paediatric patients, with particular focus on nosocomial and postoperative settings where distinguishing infectious from sterile inflammation is clinically difficult. A structured literature search across two major databases identified studies published over a recent multi-year period, with over fifty meeting inclusion criteria after screening. The review found that pancreatic stone protein levels rose significantly in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation, and were associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. Diagnostic performance was comparable to or superior to conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, with particularly strong sensitivity and specificity observed in neonatal and other high-risk populations. The authors conclude that pancreatic stone protein is a promising early diagnostic and prognostic tool for paediatric sepsis, while noting that variability across studies necessitates larger multicentre prospective trials and integration into multimarker diagnostic frameworks.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether the immature platelet fraction, a readily available marker of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity, can serve as an early diagnostic biomarker for sepsis. The authors searched major medical databases and identified studies meeting inclusion criteria, then pooled data to calculate sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and summary receiver operating characteristic curves, including a subgroup analysis restricted to adult populations. The meta-analysis found that the immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy for sepsis, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around the low-to-mid seventies percent range and moderate heterogeneity among the included studies. The authors conclude that while the immature platelet fraction may serve as a complementary biomarker in sepsis identification, the small number of eligible studies and methodological variability limit confidence in the pooled estimates. They call for further large-scale, standardized prospective studies to clarify its clinical utility.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, a condition where existing evidence had been inconsistent. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched major medical databases for controlled studies published over nearly three decades, ultimately including five studies encompassing nearly five hundred neonates. Pooled analysis demonstrated that IL-27 achieved higher sensitivity and specificity than CRP for diagnosing neonatal sepsis, with summary receiver operating characteristic curve analysis confirming that IL-27 had a notably greater area under the curve than CRP. The authors conclude that IL-27 exhibits superior diagnostic accuracy compared to CRP and may serve as a more reliable biomarker for the early and accurate identification of neonatal sepsis in clinical settings.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.
items.summary: This paper examined the landscape of diagnostic tools for neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries, where the condition remains a major driver of infant death despite limited diagnostic progress. The authors synthesized evidence across a range of current and emerging diagnostic approaches, including clinical algorithms, host-response biomarkers, haematological parameters, continuous monitoring, and artificial intelligence-based digital platforms, evaluating each against the WHO Target Product Profile for neonatal sepsis triage. They assessed not only diagnostic performance but also operational feasibility and suitability for resource-constrained and non-hospital settings. The analysis identified several promising technologies, including host-response biomarkers with greater accuracy than those currently in use and affordable tools capable of enhancing existing predictive algorithms. The authors conclude that an integrated, WHO-aligned strategy combining affordable point-of-care testing, routine clinical data, and digital decision support offers the most viable path toward earlier detection, more rational antibiotic use, and reduced neonatal mortality in these settings.
items.citation: Gleeson B, Blumel B, Ibarz Pavon AB et al.. Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.
items.summary: This study investigated whether calprotectin, a neutrophil activation marker measured in plasma, could serve as a useful diagnostic biomarker for sepsis and for identifying the source of infection in patients presenting to an emergency department. Researchers prospectively enrolled patients with suspected sepsis at a university hospital, measuring calprotectin at admission alongside established markers such as C-reactive protein. Calprotectin showed modest ability to distinguish sepsis from non-infectious systemic inflammatory response syndrome, but was not an independent predictor when combined with C-reactive protein in multivariable analysis. Notably, calprotectin demonstrated particular value in differentiating lower respiratory tract infections from both upper respiratory tract infections and urinary tract infections, and adding calprotectin to C-reactive protein significantly improved discriminatory performance for these comparisons. The authors conclude that calprotectin may enhance identification of lower respiratory tract infection source in sepsis presentations, though further research is needed to determine its role in routine clinical assessment.
items.citation: Wollmer M, Wessman T, Melander O et al.. Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse committee organized into clinical subgroups covering screening, infection, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals of care, using the GRADE methodology and an Evidence to Decision framework to formulate recommendations. The scope encompasses hospital, immediate prehospital, and immediate post-hospital settings, with explicit incorporation of antimicrobial stewardship principles including appropriate diagnostic strategies and de-escalation of therapy. Recommendations range from strong to conditional depending on the certainty of evidence and the balance of desirable versus undesirable effects, with particular attention to applicability in low- and middle-income country contexts. The guidelines aim to translate a large body of research into actionable clinical guidance to improve early identification, treatment, and outcomes for the millions of patients affected by sepsis globally each year.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it contains only background epidemiological context about sepsis and a brief statement about the importance of early identification and treatment, without describing the methods, specific recommendations, or findings of the 2026 guidelines themselves.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities
items.summary: This review paper examines the NLRP3 inflammasome, a key signaling complex of the innate immune system that detects a wide range of microbial, metabolic, and environmental danger signals. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms driving NLRP3 activation, including ion flux, mitochondrial damage, lysosomal rupture, reactive oxygen species, and post-translational modifications, as well as the negative regulatory pathways that keep inflammasome activity in check. Activation of this complex triggers recruitment of ASC and caspase-1, leading to maturation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and pyroptotic cell death, processes linked to autoinflammatory, metabolic, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and oncological diseases when dysregulated. The review also surveys emerging therapeutic strategies targeting NLRP3, encompassing direct inhibitors, allosteric modulators, biologics, and repurposed drugs, and evaluates their translational potential. The authors conclude that a better understanding of the balance between NLRP3 activation and inhibition could unlock new therapeutic avenues for a broad spectrum of inflammatory and immune-related conditions.
items.citation: Chan Zou, Shilong Jiang, Hui Li et al.. The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities. MedComm. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune cell receptors that trigger inflammatory signalling cascades and have been implicated in the chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases for human studies in which exercise was the sole intervention, ultimately including studies categorised by exercise type and duration, spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training modalities. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise showed a predominantly neutral or downregulatory effect, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs were mostly associated with unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with the majority of measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise interacts with TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and calls for further standardised research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review paper examines the biology, diagnostic utility, and therapeutic potential of exosomes, which are nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by shuttling bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis and selective cargo loading, with particular attention to the roles of ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications in generating exosomal heterogeneity. The review also covers state-of-the-art technologies and omics platforms used to characterize exosomal content, and evaluates the clinical performance of exosome-based liquid biopsies for cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases. Therapeutic applications discussed include both native and engineered exosomes for targeted drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, alongside insights from ongoing clinical trials. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation protocol variability and regulatory constraints, while highlighting emerging solutions including synthetic exosome mimetics and artificial intelligence–driven diagnostics as avenues toward exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection
items.summary: This paper examined whether large language model agents that modernize legacy Fortran scientific software preserve not just nominal computational behavior but also the code's response to faults, perturbations, and reduced numerical precision. The researchers developed a differential fault-injection validation framework that instruments a shared computational driver at multiple sites and applies identical, deterministic faults to both original and modernized code, allowing direct comparison of how each version responds. Applied to integral kernels within a quantum chemistry software package across thousands of runs, the method characterized how transient and persistent faults propagate through self-consistent-field iterations, finding that fault absorption costs follow a predictable contraction-based model and that reduced precision can induce phase-dependent parallel deadlocks and false convergence. Critically, the original and LLM-modernized kernels agreed across all paired fault-injection experiments, and a synchronization fix guided by the campaign's measurements remained compatible with the modernization. The work demonstrates that differential fault injection can reveal subtle behavioral differences that nominal testing would miss, while also providing evidence that LLM-driven code modernization can faithfully preserve fault-response characteristics of legacy scientific software.
items.citation: Evan Coleman, Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina et al.. Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive set of lecture notes on entropy in both classical and quantum settings, aimed at readers with backgrounds in both mathematics and theoretical physics. The treatment begins with classical probability theory and large deviation theory — including results from Sanov, Cramér, Gärtner-Ellis, and Varadhan — and applies these to statistical physics in both Boltzmannian and Gibbsian frameworks. Quantum entropies, including those of Umegaki and their Rényi deformations, are shown to connect to classical counterparts through their shared role in statistical hypothesis testing. The notes then develop the more technically demanding problem of defining relative entropy for states on subsystems described by von Neumann algebras, requiring modular theory and the relative entropies of Araki and Uhlmann, as well as Haagerup's noncommutative spaces for explicit computation. Finally, the course covers a quantum analogue of Kolmogorov-Sinai dynamical entropy in the setting of von Neumann algebras, with the stated motivation being relevance to black hole thermodynamics, though that application itself is not discussed.
items.citation: Klaas Landsman. The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: The paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources make a fundamental design error by conflating two distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a final decision. To address this, the authors propose a structured four-field evidence tuple that enforces a clean interface between these two stages, and they analyze a failure mode they term "count-scale drift," wherein thresholding aggregated unnormalized weights produces an operating point that shifts as the number of sources grows. They demonstrate that pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios resolves this problem through arithmetic rather than architectural changes, and show the fix generalizes beyond language models to other score-summing systems such as diagnostic panels and multi-signal detectors. The framework is instantiated on a longitudinal corpus in two temporal settings—after and before outcome resolution—where the proposed separation yields strong predictive performance on a survival task, substantially outperforming a hand-crafted baseline. The authors also explicitly delineate what components transfer across domains from those requiring re-estimation, and enumerate falsifiable predictions and known negative results to bound the framework's claims.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of identifying and tracking roles that network nodes play over time in temporal dynamic networks. The authors developed a method based on temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization that produces a consistent set of roles across all time periods along with a universal transition matrix describing the probability of moving between roles, while a regularization penalty discourages abrupt changes in role membership between consecutive time steps. The approach was evaluated on multiple real-world and synthetic datasets using both engineered and automatically generated features. Results indicate that with appropriate regularization, the method reduces role prediction errors compared to existing techniques, and analysis of the transition matrices reveals a more stable system in which individuals tend to remain in their roles rather than undergoing arbitrary transitions. The model is also reported to scale efficiently to large and sparse graphs.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
items.summary: The paper presents Twin, a system designed to play unknown grid-based games by having a frontier coding agent construct and iteratively refine an executable world model at test time, without any prior knowledge of the game's rules or goals. Rather than relying on hand-engineered models, Twin infers game transitions and objectives purely through simulation and interaction, enforcing that its world model accurately reproduces every previously observed game transition before committing to an action, and using prediction mismatches as counterexamples to repair the model. The system was evaluated on a continual learning benchmark of grid games, where it achieved very high completion rates and surpassed human action efficiency on the majority of levels it cleared. A key finding is that the system can infer the game's goal before receiving any reward signal on most levels, with automatic search as a fallback, and that constructing a usable world model proved more tractable than anticipated. The authors conclude that the primary difficulty lies not in building the world model itself but in correctly identifying the goal of the game.
items.citation: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano et al.. Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational complexity of determining whether two tournaments (complete directed graphs) are isomorphic, a problem that represents a core bottleneck in graph isomorphism research. The authors focus on tournaments of bounded VC dimension, a class for which no prior algorithmic results existed, resolving an open problem by demonstrating that isomorphism can be decided in quasi-polynomial time parameterized by the VC dimension, with automorphism groups computable in polynomial time for bounded VC dimension. To achieve this, they develop a new isomorphism-invariant decomposition method for tournaments, introduce the concept of a patched tournament to enable recursion, and design a recursive algorithm that exploits near-twin structure while balancing piece sizes against their number. In a complementary direction, they also address the class of tournaments with bounded chromatic number—which captures all 2-colorable tournaments and thus characterizes hereditary classes of unbounded VC dimension—proving that isomorphism testing for this class is likewise decidable in polynomial time. Together, these results establish that neither bounded VC dimension nor bounded chromatic number forms an obstruction to efficient isomorphism testing for tournaments.
items.citation: Simon Raßmann, Pascal Schweitzer. Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging innovations in diagnosing urinary tract infections, motivated by the clinical burden these infections impose through high recurrence, microbial diversity, biofilm formation, and rapidly spreading antimicrobial resistance. The authors survey a range of advanced molecular diagnostic technologies, including nucleic acid amplification techniques, biosensor-based platforms, microfluidic lab-on-chip systems, and omics-based approaches, positioning these as faster and more precise alternatives to traditional culture-based methods that suffer from slow turnaround times and limited resolution of resistance and virulence factors. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning models with these molecular platforms to enable rapid pathogen identification and antibiotic susceptibility profiling, thereby supporting targeted rather than empirical antibiotic therapy. The review highlights translational applications of these combined technologies for improving diagnostic accuracy, guiding antimicrobial stewardship, and enhancing surveillance of antimicrobial resistance. Challenges surrounding medical ethics, regulatory frameworks, and practical implementation are also discussed as important considerations for clinical adoption.
items.citation: Goyal S, Sharma P, Aggarwal D et al.. Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.. Molecular biology reports. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for faster and more accurate antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) in the context of growing global antimicrobial resistance, focusing on *Escherichia coli* and levofloxacin. The researchers developed a platform called AI MedLab MS, which combines dynamic MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry spectral analysis over time with a robust dynamic relative growth algorithm and machine learning, rather than relying on single-timepoint or single-colony measurements. This approach captures the evolving mass spectral profiles of bacterial populations exposed to the antibiotic, thereby accounting for intrasample heterogeneity and resistant subpopulations that static methods may miss. The platform was developed on clinical isolates and prospectively validated on an independent set, delivering susceptibility results within two hours with strong overall accuracy and notably high precision for resistant isolates. The authors conclude that dynamic trajectory modeling of bacterial populations represents a meaningful advance over conventional endpoint-based AST, offering potential clinical utility for guiding timely and targeted treatment decisions.
items.citation: Liu Y, Xie N, Hu W et al.. Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.
items.summary: This paper presents a state-of-the-science statement from two major European respiratory and infectious disease societies examining the role of rapid diagnostic tests in managing community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.
