Produced within the framework of a European Union–funded project aimed at combatting antimicrobial resistance, the work systematically reviews existing literature and current clinical practice to assess how such tests can support antibiotic stewardship. The statement evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of rapid tests for identifying causative pathogens, the utility of biomarkers and clinical decision algorithms, and how the introduction of rapid diagnostics has shifted understanding of infection aetiology. It also examines whether incorporating these tests into stewardship protocols leads to improved clinical outcomes and more appropriate antibiotic use. The overarching conclusion positions rapid diagnostic tests as potentially valuable tools for reducing unnecessary antimicrobial prescribing and curbing the emergence of multidrug resistance in respiratory infections.
items.citation: Polverino E, De Nardo P, Gentilotti E et al.. ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.. The European respiratory journal. 2026

items.title: Antibiotic resistance in <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>: mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and omics-based diagnostic solutions.
items.summary: This paper reviews antibiotic resistance in *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, a multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen responsible for severe infections in immunocompromised individuals and a major contributor to the global antimicrobial resistance crisis. The authors examined the diverse mechanisms by which this organism evades antibiotics, including efflux pump overexpression, porin modification, enzymatic inactivation, target site alterations, and phenotypic adaptations such as biofilm and persister cell formation, all of which have driven the emergence of multidrug-resistant, extensively drug-resistant, and pan-drug-resistant strains. The paper identifies critical limitations of conventional culture-based diagnostics, particularly their slowness and inability to detect heteroresistance and biofilm-associated tolerance, which delay effective treatment. In response, the authors survey omics-based approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and related fields, alongside microfluidic platforms and machine learning-driven artificial intelligence, as more rapid and precise diagnostic alternatives. The authors conclude that integrating multiple omics technologies with advanced diagnostic platforms represents a transformative strategy for comprehensive resistance profiling, though standardized protocols, clinical validation, and cost-effective implementation remain necessary to translate this potential into clinical practice.
items.citation: Rahman MS, Wakeman CA. Antibiotic resistance in <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>: mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and omics-based diagnostic solutions.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Preliminary Single-Center Evaluation of the Alifax Molecular Mouse Sepsis Panel for Rapid Detection of Bloodstream Pathogens.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Alifax Molecular Mouse sepsis panel for detecting bloodstream pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from positive blood culture broths. In a prospective single-center study, positive blood culture specimens were analyzed using the panel's cartridges targeting Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and resistance genes, with results compared against conventional microbiological methods including MALDI-TOF identification and automated susceptibility testing, as well as the FilmArray BCID2 panel. The Molecular Mouse panel demonstrated moderate-to-good agreement with routine protocols for both bacterial identification and resistance gene detection, and showed comparable performance to the FilmArray BCID2. Notably, the panel generated clinically actionable results within approximately one hour, representing a substantial reduction in turnaround time compared to the conventional workflow, which requires one to two days. The authors conclude that the panel holds potential as a rapid adjunct to routine microbiological workflows for managing bloodstream infections.
items.citation: Han JH, Kim JK, Kim JO et al.. Preliminary Single-Center Evaluation of the Alifax Molecular Mouse Sepsis Panel for Rapid Detection of Bloodstream Pathogens.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.
items.summary: This review examined emerging rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing technologies and their role in addressing the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the fundamentals of phenotypic approaches, with particular attention to growth-based methods and their clinical and operational implications. Evidence was synthesized demonstrating that these techniques can substantially reduce the time to effective therapy compared with conventional testing methods, which is especially critical in severe infections such as sepsis where treatment delays worsen outcomes. The review also addressed ongoing implementation challenges, including variability in test performance, absence of standardized protocols, and cost-benefit considerations. Overall, the authors conclude that rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing represents a meaningful advance in supporting antimicrobial stewardship and enabling more timely, evidence-based clinical decision-making.
items.citation: Glover JS, Humphries R. Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.. Clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent a comprehensive update to international recommendations for the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, incorporating evidence published through mid-2025. The guidelines were developed using GRADE methodology, encompassing screening, antimicrobial therapy, hemodynamic management, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and long-term outcomes across a total of statements that include strong recommendations, conditional recommendations, good practice statements, and acknowledgments of insufficient evidence. Notable new guidance includes conditional recommendations for prehospital sepsis screening and antibiotic administration for patients with prolonged transport times, age-stratified mean arterial pressure targets, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance settings, and active fluid removal following the acute resuscitation phase. Key changes from the 2021 guidelines include a shift away from empirical antifungal therapy for most patients, updated guidance allowing either invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring, and a preference for crystalloids alone over supplemental albumin for fluid resuscitation in most circumstances. Several recommendations were also upgraded in strength, including prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antimicrobial de-escalation, while others such as corticosteroid use and norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor were downgraded in certainty or strength based on updated evidence appraisal.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, containing only background epidemiological context about sepsis and a brief statement about the importance of early identification and treatment, with no description of the guideline methodology, specific recommendations, or findings covered in the 2026 document.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms
items.summary: This review examines the field of green synthesis, which uses biological entities such as plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and yeast as natural reducing and stabilizing agents to produce nanoparticles without toxic chemicals or harsh reaction conditions. The authors surveyed literature across multiple major scientific databases to critically assess advances in plant-mediated and microorganism-assisted nanoparticle fabrication, covering the mechanisms of particle formation, the role of biological constituents in determining particle size, morphology, and stability, and common characterization approaches. The functional applications of these biologically synthesized nanoparticles across biomedical, agricultural, catalytic, and environmental domains are evaluated, including their potential for photocatalytic degradation of pollutants. The review identifies persistent challenges surrounding reproducibility, standardization, and scalability that currently limit the translation of green nanotechnology from laboratory settings to industrial practice. Overall, the paper positions green synthesis as a viable and environmentally sustainable alternative to conventional nanoparticle production methods while outlining the research gaps that must be addressed for practical implementation.
items.citation: Shoaeb Mohammad Syed, Shivam Kulkarni, Mayur Patil et al.. A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms. Discover Green Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that support long-term comfort and integration with the body, as well as multimodal sensing approaches capable of detecting multiple analytes simultaneously. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and enabling predictive health insights is discussed alongside the device architectures that support these capabilities. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. Overall, the work synthesizes materials science, sensor engineering, and AI-assisted strategies to map the landscape and outstanding obstacles in this field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform with broad applicability across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The authors surveyed its synthesis chemistry, property modification strategies, and the structural features that enable extensive surface functionalization and configurable architectures ranging from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers applications including adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, energy storage and conversion technologies such as hydrogen production and battery systems, and advanced sensing platforms including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for biological and chemical detection. The authors highlight that graphene oxide's tunable band gap, high surface area, and adaptable surface chemistry underpin its performance across these diverse fields. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and proposes directions for addressing these limitations toward sustainable industrial implementation.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitations of existing image editing benchmarks, which are confined to simple single-image tasks and fail to differentiate performance across diverse models or capture real-world complexity. The authors propose CPI-Bench, a new benchmark comprising three subsets targeting general editing diversity (including multi-image editing), high-frequency practical user scenarios, and reasoning-intensive editing tasks. The benchmark was used to evaluate mainstream image editing models, revealing clearer performance differentiation and more reliable quantification of capability gaps across the three dimensions than prior benchmarks afford. Notably, ranking results from CPI-Bench show the highest alignment with a human-preference leaderboard, suggesting it faithfully reflects real-world user judgments and can serve as a robust proxy for practical deployment evaluation.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: The paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources conflate two distinct operations—interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations—which have fundamentally different computational requirements. The authors propose separating these operations via a structured four-field evidence tuple that fixes the interface between interpretation and aggregation. They identify a failure mode called count-scale drift, wherein thresholding summed unnormalized weights produces an operating point that shifts with the number of sources examined, and show that neither vote rules nor posterior ordering can be reconciled by a single threshold when source reliabilities vary. Pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios is proposed as an arithmetic rather than architectural fix applicable broadly to score-summing systems beyond language models, including diagnostic panels and additive multi-signal detectors. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in both retrospective and prospective settings, where a small sequence encoder combined with a tree ensemble carrying a censored survival loss substantially outperforms a hand-crafted baseline, and the authors explicitly delineate transferable components from domain-specific ones while stating falsifiable predictions and acknowledged limitations.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of embedding constrained optimization solvers into end-to-end differentiable learning systems, where fixed-depth unrolling forces difficult trade-offs between solution quality, feasibility, and computational cost. The authors propose Residual-Controlled Douglas–Rachford Splitting, a differentiable solver layer for conic linear programs that treats the unrolled solver as a feedback-controlled dynamical system, allowing a causal controller to adaptively tune relaxation and objective-drive parameters while preserving the projection-splitting structure. Theoretically, they establish that each admissible block remains an averaged relaxed operator with finite-step fixed-point residual bounds, and they analyze time-varying rollouts as summable perturbations of a limiting averaged operator to recover primal-dual diagnostics. Experiments on mixed-cone benchmarks and engineering applications demonstrate improvements in solution quality, feasibility, and downstream decision performance compared to fixed-depth unrolling approaches.
items.citation: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu. Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well self-evolving AI agents can adapt previously successful code-based designs to environments where the underlying physics have changed. The benchmark consists of source-to-target adaptation pairs spanning six physics domains, where a design that works in the source environment fails in the mutated target, and agents must iteratively revise their solutions using sandbox feedback within a limited budget. Ten self-evolving methods from four paradigms were compared, revealing that the benchmark is far from solved and that simulator-grounded reflection outperforms unverified self-revision, while memory-based approaches anchor agents to early designs and broad tree search fails to converge. Notably, even providing agents with exact information about the physical changes did not substantially raise performance, indicating that the core challenge lies in redesigning mechanisms rather than inferring altered parameters.
items.citation: Yuhao Zhan, Bingxiang He, Zecong Tang et al.. PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Survey of Large Models in Sports
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive survey examining the application of large models, particularly multimodal large language models, within the domain of sports. The authors systematically reviewed how these models are being used across diverse sports-related tasks and applications, covering different participant groups such as athletes, coaches, and fans. The survey catalogues and analyzes sports-specific datasets and benchmarks that have been developed to support this research area. The authors also critically discuss the current challenges facing the field and outline promising future research directions. The paper aims to serve as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to advance large-model-driven intelligence in sports contexts.
items.citation: Yichen Xu, Jianzhe Ma, Chuhan Wang et al.. A Survey of Large Models in Sports. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning
items.summary: This paper investigates why popular facts are more resistant to removal during large language model unlearning, attributing the difficulty to deeper memorization during pretraining due to higher training-data frequency. The authors propose AdaPop, a method that scales gradient pressure according to a fact's popularity using external proxies and local token confidence, while automating the balance between forgetting and retention through a dual-ascent controller. Tested across multiple model families and benchmarks, AdaPop substantially reduces leakage of supposedly forgotten content under both paraphrased and adversarial queries compared to competing methods. Internal representational analyses confirm that the method pushes hidden states of forgotten content further from their pre-unlearning positions while preserving the representations of retained knowledge.
items.citation: Anna Borisiuk, Andrey Savchenko, Alexander Panchenko et al.. The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect major foodborne pathogens, with particular emphasis on platforms relevant to both food safety and clinical healthcare settings. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, evaluating how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have enhanced sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, focusing on what prevents these promising agents from advancing from preclinical research into clinical use. The authors systematically identify core translational barriers, including difficulties in isolating EVs at scale, maintaining storage stability, achieving precise characterization, ensuring biosafety, and implementing robust quality control. To address these bottlenecks, the review surveys emerging technological solutions such as advanced bioreactors for large-scale production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis to handle population heterogeneity, and machine learning tools to improve standardization and clinical decision-making. The authors conclude by outlining future priorities centered on standardizing production workflows, strengthening safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the review positions itself as a roadmap intended to accelerate the clinical translation of extracellular vesicle therapies.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.
items.summary: This study developed a microfluidic platform integrating engineered zinc finger proteins to detect pathogen-specific double-stranded DNA without amplification or labeling. The researchers designed zinc finger proteins targeting the *stx2* gene of *E. coli* O157 and covalently bound them to epoxy-functionalized surfaces within a pump-free, capillary-driven microfluidic device, coupling detection to sequence-enabled reassembly of β-lactamase for colorimetric readout. The device produces a visible color shift upon target binding and enzyme reconstitution, achieving sensitive and selective detection at low picomolar concentrations with specificity confirmed against non-target sequences. The capillary-driven flow followed predictable Lucas-Washburn behavior, and the assay operated at ambient temperature with no need for DNA denaturation, hybridization, or amplification, producing an instrument-free readout in approximately ten minutes. The authors conclude that this approach provides a low-cost, practical framework for translating programmable protein-DNA recognition into point-of-care pathogen detection directly from double-stranded DNA samples.
items.citation: Bhuiyan SAM, Shumway R, Trinkle C et al.. Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.. The Analyst. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the integration of recombinase polymerase amplification, an isothermal nucleic acid amplification method that operates at mild temperatures without the complex thermal cycling required by PCR, with microfluidic and paper-based platforms for decentralized molecular diagnostics. The authors surveyed recent progress across a broad range of device architectures, including centrifugal chips, capillary-driven systems, paper-based analytical devices, electrochemical biosensors, CRISPR-coupled assays, and sample-to-answer cartridges, applied to biomedical diagnostics, food safety, environmental monitoring, and One Health biosurveillance. The review highlights how pairing these amplification chemistries with compact, low-power formats enables detection of respiratory viruses, bacterial and parasitic pathogens, antimicrobial resistance markers, agricultural diseases, and cancer-related biomarkers, among other targets. Emerging trends include the incorporation of smartphone imaging, artificial intelligence-assisted result interpretation, digital partitioning, and cloud connectivity to enhance portability, consistency, and analytical decision-making. The authors conclude that while the field is advancing rapidly, challenges related to sample preparation, multiplexing, reagent storage, quantitative reliability, scalable manufacturing, and regulatory validation must still be addressed before widespread field deployment can be realized.
items.citation: Wang HM, Lee SZ, Fu LM. Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.. Micromachines. 2026

items.title: Single-atom nanozyme-based wireless microfluidic sensing platform for noninvasive hyperuricemia diagnosis.
items.summary: The paper investigated non-invasive electrochemical detection of uric acid for diagnosing hyperuricemia, a condition linked to gout, kidney damage, and cardiovascular disease. The researchers synthesized single-atom platinum catalysts deposited on reduced graphene oxide/metal-organic framework composites via photochemical deposition, then integrated these materials into a portable wireless microfluidic electrochemical sensing platform with a hydrophilic surface-modified microfluidic device to improve biofluid collection. The resulting platform achieved a broad linear detection range and low detection limit for uric acid, with high selectivity and reproducibility. Validation studies using serum and saliva samples from hyperuricemia patients and healthy volunteers demonstrated a meaningful correlation between the two biofluids, supporting the platform's clinical utility for non-invasive point-of-care testing.
items.citation: Zhao J, Zheng J, Wei K et al.. Single-atom nanozyme-based wireless microfluidic sensing platform for noninvasive hyperuricemia diagnosis.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that support long-term comfort and integration with the body, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also assessed. Despite these advances, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. Overall, the paper synthesizes current knowledge across materials, device architectures, and AI-assisted strategies to outline the state of the field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection
items.citation: Rzgar Sirwan Raza, Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen et al.. Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by shuttling bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, with a focus on the molecular mechanisms governing their biogenesis and functional diversity. The authors synthesize current understanding of how molecular machinery — including endosomal sorting complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications — controls the selective loading of cargo into exosomes and drives their heterogeneity. The review also evaluates state-of-the-art omics platforms and machine learning tools used to characterize exosomal content for diagnostic applications, particularly in liquid biopsies for cancer, metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. On the therapeutic side, the authors assess the potential of both native and engineered exosomes for targeted drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, drawing on evidence from ongoing clinical trials. The review concludes by identifying persistent translational barriers such as isolation standardization and regulatory constraints, while proposing that emerging approaches including synthetic exosome mimetics and artificial intelligence-driven diagnostics will advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious nosocomial bloodstream infection caused by Candida species, focusing on the persistent challenges that make it difficult to manage effectively in clinical settings. The authors surveyed the epidemiology and species distribution of candidemia, then critically evaluated current diagnostic methods and their limitations, including delays inherent to conventional approaches. The review covers therapeutic strategies ranging from empiric to targeted antifungal regimens, addressing mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to combination therapy as a potential countermeasure. Emerging diagnostic technologies, novel antifungal agents in development, and compounds targeting new fungal pathways are highlighted as promising advances. The review concludes by exploring future directions including artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment strategies, with the goal of supporting clinicians and researchers in improving patient outcomes.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: This paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources incorrectly conflate two distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a decision. The authors propose separating these operations and define a four-field evidence tuple as a structured interface between them, which they argue clarifies the design of both halves. They identify a failure mode they term "count-scale drift," in which thresholding a sum of unnormalized weights implicitly performs posterior thresholding at an operating point that shifts as the number of sources grows, and they show that vote rules and posterior rules order instances differently when source reliabilities vary, with no single threshold reconciling them. Pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios is proposed as an arithmetic fix applicable beyond language models to score-summing triage engines, diagnostic panels, and additive multi-signal detectors. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in two settings—post-outcome and pre-outcome—with the pre-outcome instantiation combining a small sequence encoder with a tree ensemble achieving substantially higher precision-recall performance than a hand-crafted baseline.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of embedding constrained optimization solvers into end-to-end learning pipelines, where fixed-depth unrolling forces trade-offs between solution quality, feasibility, and computational cost. The authors propose Residual-Controlled Douglas–Rachford Splitting (RCDRS), a differentiable solver layer for conic linear programs that treats the unrolled solver as a feedback-controlled dynamical system. A causal controller dynamically adapts relaxation and objective-drive parameters during the unrolling process while preserving the projection-splitting structure of Douglas–Rachford splitting. Theoretical analysis establishes that each admissible block remains an averaged relaxed operator with finite-step fixed-point residual bounds, and safeguarded time-varying rollouts are analyzed as summable perturbations of a limiting averaged operator. Experiments on mixed-cone benchmarks and engineering applications demonstrate that RCDRS improves solution quality, feasibility, and downstream decision performance compared to fixed-depth unrolling approaches.
items.citation: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu. Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: This paper introduces PACE-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate how well self-evolving AI agents can adapt code-based solutions when the underlying physical environment changes. The benchmark comprises adaptation pairs spanning six physics domains, where each pair presents a source environment and a mutated target environment sharing the same goal and interface, requiring agents to iteratively revise a previously successful design using sandbox feedback within a limited attempt budget. Ten self-evolving methods representing four paradigms were evaluated, and none came close to saturating the benchmark, with the best-performing combination achieving success on only two-thirds of a subset. Key findings indicate that simulator-grounded reflection outperforms unverified self-revision, while memory mechanisms tend to anchor agents to early designs and broad tree search fails to converge on solutions. Notably, even providing agents with the exact physical changes does not substantially raise performance, suggesting that the central bottleneck is mechanism redesign rather than parameter inference.
items.citation: Yuhao Zhan, Bingxiang He, Zecong Tang et al.. PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PriCoRec: A Privacy-Aware Cloud-Device Collaborative Framework for Ad Recommendation under Feature Constraints
items.summary: This paper addresses the tension between privacy regulations that restrict cloud access to sensitive user data and the need for effective personalized advertising recommendations. The authors propose a cloud-device collaborative framework called PriCoRec, which splits the recommendation pipeline into a cloud-based pre-ranking stage using non-sensitive features and an on-device ranking stage that incorporates sensitive personal features locally. To overcome the quality degradation inherent in naive pipeline splitting, the framework introduces a diversity regularizer for the pre-ranking stage to improve candidate quality, alongside a cloud-guided training mechanism that keeps the on-device model lightweight while boosting its performance. Experiments demonstrate that the framework successfully preserves recommendation quality while ensuring sensitive user features never leave the user's device, offering a practical path to privacy-compliant ad recommendation at scale.
items.citation: Dairui Liu, Zhongyi Lu, Jitao Lu et al.. PriCoRec: A Privacy-Aware Cloud-Device Collaborative Framework for Ad Recommendation under Feature Constraints. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Large-scale workflow placement in serverless computing using integer nonlinear programming
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of efficiently deploying large computational workflows across heterogeneous servers and edge devices in serverless edge computing environments, with the goal of minimizing both monetary costs and workflow execution times. The authors developed a mathematical framework to model workflow and cloud node characteristics, formulating the optimal placement problem as a nonlinear integer program. To handle the scalability challenges posed by large numbers of cloud and edge nodes, as well as scenarios where knowledge of node attributes is distributed rather than centralized, they introduced a novel decomposition strategy for solving the optimization problem. A case study demonstrated that this decomposition approach scales favorably to larger infrastructures and achieves meaningful improvements in placement quality compared to a simple deployment heuristic.
items.citation: Joshua Adamek, Natalie Carl, Trever Schirmer et al.. Large-scale workflow placement in serverless computing using integer nonlinear programming. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Native multi-qubit gates on a single-junction unimon circuit
items.summary: The paper introduces a superconducting circuit architecture called the multiunimon, which encodes multiple qubits within a single Josephson junction embedded in a coplanar waveguide structure, enabling native multi-qubit gate operations. Building on the unimon qubit design, the multiunimon retains desirable properties including high anharmonicity and protection against low-frequency charge noise, while also offering partial protection against flux noise. The authors designed a three-qubit version of this device and employed a leakage-aware encoding scheme for computational states, then simulated all twelve variants of controlled-controlled-NOT gates using simple sine-squared pulses of comparable duration to single-qubit gates. The simulations achieved high mean gate fidelity, with performance primarily limited by incoherent errors from dielectric loss, and the authors suggest that further improvements in noise protection, device design, and pulse shaping could push fidelities close to fault-tolerant thresholds. The results position the multiunimon as a promising building block for highly connected superconducting quantum processors capable of efficient near-term algorithm implementation.
items.citation: Sasu Tuohino, Mikko Möttönen, Matti Silveri. Native multi-qubit gates on a single-junction unimon circuit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial with a distinctive layered architecture, as a multifunctional and sustainable platform for addressing challenges in energy, environmental remediation, and healthcare. The authors survey the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies that underpin GO's tunable characteristics, including its adjustable band gap, high surface area, structural flexibility, and adaptive surface chemistry, which together enable configurations spanning zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers a broad range of GO applications, encompassing adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, energy storage and conversion technologies such as hydrogen production and battery systems, and advanced sensing platforms including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for biological and environmental detection. The authors highlight that standalone GO demonstrates notable performance across these diverse domains without requiring composite modification, underscoring its versatile and transformative potential. The review also candidly addresses persistent challenges facing GO, including scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, while proposing possible solutions to facilitate its sustainable real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, specifically focusing on platforms applicable to both food safety monitoring and clinical healthcare settings. The authors surveyed advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, considering how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have collectively improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically evaluates biosensor design principles, signal transduction mechanisms, and performance validation while identifying persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, alongside mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular multiplexed pathogen panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infection with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia alongside a critical appraisal of diagnostic methods, highlighting how delays inherent to conventional approaches complicate timely management. The review evaluates both established and emerging diagnostic technologies, while also examining therapeutic strategies ranging from empiric to targeted antifungal regimens, including management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance. Combination therapy and drugs in clinical development targeting novel fungal pathways are discussed as potential responses to resistance. Looking forward, the authors identify artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment strategies as promising directions for improving candidemia outcomes.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.
items.summary: The paper addresses the need for accurate intracellular screening platforms for viral protease inhibitors, noting that existing methods such as fluorescent protein assays and FRET are prone to non-specific conformational interference and fail to capture true intracellular inhibitory effects. The researchers designed two modular biosensors built around engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX), in which target protease cleavage of a recognition sequence triggers reassembly of split APEX fragments, restores enzymatic activity, and produces amplified fluorescent signals. Using the coronavirus main protease as a model system, one sensor achieved an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio for enzyme activity detection, while the second sensor reliably identified potent inhibitors and avoided the false positives that plague conventional approaches. By simply swapping the protease recognition sequence, the platform could be reconfigured to detect and evaluate inhibitors of proteases from multiple coronaviruses and other viruses, including enteroviruses and herpesviruses. The authors conclude that these biosensors provide a sensitive, specific, and adaptable intracellular tool to accelerate broad-spectrum antiviral drug discovery.
items.citation: Li B, Dong B, Chen Y et al.. A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.. Virologica Sinica. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional culture methods are too slow and insufficiently sensitive for timely clinical decision-making. The researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay coupled with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, optimized to run at a fixed temperature for under an hour using a set of ten specific primers. The assay achieved femtogram-level analytical sensitivity without cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains, and when validated on sterile body fluid specimens from neonates clinically suspected of *E. coli* infection, it showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR while identifying far more positive cases than conventional culture. The entire workflow from nucleic acid extraction to visual readout was completed within approximately one hour, requiring minimal equipment. The authors conclude that this method offers a rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective approach well suited to point-of-care and resource-limited settings for early diagnosis of neonatal *E. coli* sepsis.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major cause of foodborne illness, by developing a CRISPR/Cas12a-based biosensor. The approach combined DNAzyme-catalyzed amplification with hybridization chain reaction to convert pathogen-specific targets into branched DNA nanowire structures bearing PAM sequences, which then activated Cas12a-mediated cleavage to restore a quenched fluorescent signal. This cascade strategy—linking target recognition, enzymatic signal conversion, and spatial enrichment through serial hairpin amplification—achieved an exceptionally low detection limit and a broad linear range spanning several orders of magnitude in bacterial concentration. The biosensor demonstrated straightforward operation and rapid response while maintaining high sensitivity and specificity. The authors further suggest that by swapping the recognition and primer modules, the platform could be adapted for the highly sensitive detection of other foodborne pathogens.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a major foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor. The system simultaneously targets two key genetic markers of the pathogen by exploiting the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins, creating dual fluorescence channels that enable serotype-specific identification while reducing false positives. Target gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing were all integrated into a single reaction tube, eliminating complex equipment and contamination risks. The biosensor achieved high sensitivity in controlled tests and was validated using fecal samples from a mouse infection model, with results consistent with standard PCR methods. Overall, this dual-channel approach improves specificity and serotype discrimination compared to conventional CRISPR diagnostics, offering a simple and field-deployable tool for food safety, clinical diagnostics, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor platform designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The researchers constructed disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, using non-covalent π-π stacking to attach the probes without disrupting the electrode's electronic properties or surface area. A key innovation was a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduced sensor preparation time from many hours to just two minutes while maintaining detection performance. The platform achieved amplification-free and label-free detection of the colistin resistance gene and could be readily retargeted to detect a carbapenem resistance gene simply by swapping the probe sequence. The biosensors demonstrated consistent performance across independently fabricated devices, supporting their potential for scalable manufacturing and decentralized diagnostic deployment against antimicrobial resistance and pandemic threats.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.
items.summary: This review examines advances in biosensor technologies specifically designed to detect two major foodborne pathogens, *Salmonella* spp. and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which are leading causes of foodborne illness and mortality globally. Rather than broadly surveying biosensing across many pathogens, the authors take a pathogen-specific approach, systematically mapping trends in bioreceptor development and transducer selection for these two organisms. A notable focus is placed on how artificial intelligence tools can accelerate biosensor design, optimization, and decision-making for detecting these particular pathogens, which the authors describe as a novel contribution to the literature. The review also critically evaluates which biosensing strategies hold genuine promise for scalability, portability, and practical deployment within the food industry, explicitly addressing the gap between laboratory-based research and real-world implementation. The authors position the review as a practical roadmap intended to guide future research toward field-ready and industry-relevant detection solutions.
items.citation: Gumush SE, Al-Attar R, Sandbecker E et al.. Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.. Food chemistry. Molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and translational barriers of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, which have attracted interest for their biocompatibility, cargo-carrying capacity, and ability to traverse biological barriers. The authors systematically survey the core obstacles preventing most EV products from advancing beyond preclinical stages, including difficulties in isolation, storage stability, characterization, biosafety evaluation, and quality control. They then assess emerging technologies intended to address these bottlenecks, such as advanced bioreactors for scalable production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis methods to handle heterogeneity, and machine learning tools to support standardization and clinical decision-making. The review concludes by outlining future directions centered on harmonizing production practices, strengthening safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the paper aims to map a clearer pathway for translating EV-based therapies from laboratory research into clinical application.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they serve as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels but drive disease pathology when produced in excess. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the major types, cellular sources, and molecular mechanisms underlying both normal redox signaling and oxidative stress-mediated damage across a range of conditions including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders. The review also critically evaluates contemporary and emerging methods for detecting and quantifying reactive oxygen species, encompassing biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging techniques. Drawing these threads together, the authors argue for the development of precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and a deepened mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Waste to value: microbial electrochemical technologies for sustainable water, material, and energy cycles
items.summary: Microbial electrochemical technologies (METs) were examined as a sustainable alternative to conventional wastewater treatment, which currently leaves nearly half of global wastewater untreated and relies on energy- and resource-intensive processes. The review assessed how METs, including microbial fuel cells and microbial electrolysis cells, exploit electrogenic microorganisms to oxidize organic waste while simultaneously generating electricity or producing energy carriers such as hydrogen and methane, and recovering agricultural nutrients like ammonium and phosphates. Pilot-scale demonstrations have shown substantial organic matter removal and useful energy outputs, and integration with established treatment processes such as anaerobic digestion, membrane bioreactors, and constructed wetlands has advanced the technology toward higher readiness levels. Nevertheless, commercialization remains constrained by high capital costs, material limitations, and energy efficiency barriers, with scaling from laboratory to real-world deployment representing the central challenge. The authors conclude that progress in electrode design, modular configurations, deeper understanding of microbial communities, and interdisciplinary collaboration are needed to fully realize METs' potential to convert wastewater into energy, clean water, and nutrients within a circular economy framework.
items.citation: Uwe Schröder, Falk Harnisch, Elizabeth Heidrich et al.. Waste to value: microbial electrochemical technologies for sustainable water, material, and energy cycles. Frontiers in Science. 2026

items.title: Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube
items.summary: This paper investigates the ability of the IceCube neutrino detector to probe dark matter through a novel mechanism in which dark matter particles are accelerated to relativistic energies by proton beams in blazars. The researchers modeled a fermionic dark matter scenario with a massive vector mediator coupling to quarks, computing the diffuse dark matter flux from a large sample of blazars whose proton spectra were inferred from multiwavelength observations, while incorporating dark matter spike profiles around central supermassive black holes and accounting for Earth attenuation. The dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section was calculated across elastic, resonant single pion production, and deep inelastic scattering regimes to ensure smooth coverage of the transition between low- and high-energy interactions. Using existing IceCube data, the study derives constraints on the model's parameter space and finds that this approach can surpass conventional direct-detection experiments for dark matter masses below approximately one GeV. The signal is found to be dominated by deep inelastic scattering, making it more sensitive to heavier mediators, while resonance processes moderately reduce the predicted event rate near the detection threshold.
items.citation: Alberto M. Gago, Jaime Hoefken Zink, Joel Jones-Pérez et al.. Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters
items.summary: This paper investigates how cosmic rays are accelerated and transported within young massive stellar clusters, with the goal of understanding extended very high energy gamma-ray emission detected around such sources. The authors developed a theoretical framework showing that mirror diffusion combined with pitch-angle scattering in turbulent magnetic fields produces an energy-dependent diffusion coefficient scaling as the cube root of energy, representing anomalously slow transport. They coupled three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a young massive stellar cluster with Monte Carlo cosmic-ray propagation calculations, using the cluster W43 as a benchmark case and testing both centrally injected and shell-injected cosmic-ray geometries. Their results demonstrate that this slow diffusion regime, paired with a standard cosmic-ray injection spectrum, successfully reproduces the gamma-ray spectra observed by Fermi and LHAASO, whereas conventional stronger energy-dependent diffusion requires an unusually hard injection spectrum to match observations. A key conclusion is that the observed gamma-ray emission is governed primarily by the diffusive propagation regime rather than the specific location where cosmic rays are injected, with the balance between leptonic and hadronic emission also depending sensitively on how diffusion is treated.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
items.citation: Lucas Barreto-Mota, Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino, Gaetano Di Marco et al.. Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots
items.summary: This paper presents a demographic study of Lyman-alpha emission profiles in "little red dots," a class of compact high-redshift objects detected by JWST, using both ground-based and space-based spectroscopy spanning redshifts from approximately three to nine. The researchers assembled a sample of LRDs observed with VLT/MUSE and JWST/NIRSpec from multiple survey programs, identifying Lyman-alpha emission in a subset of objects and characterizing whether that emission was broad or narrow. They found that the vast majority of Lyman-alpha–emitting LRDs display narrow line profiles comparable to those of ordinary high-redshift star-forming galaxies, with only two objects showing the broad Lyman-alpha emission previously associated with this population. While LRDs show a somewhat elevated fraction of broad Lyman-alpha emitters compared to star-forming galaxies, stacking analyses of the larger sample reveal no significant broad component beyond those two individual detections. The authors conclude that broad Lyman-alpha emission is not a ubiquitous property of LRDs but rather characterizes a rare subset that may represent a particular evolutionary phase, possibly linked to unusually strong outflows or other distinctive physical conditions.
items.citation: Yuta Kageura, Masami Ouchi, Hiroto Yanagisawa et al.. ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitation of traditional static analysis tools for vulnerability detection, which rely on syntactic pattern matching and miss deeper semantic information encoded in variable and function names. The authors propose SETYPE, a semantics-aware type system that derives type information directly from the natural language meanings of symbols and expressions in source code, using large language models to perform both type inference and type checking. A failed type check in this framework signals a potential vulnerability. They implemented a prototype called PYSETYPE targeting Python web applications and evaluated it on real-world software, achieving strong detection precision and accuracy. The system successfully identified previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities, a substantial portion of which were confirmed by developers, demonstrating the practical viability of LLM-augmented semantic reasoning for security analysis.
items.citation: Ruizhe Wang, Meng Xu, N. Asokan. Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
items.summary: Marionette is a world model for interactive games featuring articulated characters that addresses the fragility of long-horizon generation in existing approaches, which implicitly encode geometric structure within learned latent or pixel sequences. Rather than autoregressing visual observations directly, the system decomposes generation into three explicit stages: a dynamics model predicts a high-dimensional interpretable 3D world state encoding multi-entity skeletal poses, trajectories, and rotations; a parameter-free graphics renderer converts this state into structured pose-control videos with geometrically correct occlusion; and a video diffusion model then synthesizes photorealistic RGB frames conditioned on these controls. This explicit factorization makes the world state directly interpretable and controllable, as demonstrated by the finding that injecting mismatched action streams measurably shifts joint error. Long-horizon failures such as character drift and ground penetration, which emerge freely in the predicted state, can be corrected by imposing simple geometric rules on that state alone without retraining the appearance model. The approach achieves visual fidelity comparable to generation conditioned on recorded pose, suggesting that routing appearance synthesis through an explicit geometric representation incurs no detectable perceptual cost.
items.citation: Zian Meng, Zhen Li, Chuanhao Li et al.. Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX
items.summary: This study characterized the physical properties of the large open cluster NGC 2437 by combining optical data from Gaia DR3 with near-infrared photometry from the VVV Extended Survey (VVVX). The researchers used Gaia proper motions to identify cluster members and constructed both optical and near-infrared color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, including the deepest near-infrared color-magnitude diagram yet produced for this cluster using newly built VVVX deep stack images. By fitting isochrones and analyzing the resulting diagrams, they determined key parameters including the cluster's distance, reddening, age, core radius, total luminosity, and binary fraction. The deep VVVX stacks substantially increased photometric depth in the near-infrared, nearly doubling the number of detected point sources compared to shallower surveys. The revised cluster parameters were also used to reassess the properties of several nearby objects, including a neighboring open cluster, a planetary nebula, and an evolved stellar source projected near the cluster field.
items.citation: Tali Palma, Matías Gómez, Dante Minniti et al.. The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.
items.summary: This study examined the real-world use of syndromic multiplex-PCR panels for diagnosing acute infections across four clinical syndromes at a southern Italian hospital over nearly two years. Researchers retrospectively analyzed thousands of panels covering central nervous system, upper and lower respiratory, and gastrointestinal infections, removing duplicate determinations to ensure each record represented a unique diagnostic episode. They found that nearly three in five determinations returned entirely negative results, though appropriateness varied markedly by panel type, with meningitis/encephalitis and gastrointestinal panels yielding far higher negativity rates than respiratory panels. Key pathogen findings included viral predominance in central nervous system infections, rhinovirus/enterovirus dominance in respiratory specimens, clustering of antimicrobial resistance markers in Enterobacterales co-infections, and diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes leading gastrointestinal detections. Based on these patterns, the authors advocate for stricter pre-test gating criteria, tiered diagnostic algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A specimens to reduce wasteful testing and close surveillance gaps for novel zoonotic influenza strains.
items.citation: Chirizzi D, Spedicato A, Bianco G et al.. Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in children in Guangzhou, a subtropical region of southern China. Researchers retrospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swab samples from children under sixteen years old who presented with fever or respiratory symptoms, using a consistent multiplex PCR panel to compare a pre-lifting period with a season-matched post-lifting period. Following the removal of restrictions, detection rates of Influenza A, respiratory syncytial virus, and human rhinovirus increased markedly in the season-matched comparison, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined substantially. The post-lifting cohort also included a higher proportion of infants and greater frequencies of fever, wheezing, and lower respiratory tract diagnoses, though the authors caution that changes in health-care-seeking behavior and admission thresholds may confound these clinical comparisons. The findings support ongoing multiplex surveillance and age-targeted prevention strategies, while emphasizing that causal attribution to restriction lifting alone is limited by residual confounding from seasonality, concurrent SARS-CoV-2 circulation, and shifting healthcare utilization patterns.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how rapid diagnostic testing for pediatric respiratory infections can be optimized to deliver genuine clinical and economic value across different care settings. The authors address the diagnostic challenge posed by overlapping presentations of viral, bacterial, and atypical pathogens in children, and the consequent tendency toward empirical antimicrobial use despite a predominantly viral etiology. Rather than evaluating diagnostic technologies in isolation, they propose a scenario-driven framework in which "top pathogens" are defined contextually by age group, syndrome, season, care setting, and factors such as transmissibility, treatment implications, and antimicrobial resistance relevance. The review synthesizes evidence across clinical scenarios ranging from emergency triage through inpatient ward care, severe pneumonia, and intensive care to outbreak and hospital-acquired infection settings, and analyzes the economic mechanisms by which targeted testing may reduce unnecessary antibiotics, enable timely antiviral therapy, shorten hospital stays, and limit nosocomial transmission. The authors conclude that the value of rapid diagnostics depends not on analytical breadth but on applying the right test to the right patient within predefined decision pathways, and they propose implementation principles integrating diagnostic stewardship, antimicrobial stewardship, and local epidemiological context.
items.citation: Chen J, Wang H, Li Y et al.. Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adult patients admitted to a regional hospital in Chiang Mai with SARI symptoms between late 2023 and early 2024, using multiplex real-time PCR to screen for a broad panel of respiratory pathogens. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus emerging as the most frequently detected viruses, and a small proportion of cases involving co-infections. Seasonal patterns were observed, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated throughout the study period. The findings highlight that viral pathogens account for a substantial proportion of post-pandemic SARI cases and underscore the need for expanded rapid molecular diagnostics to reduce reliance on empiric antibiotic treatment.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex quantitative real-time PCR platform capable of simultaneously detecting ten viral and bacterial pathogens associated with bovine respiratory disease in dairy cattle from southern Brazil, filling a gap where only single-plex molecular assays had previously been used. The researchers designed the system to target a broad panel of pathogens including coronaviruses, herpesviruses, and several bacterial agents, then evaluated its analytical performance through standard curve analysis, repeatability, and reproducibility testing before applying it to field-collected nasal swab samples. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and robust performance across single, duplex, triplex, and fourplex configurations, with no significant differences detected between formats. Field testing revealed that a substantial majority of sampled cattle were positive for at least one pathogen, with bacterial agents predominating and co-infections of varying complexity identified across animals of different ages and clinical statuses. Pathogen occurrence was significantly associated with animal age, season, and farm-level factors, and the platform is presented as the first validated multiplex qPCR tool for bovine respiratory disease diagnostics in Brazil.
items.citation: Rodriguez MC, Silva IV, Perotta JH et al.. Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper addresses the bioinformatics bottleneck in real-time pathogen detection by developing a visualization tool for multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels. The authors adapted the existing RAMPART software to support multiplex PCR syndromic panels combined with Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing, enabling dynamic visual tracking of sequencing runs and amplicon coverage. The tool processes raw sequencing data through to taxonomic assignment within minutes, providing an accessible and user-friendly interface suitable for field or clinical diagnostic workflows. Validation experiments using complex clinical and environmental samples confirmed that the system reliably and accurately identified all pathogens present. The tool is presented as an integrated solution for rapid syndromic surveillance and genomic pathogen monitoring in the context of emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.
items.citation: Lechat P, Kwasiborski A, Vincent R et al.. VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England). 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: The paper reviews the genus *Enterococcus*, which comprises commensal bacteria found in the gastrointestinal tracts of humans and animals as well as in food and environmental sources, and which are increasingly used as probiotics, antibiotic alternatives, and protective cultures. The authors examined the beneficial roles these bacteria play, including pathogen control, microbiome modulation, food fermentation enhancement, and production of bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins with pathogen-inhibitory properties. At the same time, the review addresses serious safety concerns, particularly the association of certain enterococcal strains with healthcare-associated infections and the potential spread of antimicrobial resistance genes. The authors argue that these dual characteristics necessitate rigorous safety evaluations before enterococci can be broadly deployed in clinical or agrifood contexts. The work is presented as a comprehensive reference intended to inform future research, regulatory decision-making, and practical applications across health and food systems.
