items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America
items.summary: This study investigated the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into Antarctica, where it poses a significant threat to polar wildlife. Researchers detected the virus in carcasses of eight species across the South Shetland Islands during two consecutive austral summers, then applied whole-genome sequencing, mutational profiling, and phylogenetic reconstruction to characterize the viruses and trace their origins. The analyses revealed that the detected viruses did not derive from a single introduction event but instead descended from multiple independent incursions. One group of strains, recovered from gulls, skuas, fur seals, a tern, and an elephant seal, clustered with H5N1 strains previously identified in South American marine mammals, consistent with at least two separate introductions into Antarctica. A second group, from petrels, shags, and skuas, clustered with strains from South Georgia and a previously reported Antarctic Peninsula detection, suggesting South Georgia functions as an epidemiological stepping stone linking South America to Antarctica.
items.citation: Maria Ogrzewalska, Ralph Eric Thijl Vanstreels, Elisa Cavalcante Pereira et al.. Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses
items.citation: Rory P. Mulloy, Danyel Evseev, Noga Sharlin et al.. Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses. PLoS Biology. 2026

items.title: Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections
items.summary: This paper addresses the clinical challenge of secondary mucormycosis arising after respiratory viral infections, particularly those caused by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses. A multidisciplinary group of international experts was convened to develop a formal consensus document aimed at guiding prevention strategies for this complication. The consensus identifies high-risk populations and provides a set of preventive recommendations organized around four domains: education and training, personal protection, early diagnosis and treatment, and infection control. The document also acknowledges areas where evidence remains limited or contested and calls for future research to strengthen the evidence base. Overall, the consensus aims to systematize prevention efforts and raise awareness of mucormycosis as a serious secondary complication of respiratory viral disease.
items.citation: Junyan Qu, Xinyao Liu, Min Quan et al.. Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Efficacy of the nucleoside analog 4′-Fluorouridine against Nipah virus in the Syrian hamster model
items.citation: Olivier Escaffre, Madison L. Pearson, Terry L. Juelich et al.. Efficacy of the nucleoside analog 4′-Fluorouridine against Nipah virus in the Syrian hamster model. PLoS Pathogens. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities
items.summary: This paper reviews the current state and future prospects of point-of-care molecular diagnostics for neglected infectious diseases, with particular attention to antimicrobial resistance. The authors examined a range of emerging technologies, including isothermal nucleic acid amplification, rapid polymerase chain reaction, CRISPR-based detection, nanomaterial biosensors, and microfluidic platforms, all designed to deliver rapid, laboratory-quality results without centralized infrastructure. The review also considered how artificial intelligence and cloud-based digital health systems can support automated result interpretation, resistance surveillance, and antimicrobial stewardship. These next-generation platforms are shown to offer mechanistic insights into drug resistance in diseases such as tuberculosis, malaria, and bacterial infections, though the authors identify clinical validation, cost, scalability, and equitable access as persistent barriers. The paper concludes that the convergence of molecular diagnostics, nanotechnology, and AI analytics presents transformative opportunities for precision therapy, resistance monitoring, and infectious disease preparedness in low-resource settings.
items.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
items.citation: Qi Zhang, Xiajun Zhang, Jie Yang et al.. Point-of-care molecular diagnostics and drug-resistance mechanisms in neglected infectious diseases: current advances and future therapeutic opportunities. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Joint Estimation of Sparse Multilayer Networks via Graph Limits
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of estimating the structure of multiplex networks, where multiple types of interactions occur among the same set of individuals. The authors model such data using graph limits known as scaled graphons, which flexibly accommodate varying sparsity across network layers, and develop a nonparametric joint estimator called the multi-network histogram based on blockmodel approximations. Shared latent variables link the layers, allowing information from denser or better-observed layers to improve estimation in sparser ones. The theoretical analysis establishes an upper bound on the weighted mean integrated squared error and derives the optimal bandwidth for minimizing this error, showing that joint modeling yields a smaller optimal bandwidth and lower error than single-layer approaches. The framework is validated through simulations and applied to socioeconomic multiplex networks from an Indian village, demonstrating practical gains from joint estimation.
items.citation: Youngseok Song, Sofia C. Olhede. Joint Estimation of Sparse Multilayer Networks via Graph Limits. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: This paper argues that systems using language models to synthesize conclusions from multiple sources incorrectly conflate two distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a decision. The authors propose separating these operations and define a four-field evidence tuple as the interface between them, which they argue simultaneously constrains the design of both the interpretation and aggregation components. They identify a failure mode called count-scale drift, where thresholding aggregated evidence produces an operating point that shifts with the number of sources consulted, and show that pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios resolves this problem arithmetically rather than architecturally. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in two settings—after and before outcome resolution—where the proposed separation improves performance, with a small sequence encoder combined with a tree ensemble carrying a survival loss substantially outperforming a hand-crafted baseline on a clinical prediction task. The authors also explicitly delineate which components transfer across domains, which must be re-estimated, enumerate falsifiable predictions, and report negative results.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CytoBERT: A Foundation Model for Cytometry Data
items.summary: CytoBERT is a foundation model designed to address the challenges of analyzing highly heterogeneous and unstandardized single-cell cytometry data, which measures characteristics such as protein expression in immune cells. The model was pretrained in a self-supervised fashion on a large curated corpus of human cytometry datasets spanning heterogeneous marker panels and tens of millions of cells, using marker standardization to harmonize the data. By learning transferable inter-marker relationships at the single-cell level, CytoBERT aims to overcome the difficulty of applying machine learning across studies that differ in experimental protocols and measured features. Fine-tuning the pretrained model for sample-level classification demonstrated that transfer learning is feasible across diverse cytometry datasets. The authors release CytoBERT as a publicly available, open-source, open-weight model intended to serve as a generalizable starting point for scalable cytometry analysis.
items.citation: Syed Abdul Haseeb Qadri, Bjarne C. Hiller, Felix Blanke et al.. CytoBERT: A Foundation Model for Cytometry Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Change Point Detection and Localization in High-Dimensional Time Series
items.summary: This paper develops new statistical methodology for detecting and localizing change points in high-dimensional time series, addressing both sequential testing on incoming data streams and retrospective identification of multiple change points with confidence intervals controlling error at a global level. The test statistics are constructed using the maximum norm to maintain power against sparse and asynchronous changes, and are based on multiscale statistics that examine the data at many different resolutions simultaneously. A key theoretical contribution is the development of Hölder-Gauss-approximations, which extend classical Hölderian invariance principles to high dimensions by providing Gaussian approximations for the Hölder-norm of high-dimensional partial sum processes, a result with broader applicability beyond change point detection. The methods are validated through simulation studies examining finite-sample performance, and applied to real data on air contamination from California wildfires, where changes occur asynchronously across a network of monitoring stations.
items.citation: Patrick Bastian, Daria Tieplova, Nina Dörnemann et al.. Change Point Detection and Localization in High-Dimensional Time Series. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Reflective Metasurface for High-Efficiency Terahertz Cross-Polarization Conversion
items.summary: This paper investigated a reflective metasurface designed to convert the polarization state of terahertz radiation with high efficiency. The researchers constructed a device based on a double-ring aluminum resonator on a quartz substrate and used full-wave electromagnetic simulations to optimize the geometry and understand the underlying conversion mechanism through phase analysis, polarization ellipses, and surface-current distributions. The optimized design achieved near-unity polarization conversion ratios at two distinct terahertz resonance frequencies in simulation. Experimental validation using reflection-mode terahertz time-domain spectroscopy confirmed the simulated predictions, with measured polarization conversion ratios exceeding a high threshold at both resonance frequencies, demonstrating effective cross-polarization conversion in reflection mode.
items.citation: Muhammad Fayyaz Kashif, Shobit Agarwal, Antonio Iodice et al.. A Reflective Metasurface for High-Efficiency Terahertz Cross-Polarization Conversion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MRI-guided cardiac radiotherapy using a 1.5 T MR-linac: surveying emerging patterns of care
items.summary: This paper investigated the emerging use of MRI-guided radiotherapy delivered on a high-field MR-linac system as a noninvasive treatment approach for cardiac tumours, which are rare and otherwise managed through complex surgical resections. The authors conducted an international survey distributed to clinical users of the MR-linac platform who had treated patients with cardiac tumours, gathering detailed information on imaging protocols, treatment planning, motion management strategies, and clinical outcomes. The survey captured responses from six international institutions reporting on a small series of cardiac treatments performed over a multi-year period, revealing that prescribed doses ranged broadly and that the majority of cases were delivered in five fractions using hypofractionated regimens. Respiratory motion monitoring through cine MRI was employed in nearly all cases, and daily adaptive planning was a common feature of the workflow. The authors found that local control was achieved in nearly all reported cases without serious adverse events, supporting the feasibility of this approach and providing a foundation for developing standardized treatment recommendations and protocol harmonization across institutions.
items.citation: O. Akdag, S. Mandija, J. Pomp et al.. MRI-guided cardiac radiotherapy using a 1.5 T MR-linac: surveying emerging patterns of care. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Dual-Hue Recognizable Lateral Flow Immunoassay Corresponding to Distinct Sensitivity Ranges for Timely and Quantitative Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This paper developed a lateral flow immunoassay platform designed to simultaneously detect two prostate cancer biomarkers—total and free prostate-specific antigen—with both visual and smartphone-based readout capabilities. The system exploits dual-ratiometric fluorescence transitions driven by the inner filter effect, creating two distinct color-change pathways with different sensitivity ranges that are theoretically and experimentally characterized. This design allows the clinically ambiguous diagnostic "gray zone," where standard tests struggle to differentiate benign from malignant conditions, to be assessed semiquantitatively by the naked eye, while a smartphone app analyzing color tone provides precise risk stratification based on the ratio of the two biomarkers. Validated against clinical serum samples, the platform achieved diagnostic accuracy comparable to established chemiluminescent assays while being substantially faster and simpler to operate. The authors propose that this dual-hue ratiometric framework represents a generalizable approach for multiplexed point-of-care diagnostics of noncommunicable diseases.
items.citation: Rong Hu, Xi Zhang, Liang Huang et al.. A Dual-Hue Recognizable Lateral Flow Immunoassay Corresponding to Distinct Sensitivity Ranges for Timely and Quantitative Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer. ACS Nano. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines lateral flow immunoassay technology as a diagnostic platform for viral infectious diseases, reframing it not merely as a point-of-care tool but as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three dimensions: signal generation and transduction strategies employing diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches designed to improve sensitivity, accuracy, and throughput; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. The review also comprehensively covers applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids. Current limitations including sensitivity constraints, target specificity issues, and practical challenges related to cost, usability, and stability are critically assessed, with future directions emphasizing advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection strategies. Overall, the authors argue that lateral flow immunoassay, particularly colorimetric formats, holds transformative potential as an emergency screening tool and for routine decentralized testing in strengthening global public health infrastructure.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether polydopamine nanoparticles could serve as superior signal labels in lateral flow immunoassay platforms to overcome the sensitivity limitations of conventional gold nanoparticle-based single-mode colorimetric detection. The researchers constructed a dual-mode colorimetric and photothermal lateral flow immunoassay using polydopamine nanoparticles, exploiting their high molar extinction coefficient and broadband ultraviolet-to-near-infrared absorption, and applied it to detect two thromboembolism-related biomarkers, thrombomodulin and α₂-plasmin inhibitor-plasmin complex, in clinical serum samples. The photothermal readout mode substantially amplified detection sensitivity beyond the colorimetric mode alone, and clinical validation against established clinical methods using serum samples demonstrated good agreement. The authors conclude that this polydopamine nanoparticle-based dual-mode platform offers a practical strategy for improving the sensitivity and reliability of lateral flow immunoassays for point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Yin J, Qiu Y, Nie Y et al.. Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.. RSC advances. 2026

items.title: Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation during immobilization affects the sensitivity and consistency of lateral flow immunoassays, with random immobilization identified as a key limiting factor. The researchers developed a boronate affinity-based strategy that exploits covalent reactions between boronic acid and cis-diol groups on Fc-region glycans to achieve site-specific antibody orientation, and used molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the mechanistic basis of this approach. Simulations revealed that the boronate-antibody configuration exhibited highly favorable binding energy and rapid conformational stabilization, proceeding through sequential electrostatic guidance followed by hydrogen-bond and covalent bond formation. Experimentally, the oriented immobilization yielded near-complete antibody conjugation efficiency, high Fab exposure, and superior antigen-binding affinity compared to conventional passive adsorption. When applied to detecting the mycotoxin zearalenone in corn, the oriented lateral flow assay achieved a detection limit dramatically lower than traditional colloidal gold assays, with recovery rates and correlation to confirmatory mass spectrometry analysis demonstrating the method's accuracy and practical utility.
items.citation: Yang Z, Yan X, Yang Z et al.. Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a lateral flow microarray immunoassay for detecting antibodies against Usutu virus and West Nile virus in wild birds directly in the field, addressing the lack of on-site, multi-analyte serological tools for arbovirus surveillance. Researchers captured wild birds at ringing sites in the Netherlands and tested them using the species-independent assay, then compared results against the gold-standard focus reduction neutralization test for a subset of birds. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for Usutu virus detection and successfully identified seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird, which was independently confirmed. Performance was also evaluated against the WHO REASSURED framework for point-of-care diagnostics, where the assay achieved a strong proportion of the maximum possible score. The findings support the feasibility of this rapid, equipment-light assay for on-site arbovirus surveillance in both Dutch ringing sites and resource-limited settings, though further validation is recommended.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation on gold nanoparticles affects the performance of lateral flow immunoassays, and whether a new nanoparticle synthesis strategy could overcome the limitations of conventional approaches. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature method to produce phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles at large scale, enabling oriented antibody immobilization through boronate-affinity interactions with the carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments, rather than relying on random physical adsorption. This oriented coupling approach was designed to preserve accessibility of antigen-binding sites, directly improving diagnostic sensitivity. When tested for fecal occult blood detection, the new nanoparticles dramatically outperformed conventional citrate-capped gold nanoparticles in sensitivity, while the synthesis process was also substantially faster and more scalable than traditional high-temperature reflux methods. The authors conclude that this platform offers strong potential for clinical translation in high-sensitivity point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.
items.summary: This paper addressed the limited sensitivity of conventional lateral flow immunoassays, which stems from weak optical signals, randomly oriented antibodies, and inconsistent nanoprobe fabrication. The researchers developed a dual-enhancement approach combining gold-decorated ferritin nanocages with SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry, where engineered ferritin displaying SpyTag peptides served as a precise template for controlled gold nanocluster growth while retaining functional sites for subsequent antibody attachment. The resulting core-shell nanostructures were highly uniform, and the SpyCatcher-fused antibodies conjugated to them via spontaneous covalent isopeptide bonds in a site-specific, oriented manner that greatly improved antigen-binding capacity compared to random adsorption. Testing against human chorionic gonadotropin as a model analyte, the optimized assay achieved a limit of detection dramatically lower than commercial gold nanoparticle-based strips, while also demonstrating reliable performance in urine samples with acceptable spike-recovery rates. The authors conclude that this synergistic strategy offers a versatile platform for substantially improving the sensitivity of point-of-care diagnostic tests.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Yuan X, Zhu X, Xu Y et al.. Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, with an emphasis on clinical relevance and field deployment. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, exploring how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, which the review argues transforms conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools capable of real-time analytics, pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection. The review critically assesses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory standardization, and proposes mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examines the dual biological roles of reactive oxygen species, which act as essential signaling molecules at physiological concentrations but drive disease when produced in excess or dysregulated. The authors synthesize current knowledge on ROS types, their cellular and molecular origins, and the key pathways through which redox imbalance causes cellular damage and signaling disruption. The review also critically evaluates contemporary detection and quantification methods for oxidative stress, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches applicable to both clinical and preclinical settings. The contribution of oxidative stress to major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders is examined within this framework. The paper concludes by outlining future directions in precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved ROS detection technologies and a deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine
items.summary: Spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) are nanostructures consisting of a nanoparticle core densely coated with a radially oriented shell of oligonucleotides, and this review traces their development over three decades as a case study in how fundamental nanoscience drives translational innovation. The paper examines how advances in synthetic control over nanostructure size, shape, and composition, combined with the discovery of emergent phenomena, have produced a well-defined set of design rules for SNA construction across dozens of structural classes. A key focus is the distinctive properties that arise from the SNA architecture, including enhanced nucleic acid binding affinity, resistance to enzymatic degradation, reduced immune activation, and efficient cellular uptake without transfection agents, which together underpin their use as intracellular probes, gene regulation tools, vaccines, and CRISPR-based gene editing platforms. In parallel, SNAs function as programmable building blocks for assembling DNA-mediated colloidal crystals with tunable lattice symmetries and nanoparticle compositions, enabling metamaterials with properties such as negative refractive indices and shape memory. The authors argue that SNAs illustrate a broader paradigm in which synthetic mastery and fundamental discovery together catalyze interdisciplinary breakthroughs spanning chemistry, biology, materials science, and medicine.
items.citation: Connor M. Forsyth, Rachel R. Chan, Tanner D. Fink et al.. Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine. Accounts of Chemical Research. 2026

items.title: Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths
items.citation: Alessandro C Pasqualotto, Thuy Vi Le, Tarsila Vieceli et al.. Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths. The Lancet HIV. 2026

items.title: Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling
items.summary: This paper examines how extracellular vesicles communicate between cells, challenging the dominant paradigm that their signaling occurs primarily through cellular uptake and release of internal cargo into the cytoplasm. The authors propose two alternative surface-binding mechanisms — termed "bind-and-stay" and "bind-and-leave" — in which vesicles signal through interactions at the cell surface without being internalized. The "bind-and-leave" mode is particularly notable because it allows a single vesicle to transiently bind and activate signaling in multiple recipient cells sequentially, directly contradicting the conventional assumption that each vesicle acts on only one cell. The paper offers a forward-looking perspective on the relative efficiency and effectiveness of these different signaling modes and identifies experimental approaches that could be used to investigate them. The authors argue that a more complete understanding of extracellular vesicle signaling mechanisms is essential for both fundamental cell biology and the development of vesicle-based therapeutics.
items.citation: Wojciech Chrzanowski, Joy Wolfram. Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters
items.summary: This paper investigates young massive stellar clusters as potential sources capable of accelerating cosmic rays to extreme energies, focusing on how cosmic ray transport within these environments shapes the observed gamma-ray emission. The authors developed a theoretical framework showing that mirror diffusion combined with pitch-angle scattering in turbulent magnetic fields suppresses cosmic ray transport, producing an energy-dependent diffusion coefficient scaling as energy to the one-third power. They coupled three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a young massive stellar cluster with Monte Carlo cosmic ray propagation calculations, using the cluster W43 as a benchmark, and tested two different cosmic ray injection geometries alongside multiple diffusion regimes. Their results demonstrate that the slow mirror-plus-scattering diffusion regime, combined with a standard cosmic ray injection spectrum scaling as energy to the negative two, successfully reproduces the gamma-ray spectra observed by Fermi and LHAASO, whereas stronger energy-dependent diffusion requires an anomalously hard injection spectrum to match observations. The study concludes that the observed gamma-ray emission is governed primarily by the diffusive propagation regime rather than the specific location of cosmic ray injection within the cluster.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
items.citation: Lucas Barreto-Mota, Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino, Gaetano Di Marco et al.. Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comment on arXiv:2106.08363v3 [math.NA], E. Abreu, A. Espirito Santo, W. Lambert, and J. Perez, Convergence of a Lagrangian--Eulerian scheme by a weak asymptotic analysis for one-dimensional hyperbolic problems
items.summary: This comment targets a published numerical analysis paper that introduced space-time control volumes with lateral boundaries called "no-flow curves," claimed as a novel contribution for solving one-dimensional hyperbolic problems via a Lagrangian–Eulerian scheme. The commenting authors demonstrate, through equation-by-equation comparison, that these no-flow curves are mathematically identical to the space-time integral curves already defined in a earlier locally conservative Eulerian–Lagrangian method, and that the bounding tube structure also appeared in subsequent related work. A key technical point is emphasized: the characteristic velocity used to move control volumes matters critically, as two candidate expressions coincide only for linear fluxes, and only one of them correctly ensures vanishing lateral mass flux. The comment further documents, using a corpus of papers including works published after the commented article, a pattern of shifting terminology and incomplete attribution that obscures this priority. The discrete numerical contributions of the later works are explicitly not disputed; the concern is solely with the attribution of the continuous geometric object.
items.citation: Frederico Furtado, Felipe Pereira, Li-Ming Yeh. Comment on arXiv:2106.08363v3 [math.NA], E. Abreu, A. Espirito Santo, W. Lambert, and J. Perez, Convergence of a Lagrangian--Eulerian scheme by a weak asymptotic analysis for one-dimensional hyperbolic problems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: The paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources make a conceptual error by conflating two distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a decision. The authors propose separating these operations and define a structured four-field evidence tuple as the interface between them, which they argue determines the design of both halves. They identify a failure mode they call count-scale drift, where summing unnormalized weights creates a decision threshold that shifts with the number of sources consulted, and show that the vote rule and posterior ordering diverge when source reliabilities differ, with no threshold able to reconcile them. Pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios is proposed as an arithmetic rather than architectural fix applicable broadly to score-summing systems beyond language models, including diagnostic panels and multi-signal detectors. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in both prospective and retrospective settings, where the proposed separation achieves substantially higher predictive performance than a hand-crafted baseline, and the authors explicitly enumerate falsifiable predictions and acknowledged negative results.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Optimal Scheduling of Road Maintenance Jobs Considering Impact on Traffic Flows
items.summary: The paper examines how to efficiently schedule road maintenance at the network level while accounting for how maintenance-induced capacity reductions affect traffic flows. Because repeatedly solving equilibrium traffic assignment models within a scheduling optimization is computationally prohibitive, the authors developed data-driven surrogate models that approximate equilibrium arc flows directly from origin-destination demand data, using optimization-based solutions as ground truth for training. The approach was validated through a real-world case study using traffic data from a metropolitan area, demonstrating that the surrogate models can serve as a scalable substitute for full equilibrium computations. The work positions these surrogate models as practical building blocks for embedding traffic-impact considerations into future network-level maintenance scheduling frameworks.
items.citation: Charitha Nandepu, Lohitha Kalepu, Gabriele Ciavarella et al.. Optimal Scheduling of Road Maintenance Jobs Considering Impact on Traffic Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Fisher Metric of the Ricci Flow Heat Kernel
items.summary: This paper introduces and systematically studies a Fisher information metric associated to the conjugate heat kernel of a Ricci flow, a tensor that quantifies how the pointed heat-kernel measure varies as the base point moves at a fixed scale. The authors establish fundamental analytic properties of this metric, including monotonicity in scale and a sharp upper bound by the Riemannian metric, and they derive a matrix square identity for the Fisher defect that characterizes the gap between the two metrics. This identity yields a rigidity theorem: on closed connected Ricci flows the Fisher metric is strictly sandwiched between zero and the Riemannian metric at every positive scale, while in the complete case equality forces a Euclidean splitting. Building on this framework, the authors derive several consequences including a sharp reverse Poincaré inequality for the heat semigroup, a contraction formula for generalized divergences along conjugate heat flow, and a canonical construction of splitting maps from large eigenvalues of the Fisher endomorphism. As applications, they connect pointed Nash entropy near zero to small Fisher deficit at comparable scales and establish a codimension-one Fisher-metric criterion for invoking an existing epsilon-regularity theorem in Ricci flow.
items.citation: Bennett Chow, Robert Koirala. The Fisher Metric of the Ricci Flow Heat Kernel. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Memory Allocation for Constant-Bounded Programs
items.summary: This paper investigates memory allocation strategies specifically for constant-bounded programs — programs whose execution length is syntactically constrained regardless of input, such as verified kernel extensions, cryptographic routines, and fixed-shape machine-learning models. The authors demonstrate that this class of programs allows control flow to be modeled as a tree, enabling a polynomial-time approximation of optimal stack usage through a tree-scan allocation strategy combined with memory defragmentation. Their approach provides a theoretical guarantee that memory usage is bounded by the maximum live memory plus at most the size of the largest buffer, achieving optimality when in-place swapping is allowed. The allocator was validated in two practical settings: as a stack spiller in an Elixir-to-eBPF compiler and as a static heap allocator for bounded programs using the MLIR Structured Control-Flow dialect. Results show dramatic stack usage reductions on real workloads, with defragmentation being rarely necessary and memory consumption remaining far below that of naive allocation approaches.
authors: Márcio Costa e Fernando Magno Quintão Pereira
items.citation: Vinícius Silva, Kael Soares, Márcio Costa e Fernando Magno Quintão Pereira. Memory Allocation for Constant-Bounded Programs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This paper describes the design and enrollment progress of a prospective longitudinal mixed-methods study evaluating point-of-care nucleic acid tests (POC NATs) for HIV diagnosis and viral load monitoring in the United States. The study enrolled participants across a hospital-based clinic and a community LGBTQ+ center in Seattle, using two versions of a whole-blood POC NAT alongside standard laboratory testing, and included a randomized clinical trial arm for people with HIV to compare standard care with and without POC viral load monitoring. Participants also completed acceptability surveys and qualitative interviews, and clinic patient flow was observed to assess the operational impact of POC testing. The abstract reports enrollment figures and study procedures but does not yet present test performance, clinical, or qualitative findings, as analyses are anticipated in future publications. The paper is therefore primarily a protocol and feasibility description rather than a report of completed outcomes.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study examined whether pharmacologic measures of tenofovir adherence could predict future HIV viremia among people living with HIV in South Africa. Researchers compared three adherence metrics — a point-of-care urine tenofovir antibody-based assay, quantitative urine tenofovir measured by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and assessed their associations with current and subsequent viral load outcomes at twenty-four weeks using logistic regression. Tenofovir-diphosphate in dried blood spots was the only measure significantly associated with viremia at twenty-four weeks, with higher concentrations linked to lower odds of detectable virus, suggesting it may be useful for predicting future treatment failure. In contrast, neither the point-of-care urine assay nor quantitative urine tenofovir showed significant associations with subsequent viremia, though undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir was associated with current viremia, lower CD4 counts, and likely recent antiretroviral therapy initiation. The findings suggest that dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate measurement may offer the greatest utility for identifying patients at risk of future viremia and targeting adherence interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation
items.summary: This qualitative study examined perceptions of integrating a point-of-care triage test measuring interferon-gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10), a chemokine correlated with HIV viral load, into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique. Conducted within a clinical evaluation at two primary healthcare facilities, the researchers interviewed people living with HIV who underwent IP-10 testing across multiple rounds, as well as healthcare providers and HIV programme stakeholders, analyzing data through an inductive-deductive thematic approach. Participants broadly valued routine viral load monitoring but identified significant barriers including laboratory delays, access difficulties, and health system constraints. The IP-10 point-of-care test was widely acceptable, with same-day results perceived to reduce patient anxiety, support treatment adherence, and enable timely clinical decisions, while providers recognized its potential to prioritize patients needing confirmatory viral load testing. The authors conclude that successful integration would require attention to training, workflow adaptation, quality assurance, and clear patient communication, but that the test could contribute to more efficient, differentiated HIV care by reducing unnecessary testing among virally suppressed individuals.
items.citation: Myburgh H, Saura-Lázaro A, van den Bogaart E et al.. Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection, a central and contested question in exercise immunology. The authors present opposing arguments addressing whether high-performance athletes face greater infection risk than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity apart from confounding factors such as sleep disruption, anxiety, travel, and nutritional deficits, and whether available biomarkers and study designs are adequate to draw firm conclusions. While there is general agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise of shorter duration is beneficial for immune defense, the picture is more complex for arduous exercise practiced by elite athletes and military personnel, where high infection burdens have historically been attributed to exercise-induced immune suppression. Both sides of the debate agree that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in nature, making it difficult to isolate exercise as an independent causative factor. The article concludes that the question of whether exercise per se drives increased infection risk in athletes remains unresolved and calls for more rigorous empirical research.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines exosomes — nanoscale extracellular vesicles that carry proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids between cells — with a focus on the molecular mechanisms governing their biogenesis, cargo loading, and functional heterogeneity. The authors synthesize current understanding of the regulatory machinery involved, including ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications, and survey state-of-the-art omics platforms and machine learning tools used to characterize exosomal content. The review evaluates the diagnostic utility of exosomes as liquid biopsy biomarkers across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, as well as their therapeutic applications in targeted drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, including ongoing clinical trials. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation protocol variability, cargo heterogeneity, targeting specificity, and regulatory constraints. They conclude by proposing a forward-looking framework that integrates biological, engineering, and clinical perspectives — encompassing synthetic exosome mimetics and AI-driven diagnostics — to advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter
items.citation: Jordan S. Orange, Javier Chinen, Caroline C. Horner et al.. 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter. Annals of Allergy Asthma & Immunology. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label randomized trials examined whether nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces hospitalizations and deaths in higher-risk outpatients with COVID-19 who were predominantly vaccinated or had prior immunity, a population distinct from the unvaccinated high-risk patients in whom the drug originally demonstrated benefit. Participants aged fifty or older, or younger adults with coexisting conditions, who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 within five days of symptom onset were randomly assigned to receive either usual care plus a five-day course of nirmatrelvir–ritonavir or usual care alone. Across both trials, rates of hospitalization or death within twenty-eight days were very low and did not differ meaningfully between treatment and control groups, with neither trial demonstrating a statistically credible benefit of the antiviral. Although a substudy confirmed that the drug did reduce viral load by the end of treatment, this biological effect did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. The findings indicate that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir does not reduce hospitalization or death in vaccinated higher-risk outpatients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping the landscape of precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how multiomics approaches—spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—generate deep molecular insights into disease pathogenesis, while advanced deep learning architectures enable the deciphering of complex biological datasets to construct predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas such as oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions are examined as illustrative cases, with the authors arguing that the fusion of these technologies accelerates hypothesis generation and data-driven therapeutic innovation. The review also acknowledges persistent challenges, including the harmonization of disparate omics data, reproducibility concerns, and the need to address algorithmic biases, while presenting an optimistic vision for bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers
items.summary: This paper investigated whether moral preference elicitation—a method in which developers poll people on ethical dilemmas to train AI decision-making policies—is as neutral or objective as it is often assumed to be. The researchers examined three key choices developers make before any voting occurs: which features are included in the dilemmas, which people are invited to vote, and how the questions are worded. Across two study phases and three deployment contexts involving AI systems for kidney allocation, workplace simulation, and generative depictions of deceased individuals, they found that each of these pipeline choices meaningfully shapes the moral preferences that emerge. Morally relevant features varied across deployment contexts, ideological differences in preferences appeared for a substantial portion of features and sometimes reversed direction depending on the voter pool's composition, and question framing could shift ideological gaps by as much as a full scale point while also altering how moral foundations related to participants' judgments. The authors conclude that aggregation-based voting cannot on its own produce fair or transparent AI alignment, and that each stage of the moral elicitation pipeline requires systematic auditing and public disclosure.
items.citation: Taenyun Kim, Edyta Bogucka, Daniele Quercia. Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effect of Twisted-Yarn Architecture on Pressure and Proximity Sensing Characteristics of Textile Capacitive Sensors for Robotic Skin
items.summary: This study investigated how the twisted-yarn architecture of textile capacitive sensors affects their pressure and proximity sensing performance, with applications in wearable electronics and robotic skin. Silver-coated yarns were coated with polydimethylsiloxane and assembled into one-, two-, and four-layer twisted configurations, allowing systematic examination of how electrode overlap area and inter-fiber separation govern capacitive transduction. The researchers found that increasing the number of layers improved both mechanical properties and sensing sensitivity, with the four-layer configuration achieving the highest pressure sensitivity, low hysteresis, minimal thermal drift, and stable performance over tens of thousands of cycles. However, a trade-off was identified between sensitivity and proximity detection range, as higher-layer sensors exhibited greater pressure sensitivity but shorter proximity detection distances. Integration of a textile sensing array into a robotic arm demonstrated real-time spatial contact mapping and proximity detection, establishing yarn architecture as a controllable design parameter for tuning the characteristics of textile-based capacitive sensing systems.
items.citation: Ishtia Zahir, Eslam Saleh, Maryam Rezayati et al.. Effect of Twisted-Yarn Architecture on Pressure and Proximity Sensing Characteristics of Textile Capacitive Sensors for Robotic Skin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
items.summary: This paper addresses a performance bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts language models during small-batch decoding, a regime common in latency-sensitive applications like coding assistants and real-time audio-video systems. The authors identify that under small-batch conditions, MoE inference becomes memory-bound due to the cost of loading expert weights, and existing remedies such as weight compression or fine-grained expert design trade off accuracy or introduce additional overhead. To solve this, they propose DeaMoE, an architecture that organizes experts into departments where experts within the same department share most of their parameters while retaining a small set of private parameters to preserve individual specialization. They also introduce a customized two-stage routing strategy that avoids redundant weight loading during decoding. The resulting system substantially reduces the amount of weights loaded per decoding step and achieves meaningful end-to-end speedups on standard hardware for both a pretrained model and in benchmarks applied to a large-scale existing MoE model.
items.citation: Zewen Jin, Shen Fu, Zeping Duan et al.. DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations
items.summary: This paper investigates how intrinsic dimensionality, a measure of representational complexity in language models, is affected by dataset construction choices rather than purely by properties of language itself. The researchers focused on lexical diversity, specifically the number of unique final tokens in a dataset, and examined how it shapes intrinsic dimensionality estimates across different scales. They discovered a scale-dependent transition between two distinct regimes: at low lexical diversity, fewer unique final words paradoxically yield higher intrinsic dimensionality, while at high lexical diversity the relationship reverses, with more unique words producing higher intrinsic dimensionality. The researchers derived an exact, parameter-free formula that accurately predicts the transition point between these two regimes at every scale tested. These findings caution against naively interpreting intrinsic dimensionality as a direct reflection of representational complexity, while also revealing a general organizational principle governing how linguistic data is structured within language model representation spaces.
items.citation: Arwa Osman, Marco Baroni, Iuri Macocco. Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Accelerating Large-scale Bundle Adjustment for LiDAR Mapping via Parallel Computing
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck of LiDAR bundle adjustment, a technique used to build globally consistent large-scale point cloud maps. The authors propose the first fully parallel computing framework for this task, introducing three core innovations: an adaptive asynchronous data loading strategy for memory-constrained GPUs, a bottom-up voxelization method for parallelized planar feature extraction, and a majorization-minimization-based optimization that parallelizes residual, Jacobian, and Hessian computations alongside a parallel increment solver. The framework's time complexity is analyzed both theoretically and experimentally, and the approach is benchmarked across multiple large-scale public datasets and computational platforms. Results demonstrate substantial gains in computational efficiency compared to existing methods while maintaining mapping accuracy on par with state-of-the-art approaches.
items.citation: Yixi Cai, Rundong Li, Yuhan Xie et al.. Accelerating Large-scale Bundle Adjustment for LiDAR Mapping via Parallel Computing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Launching Jets in Tidal Disruption Events: Magnetic Flux Advection and Plasma Loading
items.summary: This paper investigates why only a small fraction of tidal disruption events, in which a star is torn apart by a black hole's tidal forces, produce relativistic jets. The authors propose a scenario in which magnetic flux stored in a pre-existing low-Eddington accretion disk is advected toward the black hole by the super-Eddington accretion flow that develops after stellar disruption, with low-density stars such as red giants being capable of supplying sufficient magnetic flux to power a jet via the Blandford–Znajek mechanism. They find that once enough magnetic flux accumulates near the black hole, an equatorial current sheet forms where magnetic reconnection generates high-energy gamma rays, and subsequent photon–photon pair production supplies the magnetosphere with the plasma needed to launch and sustain the jet. This mechanism is further shown to simultaneously provide enough radiating particles to explain the observed prompt emission from jetted tidal disruption events, thereby addressing both the magnetic flux origin and the plasma loading problems in a unified framework.
items.citation: Rin Oikawa, Yuri Sato. Launching Jets in Tidal Disruption Events: Magnetic Flux Advection and Plasma Loading. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: The study examined whether the benefits of a linkage case management intervention for hospitalized people with HIV would persist beyond the original intervention period. Participants from the Daraja randomized clinical trial were followed for an additional year past the primary endpoint, extending observation to two years after hospital discharge, with outcomes including continuity in HIV care, antiretroviral therapy adherence, and viral load suppression. Intervention participants demonstrated significantly higher rates across all three outcomes compared to those receiving standard care, with differences of more than ten percentage points sustained at the two-year mark. A notable proportion of control participants remained untreated even two years after discharge, underscoring the durability of the intervention's advantage. The findings indicate that linkage case management initiated at hospitalization produces lasting improvements in HIV care engagement and treatment outcomes well beyond the active intervention period.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Willkens M, Issarow B, Kisigo GA et al.. Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.
items.summary: This paper investigated how to distinguish people newly entering HIV care from those transferring between care settings within United States clinical cohorts, a distinction that requires access to historical patient data. The researchers examined the availability of five types of historical HIV data — antiretroviral therapy prescriptions, CD4 counts, viral loads, suppressed viral load at enrollment, and AIDS-defining conditions — across cohorts participating in a large North American collaborative network spanning two decades. Using these data types, they developed an algorithm to classify participants as new to care, transfers, re-engaging after a gap in care, or previously in care with unknown transfer status. They found that the proportion of participants who were transfers grew substantially over time while those genuinely new to care declined, and that the historical timespan between a participant's earliest known HIV date and cohort enrollment also lengthened considerably. The authors recommend that HIV cohorts systematically collect all five data types and apply their classification algorithm to improve the accuracy of care-history characterization in research.
items.citation: Haw NJL, Hogan B, Humes E et al.. New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.. American journal of epidemiology. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable insulated isothermal PCR platform as an alternative to quantitative real-time PCR for diagnosing Mpox caused by MPXV Clade IIb, with particular attention to performance in a cohort with high HIV prevalence. Researchers prospectively enrolled confirmed Mpox patients, testing multiple specimen types with both the portable iiPCR system and reference qPCR, while also assessing viral load dynamics across specimen types and time since symptom onset. The two platforms showed identical analytical limits of detection and complete qualitative concordance, with lesion-derived specimens yielding the highest detection rates and lowest cycle threshold values, while non-lesion specimens showed more variable positivity. Among people living with HIV who were receiving antiretroviral therapy and had preserved immune function, no differences in diagnostic performance were observed compared to HIV-negative individuals. The findings support the potential of the iiPCR platform as a decentralized diagnostic tool for Mpox, particularly when lesion specimens are available.
items.citation: Liu LT, Chen CJ, Lin PC et al.. Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.. Annals of medicine. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, a setting where conventional HRP2-based tests are limited by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the Bioline Malaria multi-Ag RDT, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity declined substantially when qPCR served as the reference, revealing that submicroscopic and low-density infections were frequently missed. qPCR detected the highest overall prevalence of malaria and identified more cases of each species as well as mixed infections than either RDT or microscopy. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is clinically useful for routine diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti during a period when conventional surveillance was disrupted by political instability and security concerns. Researchers repurposed discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients across two Haitian departments, extracting nucleic acids from the test strips and applying a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus, followed by next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Dengue virus serotype three was identified as the sole arbovirus detected, with all positive samples originating from collections made in a single year, and phylogenetic analysis placed these sequences in close relationship to strains circulating across the Caribbean region during the same period. No evidence of alphavirus or Oropouche virus infection was found in the subset of samples tested. The findings demonstrate that discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests can serve as a practical surveillance tool for arboviral pathogens in resource-limited or conflict-affected settings where traditional public health infrastructure is compromised.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper presents an IoT and AI integrated wireless health monitoring framework designed for elderly and chronically ill patients in remote or auxiliary care settings. The system uses ZigBee protocol to transmit physiological data—including heart rate, body temperature, and oxygen levels—from wearable sensors to a centralized cloud-based processing unit with low power consumption and minimal communication delay. Multiple machine learning algorithms, including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression, were applied to detect health anomalies, with the random forest model achieving the highest classification performance. Testing in a real-world care facility demonstrated that the system operates with very low latency and energy consumption, making it suitable for continuous long-term deployment. The authors claim their framework addresses key limitations of existing telehealth systems, such as high latency and excessive false alarms, while offering a scalable and modular design that can accommodate additional sensor types.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.citation: Hedvig Hricak, Zachary J. Ward, Fabio Ynoe Moraes et al.. Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission. The Lancet Oncology. 2026

items.title: Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis
items.summary: The paper investigated why chronic joint inflammation persists in rheumatoid arthritis despite the presence of macrophages that are normally associated with tissue repair. The researchers found that patient-derived pro-repair macrophages in the synovium produce high levels of the complement protein C1q while simultaneously expressing its receptor, creating an autocrine signaling loop. C1q stimulation drove metabolic exhaustion in these macrophages through the enzyme SARM1, which depleted mitochondrial NAD by converting it into cyclic ADP ribose, ultimately triggering a form of inflammatory programmed cell death called PANoptosis. In vivo experiments confirmed that C1q worsened synovitis while pharmacological inhibition of SARM1 provided therapeutic benefit. The study identifies SARM1 as both a marker of metabolically stressed macrophages and a key executor of the pro-inflammatory cell death that sustains pathological tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.citation: Tao Huang, Yoshinori Takashima, Jitendra Kumar et al.. Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis. Immunity. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This study evaluated the safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system embedded in electronic medical records across primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed over a thousand patient encounter records to assess the frequency of hallucinations, guideline adherence, and the clinical safety of the system's recommendations. The system rarely hallucinated and its guidance overwhelmingly aligned with local clinical guidelines, demonstrating strong technical performance. However, a concerning pattern emerged in how clinicians interacted with the tool: harmful recommendations from the model appeared in final documentation at a meaningful rate, while clinicians less consistently adopted the model's beneficial suggestions that could have mitigated pre-existing risks in their own notes. The authors conclude that while the tool shows promise for supporting quality improvement in primary care settings, the asymmetric uptake of harmful versus beneficial outputs highlights the urgent need for usability improvements, locally tailored safeguards, and prospective trials to establish patient-level benefit.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Literature Review of You Only Look Once Architectures (v1–v12) in Healthcare Systems
items.summary: This systematic review examined the application of the full YOLO (You Only Look Once) family of object detection architectures, spanning versions one through twelve, to medical imaging and diagnostic tasks in healthcare. Following established reporting guidelines, the authors retrieved and synthesized peer-reviewed studies that applied YOLO models to tasks including disease and lesion detection across radiological, pathological, ophthalmological, and endoscopic domains, evaluating performance through metrics such as average precision, accuracy, inference time, and computational efficiency. The review found that successive architectural generations have brought progressive improvements in diagnostic performance, with two particular versions emerging as the most widely adopted due to their favorable balance between accuracy and computational demand. Despite strong overall performance across diverse clinical imaging contexts, the review identifies persistent challenges around model interpretability, generalization across institutions, and deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize explainability in YOLO-based diagnostic systems and the development of energy-efficient model designs.
items.citation: Özgür Koray Şahingöz, Gozde Karatas Baydoğmus, Emin Kugu. A Systematic Literature Review of You Only Look Once Architectures (v1–v12) in Healthcare Systems. Diagnostics. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: The paper addresses limitations in existing image editing benchmarks, which are restricted to simple single-image tasks and struggle to differentiate performance across diverse models or capture real-world complexity. To overcome these shortcomings, the authors propose CPI-Bench, a benchmark comprising three subsets targeting general editing diversity (including multi-image editing), high-frequency practical user scenarios, and reasoning-intensive editing tasks. Evaluations of mainstream image editing models using CPI-Bench demonstrate improved performance differentiation compared to prior benchmarks, providing more reliable quantification of gaps across general, practical, and reasoning-based editing capabilities. Notably, ranking analysis shows that CPI-Bench achieves the highest alignment with a human-preference leaderboard, suggesting it faithfully reflects real-world user judgments and can serve as a robust proxy for human evaluation.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection

items.title: The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: This paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources make a design error by concatenating all sources into a single prompt, conflating two fundamentally distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a decision. items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper presents a method for discovering and tracking roles in temporal dynamic networks, where the structure of connections changes over time. The approach uses temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization to produce a consistent set of roles across all time periods, accompanied by a universal transition matrix describing the probability of moving between roles, with a regularization penalty to prevent abrupt changes in role membership between time steps. The method was evaluated on multiple real-world and synthetic datasets using both engineered and automatically learned features. Results indicate that with appropriate regularization weighting, the approach reduces prediction errors compared to existing techniques and produces a more stable system in which individuals tend to remain in their roles with fewer arbitrary transitions. The model is also reported to scale efficiently to large, sparse graphs.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026
