items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This review synthesizes major advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over roughly a five-year period, culminating in updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types and populations. Progress in drug-resistance testing has been marked by new molecular platforms and the formal endorsement of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive drug-susceptibility profiling at reference laboratory level, while novel specimen types including tongue swabs and pooled sputum have improved bacteriological confirmation in children and others unable to produce sputum. Urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic gains in people with HIV and advanced disease, though their broader applicability remains limited, and host blood transcriptomic signatures show promise for triage and prognosis without yet meeting criteria for point-of-care use. The authors conclude that substantial gaps in performance, implementation, and equity persist, and that no biomarker has yet achieved the WHO target product profile for reliably distinguishing infection from disease, particularly subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from 1990 to the present, focusing on the particular challenges posed by this co-infection. People with HIV present diagnostic difficulties because they tend to have lower bacillary loads in sputum, higher rates of extrapulmonary or disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, while simultaneously requiring rapid diagnosis due to swift disease progression. The review traces the limitations of earlier approaches, including smear microscopy and smear-negative diagnostic algorithms, which contributed to both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis with consequent increases in mortality and missed alternative diagnoses. The introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside the widespread use of antiretroviral therapy, has substantially improved the diagnostic landscape and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and deaths. Nevertheless, the authors conclude that significant gaps remain, as no currently available rapid test achieves ideal sensitivity and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection is simultaneously affordable and suitable for point-of-care use, underscoring the continued need for novel accurate diagnostic tools.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.
items.summary: This scoping review examined how coverage of rapid molecular testing for tuberculosis has been conceptualized and measured across different international settings. The authors systematically searched multiple major databases spanning over a decade to identify and synthesize relevant studies on the topic. The review found substantial conceptual heterogeneity in how coverage was defined and operationalized, ranging from testing proportions in specific population groups to indicators of equipment availability and geographic access, with no standardization across countries. Reported coverage values varied enormously, and socioeconomic, structural, and financial barriers were consistently identified as obstacles to test uptake. The authors conclude that meaningful comparison and expansion of rapid molecular test coverage requires greater methodological standardization, governmental commitment, decentralization of testing services, and alignment with international guidelines.
items.venue: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
items.citation: Silva DHMD, Valença ABM, Ferreira MRL et al.. Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.. Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P. 2026

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, a persistent global health threat caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*. The authors survey current serological biomarkers being explored for TB diagnosis and discuss how advanced diagnostic technologies can be integrated with these markers. Serological methods are highlighted for their simplicity, speed, and cost-effectiveness, making them particularly valuable for diagnosing extrapulmonary TB and for patients who test negative using conventional sputum culture or rapid molecular assays. The review argues that continued identification of novel biomarkers, combined with emerging diagnostic platforms, holds meaningful potential to improve TB detection across varied clinical contexts.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests, Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance in presumptive TB patients in India. Using mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing as reference standards, the researchers prospectively tested paired sputum specimens from over six hundred patients at a tuberculosis centre in New Delhi. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for both TB detection and rifampicin resistance identification, and produced substantially fewer invalid and indeterminate results compared to Truenat MTB Plus. However, Truenat offered a considerably lower cost per test, making it more attractive for decentralized deployment despite the increased operational burden associated with its higher rates of invalid and repeat testing. The authors conclude that a tiered diagnostic strategy leveraging both platforms according to their respective strengths could help expand molecular testing access and advance global TB elimination efforts.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.
items.summary: This study examined the feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis, a strategy in which samples from multiple individuals are combined into a single molecular assay to reduce costs and extend access to rapid diagnostics in resource-limited settings. Using a multicountry qualitative design, researchers conducted key informant interviews and focus group discussions with a range of stakeholders—including national tuberculosis programme representatives, laboratory technicians, people with tuberculosis, and international experts—across seven high-burden countries in Africa, Asia, and South America. Feasibility was found to depend on compatibility with existing diagnostic algorithms and laboratory workflows, biosafety standards, staff training, and clear standard operating procedures. Acceptability operated at two levels: securing professional buy-in through early engagement with healthcare providers, and ensuring that people undergoing testing received clear communication about the approach. Overall, pooled testing was considered a pragmatic and workable strategy in settings with sufficiently robust laboratory infrastructure, though readiness varied considerably across countries, with some requiring system strengthening before implementation could be scaled up.
items.citation: Iem V, Vo LNQ, Codlin AJ et al.. Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.. BMJ open. 2026

items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: The paper reports on the implementation and outcomes of the NHS England Targeted Lung Health Check Programme, a national lung cancer screening initiative that began in 2019 and aims for full coverage by 2030. Individuals aged 55 to 74 who had ever smoked were invited for low-dose computed tomography screening if they met risk thresholds determined by multivariable models, delivered through a regionally federated clinical infrastructure guided by national frameworks. Over five years the programme invited more than two million people and diagnosed thousands of lung cancers, with the majority detected at early tumor-node-metastasis stages, representing a meaningful shift toward earlier-stage diagnosis across England and particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions. The authors conclude that large-scale, rapid implementation of lung cancer screening is feasible and scalable in reaching high-risk and underserved populations, though inequalities in participation remain a challenge to be addressed. They argue these findings support broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the United Kingdom and internationally, and offer practical frameworks for adaptation elsewhere.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and structural bone and cartilage damage. The authors synthesized current knowledge on nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system, as well as pathological changes in bone architecture and chondrocytes driven by inflammatory cytokines and organelle dysfunction. Key drivers of disease progression identified include mitochondrial dysfunction with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization caused by hydroxyapatite digestion, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress arising from compensatory protein overproduction. Based on these mechanistic insights, the review outlines emerging pharmacological strategies that simultaneously target inflammatory cascades, restore organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuate pain signaling. The authors further highlight organelle-targeted drug delivery systems as a means to improve therapeutic efficacy, collectively proposing a multimodal framework for novel osteoarthritis interventions.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities
items.summary: This review examines the NLRP3 inflammasome, a key innate immune signaling platform capable of detecting a wide range of microbial, metabolic, and environmental danger signals. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms driving NLRP3 activation, including ion flux, mitochondrial damage, lysosomal rupture, reactive oxygen species, and post-translational modifications, as well as the negative regulatory pathways that keep inflammasome activity in check. Activation of this complex recruits ASC and caspase-1, leading to maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 and induction of pyroptotic cell death, processes that when dysregulated contribute to autoinflammatory syndromes, metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, neurodegeneration, and cancer. The review also surveys therapeutic strategies targeting NLRP3, encompassing direct inhibitors, allosteric modulators, biologics, and repurposed drugs, evaluating their translational prospects. The authors conclude that a deeper understanding of the balance between NLRP3 activation and inhibition opens meaningful opportunities for treating a broad spectrum of inflammatory and immune-related diseases.
items.citation: Chan Zou, Shilong Jiang, Hui Li et al.. The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities. MedComm. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents an updated set of clinical practice recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for the management of Behçet's syndrome, a complex multisystem inflammatory disorder. A large multinational task force spanning multiple medical specialties, including patient representatives, used a systematic literature review informed by structured research questions to revise and expand upon prior guidance. The updated framework comprises five overarching principles and twelve recommendations organized by organ involvement, with one entirely new recommendation and the majority of existing ones substantively modified. Key guidance emphasizes individualizing treatment to disease activity and prognostic factors, with colchicine as first-line therapy for mucocutaneous and joint disease, apremilast or TNFα inhibitors for refractory cases, and early use of monoclonal anti-TNFα agents alongside glucocorticoids and immunosuppressives for organ-threatening or life-threatening manifestations. The recommendations also stress the importance of a multidisciplinary approach, patient education, and shared decision-making to optimize care quality across all affected organ systems.
items.citation: Gulen Hatemi, Sofia Ramiro, Yeşim Özgüler et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), pattern recognition receptors on immune cells that drive inflammatory signalling and are implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary behaviour and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was the sole intervention in human participants, categorising findings by exercise modality (resistance, aerobic, or combined) and duration (acute or chronic training programs). Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise more often produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, while chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise and TLR signalling interact in a modality- and duration-dependent manner, but caution that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing

Notably, the benchmark's rankings align more closely with a human-preference leaderboard than existing alternatives, suggesting it serves as a reliable proxy for real-world user experience and can guide future model optimization.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.summary: This paper examines systems that use language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources, arguing that concatenating all sources into a single prompt conflates two fundamentally distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a final decision. items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting and tracking roles that nodes play in networks as they evolve over time. The authors developed a dynamic role discovery method based on temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization, which enforces consistency in role definitions across time periods and applies a regularization penalty to prevent abrupt changes in role membership between consecutive time steps. A universal transition matrix is learned to characterize the probabilities of nodes moving between roles over time. The method was evaluated on multiple real-world and synthetic datasets using both engineered and automatically extracted features, demonstrating reduced prediction errors compared to existing approaches when an appropriate regularization weight is chosen. Analysis of the transition matrices further showed that the resulting system is more stable, with nodes tending to remain in their roles rather than making arbitrary transitions, and the approach scales efficiently to large, sparse graphs.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
items.summary: This paper introduces Twin, a Test-time World-model Inference system designed to tackle continual learning tasks such as ARC-AGI-3 games, where the rules and goals of each game are hidden and must be discovered through interaction alone. Rather than hand-engineering a custom model for each task, a frontier coding agent constructs an executable world model by simulating and interacting with the game environment, using a validation mechanism that requires the world model to reproduce every previously observed game transition before any action is taken. When the world model's predictions diverge from actual outcomes, the discrepancy is treated as a counterexample used to repair the model, iteratively refining it toward the true underlying rules. The system achieves near-complete success on the benchmark, clearing the vast majority of levels and outperforming human efficiency on most of those it clears, with the world model approach dramatically improving performance over both the base model alone and a standard off-the-shelf harness. A key finding is that constructing a functional world model proved more tractable than anticipated, while correctly inferring the game's goal—which the system accomplishes before receiving any reward on most cleared levels—emerged as the harder underlying challenge.
items.citation: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano et al.. Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic on the outskirts of Beirut, while also assessing their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, a physician conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and collected data through an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, risk behaviours, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese men, though a notable minority were Syrian, and a substantial proportion were living with HIV. Despite high levels of STI and HIV awareness among participants, condomless sex and recreational drug use were common, and HIV-related stigma emerged as a significant barrier to testing and care-seeking. The study concludes that integrating point-of-care testing into community sexual health services enables same-day diagnosis, counselling, and linkage to confirmatory care, representing a valuable approach for reaching this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the costs of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, compared to the standard syndromic management approach. Researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare and collected economic cost data through staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and review of study records, then modelled implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. The prevalence of the targeted infections was notably high among pregnant women screened, with test kits and personnel representing the dominant cost components. The incremental costs per person screened and treated were substantially higher for point-of-care testing than for syndromic management, primarily driven by test kit and personnel expenses. The authors conclude that reductions in the cost of point-of-care diagnostic tests will be essential for this screening approach to become a feasible and scalable component of routine antenatal care.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote Australian First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is disproportionately high among young people. Using a decision analytic model with a government payer perspective and a ten-year time horizon, the researchers compared point-of-care testing against standard laboratory-based testing in terms of costs and quality-adjusted life years gained. The programme was found to be cost-effective relative to the willingness-to-pay threshold used, generating a favourable incremental cost per quality-adjusted life year ratio. Beyond cost-effectiveness, the model predicted meaningful reductions in pelvic inflammatory disease diagnoses and preterm or low birth weight births among those with infections. The analysis concludes that sustained, scaled point-of-care testing in remote primary care settings is a cost-effective strategy likely to improve reproductive health outcomes for this population.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of various testing and screening strategies for trichomoniasis, the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection in women, across both symptomatic and asymptomatic populations in U.S. primary care settings. Researchers constructed a decision tree model applied to a hypothetical cohort of women aged 15 to 59 years, comparing eleven strategies using combinations of wet mount microscopy, rapid antigen testing, and nucleic acid amplification testing, while accounting for downstream health consequences including preterm birth, HIV acquisition, and cervical cancer over the cohort's lifetime. They found that adding nucleic acid amplification testing to wet mount microscopy for symptomatic women improved health outcomes and fell within a commonly accepted willingness-to-pay threshold, making it a cost-effective approach. By contrast, adding nucleic acid amplification testing to rapid antigen testing for symptomatic women, as well as universal nucleic acid amplification testing screening of asymptomatic women, exceeded that threshold and were not considered cost-effective at standard benchmarks. The findings suggest that while enhanced testing can improve outcomes for symptomatic women, broader asymptomatic screening would require substantially higher societal willingness-to-pay thresholds to be economically justified.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Rong R, Stoecker C, Kissinger PJ et al.. Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.
items.summary: This review examines the epidemiology, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnosis, and prevention of anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections, focusing primarily on chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis. The authors synthesize current evidence on why these infections are rising globally despite available testing, noting that anorectal infections are frequently asymptomatic—particularly among men who have sex with men—due to bacterial adaptation to rectal tissues and attenuated local immune responses. Molecular diagnostics have improved detection, but challenges remain in distinguishing viable from non-viable organisms, expanding point-of-care testing, and managing antimicrobial stewardship, especially as gonorrhoea develops resistance to existing treatments. The review highlights doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis and artificial intelligence applications as promising prevention advances, while acknowledging that implementing these tools broadly across diverse clinical settings remains difficult. The authors identify key gaps in knowledge and propose research priorities to strengthen control of these infections.
items.citation: Latt PM, Kong FYS, Khosropour CM et al.. Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.. Nature reviews. Gastroenterology & hepatology. 2026

items.title: Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective
items.summary: This paper examines how digitalization and technologization intersect with gender dynamics in contemporary digital culture, asking whether digital transformation constitutes a paradigmatic shift in how gender identities are constructed, performed, and contested. Through a systematic literature review of recent high-impact research, the study draws on feminist theory, sociology, communication studies, health informatics, and STEM education to analyze these intersections from an intersectional perspective. The findings reveal that digital technologies carry genuine emancipatory potential by enabling anonymity, accessibility, and broader public participation, yet simultaneously replicate and intensify patriarchal norms through mechanisms such as cyberviolence, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, and persistent underrepresentation of women in STEM. Digital spaces are therefore characterized not as ideologically neutral or inherently egalitarian, but as contested terrains where power relations are renegotiated in novel forms. The paper concludes by calling for intersectional, gender-sensitive policies and multi-stakeholder collaborations to resist the reinforcement of masculine dominance and to cultivate inclusive, equitable technological ecosystems.
items.venue: Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics
items.citation: Şevki Işıklı, Esra Fatma FAZLIOĞLU. Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective. Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
items.summary: This narrative review examines the current state of knowledge on Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder and Problematic Pornography Use, two widely studied but contested constructs relating to dysregulated sexual behavior. Drawing on contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized empirical and theoretical literature across eleven key domains, including historical context, assessment, epidemiology, etiology, co-occurring disorders, potential harms, and treatment. The review also addresses underrepresented groups such as adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors in shaping how these behaviors are understood and experienced. The authors identify persistent methodological challenges and ongoing conceptual controversies that have hampered progress in the field. The work concludes by calling for greater interdisciplinary collaboration and more rigorous research to strengthen clinical practice and inform public health policy.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis investigated epidemiological approaches to controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with a focus on contact tracing and screening as tools for identifying asymptomatic infected individuals. The research evaluated contact tracing routines, compared characteristics of chlamydia-infected women and their partners identified through different clinical settings, and assessed whether contact tracing data could inform mathematical models of partner choice and disease spread. Contact tracing successfully controlled a gonorrhoea microepidemic and identified previously unknown HIV-positive individuals, while chlamydia screening in family planning clinics revealed meaningful prevalence and identified key risk factors including young age, short relationship duration, and inconsistent condom use. Comparisons between chlamydia cases found through screening versus those presenting at sexually transmitted disease clinics showed only minor differences in partner numbers and infection rates, leading to the conclusion that both groups warrant equivalent effort in partner management. Partner choice analysis indicated that steady partnerships were relatively restricted while casual partnerships followed a more random pattern, findings that do not support a purely random mixing model for describing disease spread.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks
items.summary: This study examined the relationship between housing instability and drug overdose risk among young people who inject drugs, with a focus on developing a more comprehensive measure of housing instability than those used in prior research. Using baseline data from a network-based longitudinal study of young people who inject drugs and their social networks in metropolitan Chicago, the researchers constructed a multi-dimensional housing instability risk index comprising five dichotomous variables, then analyzed its association with lifetime overdose count using negative binomial regression. After adjusting for multiple covariates, a significant positive association was found between higher housing instability risk scores and greater lifetime overdose counts. The findings support the value of a multi-dimensional, holistic approach to measuring housing instability over single-dimension operationalizations such as housing type or homelessness status alone. The authors conclude that interventions targeting overdose risk should incorporate this broader conceptualization of housing instability to better identify and address vulnerability in this population.
items.citation: Kathleen Kristensen, Leslie D. Williams, Charlie Kaplan et al.. A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks. Journal of Urban Health. 2026

items.title: Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads
items.summary: This paper developed an enzyme-free platform for ultrasensitive protein biomarker detection intended to make advanced diagnostics accessible in resource-limited settings. The researchers adapted the Molecular On-bead Signal Amplification for Individual Counting approach by replacing enzymatic signal amplification with hybridization chain reaction-based amplifiers on magnetic beads, simplifying the assay workflow. The resulting platform, termed efMOSAIC, achieved detection limits comparable to established single-molecule detection methods such as Simoa, which are orders of magnitude more sensitive than conventional ELISA. A key practical advantage demonstrated was that the signal amplifier reagents remained stable at room temperature for at least six months, eliminating the need for cold chain infrastructure. The platform was validated for detecting cytokines in human plasma and shown to support multiplexed biomarker detection, positioning it as a promising tool for ultrasensitive diagnostics in low- and middle-income countries and point-of-care settings.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Karan Malhotra, Louise L. Hansen, Samuel Han et al.. Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Cancer Incidence in Women After Medically Assisted Reproduction
items.summary: This large population-based cohort study examined cancer incidence among Australian women who underwent medically assisted reproduction, comparing outcomes against age- and calendar year-matched general population data using linked administrative health and cancer registry records. Three treatment groups were studied: assisted reproductive therapy, intrauterine insemination with ovarian stimulation, and ovulation induction with clomiphene citrate, encompassing hundreds of thousands of women followed over many years. Overall invasive cancer incidence was comparable to the general population for all three treatment groups, though the clomiphene citrate group showed a slight elevation. Certain site-specific cancers, including uterine cancer, melanoma, and ovarian cancer, were elevated across some or all cohorts, while cervical and lung cancers occurred less frequently than expected; however, the absolute excess numbers of cases were small. The authors conclude that while medically assisted reproduction does not appear to meaningfully increase overall cancer risk, the findings on specific cancer types warrant attention in clinical counselling, though causation cannot be established from this descriptive evidence.
items.citation: Claire Melissa Vajdic, Adrian Walker, Antoinette Anazodo et al.. Cancer Incidence in Women After Medically Assisted Reproduction. JAMA Network Open. 2026

items.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of validating large language model-driven modernization of legacy scientific software, specifically questioning whether such transformations preserve not just nominal behavior but also how code responds to faults, numerical perturbations, and reduced precision. The researchers developed a differential fault-injection methodology that instruments a shared computational driver in the quantum chemistry package GAMESS at multiple sites, applying identical deterministic faults to both original and modernized code versions to isolate differences in the converted components. Across thousands of runs, the method characterized how transient and persistent faults propagate through self-consistent-field calculations, revealing phase-dependent parallel deadlocks and false convergence under reduced precision that nominal testing would miss. Critically, the original and LLM-modernized integral kernels showed complete agreement across all paired fault injections, and a synchronization fix derived from the campaign also composed correctly with the modernization. The work establishes differential fault injection as a rigorous complement to nominal validation for assessing the fidelity of automated code modernization.
items.citation: Evan Coleman, Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina et al.. Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive set of lecture notes covering classical and quantum entropy from both mathematical and physical perspectives. The work develops classical entropies through large deviation theory and connects them to statistical physics, then extends the treatment to quantum entropies by emphasizing their role in statistical hypothesis testing as the deeper structural link to their classical counterparts. The quantum treatment progresses through increasingly sophisticated mathematical machinery, including Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and Haagerup's noncommutative function spaces, to rigorously define and compute relative entropies such as those introduced by Araki and Uhlmann on von Neumann algebras. The lectures also introduce a quantum analogue of Kolmogorov-Sinai dynamical entropy in the setting of von Neumann algebras and ergodic theory. The course is designed to be simultaneously rigorous for mathematicians and accessible to theoretical physicists, with black hole thermodynamics as a motivating application, though that application itself is not covered.
items.citation: Klaas Landsman. The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Learning-to-Transition for Large-scale and High-Order MIMO Detection
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of high-order MIMO detection, which requires searching over large discrete symbol spaces while providing reliable soft information for channel decoding. The authors develop a learning-to-transition framework that models MIMO detection as a stochastic sequence of complete-vector transitions, using a channel-coupled Transformer with a blockwise autoregressive factorization to capture inter-stream dependencies at manageable complexity. For hard-output detection, the system is trained through a residual-to-bit-error-rate curriculum that first learns the search geometry from residual metrics before aligning with transmitted-bit accuracy. For soft-output detection within an iterative detection and decoding receiver, the trained hard-output policy is transferred to each receiver layer through a tied-to-untied parameter cloning strategy, allowing layer-specific specialization under decoder feedback while preserving the original search dynamics. The framework incorporates Bayesian prior tilting during candidate generation and a multi-stage training strategy to stabilize the transition from hard to soft detection, ultimately producing posterior and extrinsic log-likelihood ratios compatible with LDPC decoding.
items.citation: Yubo Zhang, Yiyao Liu, Xiaodong Wang. Learning-to-Transition for Large-scale and High-Order MIMO Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of identifying and tracking roles that nodes play in networks that evolve over time. The authors developed a dynamic role discovery method based on temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization, which enforces consistency in role definitions across all time periods and applies a regularization penalty to prevent abrupt changes in role membership between consecutive time steps. Unlike existing approaches, the method also learns a universal transition matrix that quantifies the probability of moving between roles over time. Testing on multiple real-world and one synthetic dataset, using both engineered and automatically generated node features, showed that appropriate regularization reduces role prediction errors compared to alternative techniques. Analysis of the transition matrices further revealed that the resulting system is more stable, with individuals tending to remain in their roles rather than making arbitrary transitions, while the approach also scales efficiently to large, sparse graphs.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
items.summary: This paper introduces a system called Twin (Test-time World-model Inference) designed to play unknown games by constructing executable world models at test time, without any prior knowledge of the game's rules or goals. Rather than relying on hand-engineered models, the system uses a frontier coding agent to infer game transitions and objectives purely through simulation and interaction, with a digital twin world model used to validate actions by ensuring the program reproduces every previously observed game transition before any real action is taken. Mismatches between world model predictions and actual outcomes serve as counterexamples that trigger automatic repair of the model. The system was evaluated on a continual learning benchmark of grid-based games, where it successfully cleared the vast majority of levels, outperforming human efficiency on most of them and frequently inferring the correct goal before receiving any reward signal. A key finding is that constructing a functional world model proved more tractable than anticipated, while correctly identifying the goal emerged as the more challenging aspect of the problem.
items.citation: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano et al.. Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational complexity of the tournament isomorphism problem, which is a central bottleneck in developing faster algorithms for graph isomorphism. The authors focus on tournaments of bounded VC dimension, a class for which no prior algorithmic results existed despite the VC dimension being a fundamental notion of combinatorial tameness. To resolve an open problem, they develop a new isomorphism-invariant decomposition method for tournaments, introduce the concept of a patched tournament to enable recursion, and design a recursive algorithm that balances piece sizes against their number while exploiting near-twin structure. Their main result establishes that isomorphism of tournaments with VC dimension bounded by a parameter can be decided in quasipolynomial time in the input size, and that automorphism groups of such tournaments can be computed in polynomial time. As a complementary result, they also show that tournament isomorphism is polynomial-time decidable for tournaments of bounded chromatic number, addressing the class that characterizes unbounded VC dimension in hereditary tournament families.
items.citation: Simon Raßmann, Pascal Schweitzer. Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension. arXiv. 2026

query: CRISPR based diagnostics infectious disease detection

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a CRISPR-Cas12a diagnostic assay for the rapid, specific detection of *Shigella flexneri* 2a, the leading serotype causing shigellosis and a significant public health burden in developing countries. The assay couples recombinase polymerase amplification with Cas12a-mediated collateral cleavage, targeting two genes unique to the *S. flexneri* 2a serotype, and supports both fluorescence and lateral flow readouts without requiring specialized equipment. The method achieves a detection limit of ten copies per microliter, completes within one hour at room temperature, and showed complete analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity against other bacteria. Clinical validation using a large cohort of stool specimens demonstrated diagnostic sensitivity and specificity comparable to conventional PCR. The authors conclude that the assay's simplicity, speed, and accuracy make it well-suited for point-of-care diagnostics and field-based surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The study developed a centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD to enable rapid, multiplexed point-of-care detection of respiratory pathogens while overcoming sensitivity and complexity trade-offs in existing systems. The platform integrates a polymethyl methacrylate rotating disc pre-loaded with lyophilized CRISPR/Cas13a reagents with a portable fluorescence analyzer, and employs a novel resin-based nucleic acid purification method for throat swab samples. The system can simultaneously screen six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples in a single automated run. Analytical validation confirmed single-copy sensitivity with no cross-reactivity, and clinical validation using retrospective patient samples demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity. The authors conclude that iCARD represents a robust and accurate tool suitable for decentralized molecular screening and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.
items.summary: This review examines how CRISPR-based diagnostic systems can be engineered to achieve single-nucleotide discrimination in nucleic acid detection, addressing the persistent challenge of off-target activation and insufficient specificity when distinguishing closely related sequences. The authors synthesize advances in CRISPR RNA engineering, detailing how structural features such as spacer length, intentional mismatch design, secondary-structure modulation, chemical modification, and strand-displacement gating collectively govern target recognition and cleavage fidelity. Key strategies including computational prediction, high-throughput screening, and hybrid guide architectures are assessed for their ability to improve single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination, stabilize assay performance, and enable multiplexed detection of pathogens and disease-associated mutations. The review identifies remaining obstacles including interference from complex clinical samples, the absence of unified evaluation standards, and scalability limitations that currently impede clinical translation. The authors conclude that integrated crRNA design combined with system-level optimization and standardized benchmarking will be essential to realizing portable, ultrasensitive point-of-care diagnostics capable of supporting precision medicine and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: Sun T, Yuan A, Xie W et al.. CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.. Angewandte Chemie (International ed. in English). 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for COVID-19 diagnosis, motivated by the pandemic's demonstration of urgent need for rapid, decentralized diagnostic tools. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases and evaluated molecular assays, antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods including rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suitable for decentralized use, while antigen tests provide speed and affordability but with variable performance depending on viral load, symptom timing, and circulating variants. Antibody-based testing was deemed more appropriate for seroprevalence and immune monitoring than acute infection detection, and emerging biosensor and AI systems showed promise but largely remain at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical assessment. The review concludes that no single testing modality is universally optimal, and that the complementary strengths of different approaches, combined with advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient design, will be essential for both COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examines the translational progress of CRISPR-Cas systems across three major applications in infectious disease management: diagnostics, therapeutic genome editing, and vaccine development. The authors surveyed a decade of advances, focusing on diagnostic platforms that enable rapid pathogen detection, CRISPR-Cas9-based strategies targeting viral genomes and antimicrobial resistance, and the engineering of live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. They found that CRISPR-based diagnostics have advanced furthest toward clinical evaluation, while therapeutic applications and personalized neoantigen vaccines remain at earlier, more exploratory stages, largely due to challenges in delivery, safety, and regulatory oversight. The review uniquely integrates all three application areas within a single infectious disease framework and critically assesses the maturity of each, identifying off-target effects, delivery inefficiency, and ethical concerns as key barriers to safe and equitable clinical translation. The authors conclude that although CRISPR-Cas holds transformative potential for infectious disease management, these technical and regulatory challenges must be systematically addressed before widespread clinical implementation can be realized.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.
items.summary: This review paper examines the evolution and clinical integration of polymerase chain reaction technology and related molecular diagnostic tools in laboratory medicine. The authors survey the progression from traditional PCR to advanced platforms including quantitative, digital, reverse transcription, and multiplex variants, assessing how each contributes to nucleic acid detection, quantification, and high-throughput analysis. The paper also explores how PCR-based approaches can be combined with next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, microarrays, and epigenetic profiling to provide more comprehensive characterization of disease states. Particular attention is given to clinically relevant molecular targets in oncology, such as mutations in cancer-associated genes and circulating tumor DNA, as well as applications in infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial resistance tracking, inherited disorder detection, and minimal residual disease monitoring. The authors conclude that while challenges related to cost, standardization, skilled personnel, and data management persist, ongoing technological advances including liquid biopsy, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted multi-omics integration are steadily expanding access to precision molecular diagnostics.
items.venue: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
items.citation: Saleem MA, Riaz T, Saleem F et al.. PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.. Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, with implications for both food safety and clinical healthcare. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have substantially improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability constraints, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI frameworks, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review examines the diverse programs by which cancer cells die and how their evasion contributes to tumor development, progression, and treatment resistance. The authors synthesize knowledge across apoptosis and more recently characterized modalities including necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, framing these within a unified conceptual model of cancer biology. While apoptosis remains the dominant mechanism triggered by conventional radiation and chemotherapy, non-apoptotic programs are highlighted for their capacity to generate inflammatory signals that shape interactions between tumor cells, stromal tissue, and the immune system, with consequent effects on immunotherapy efficacy. Ferroptosis receives particular attention as a distinct, iron-dependent modality driven by lipid peroxidation and perturbations in redox and iron metabolism, lacking a single canonical induction signal. The review ultimately argues that a deeper mechanistic understanding of these cell death programs, and of how tumors resist them, is essential for developing strategies to restore cancer cell death therapeutically.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, which combine light-activated mechanisms with nanomaterials to treat a broad range of diseases with improved precision. The authors survey the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that enhance light absorption, reactive oxygen species generation, and localized heating in photodynamic and photothermal therapy. At the molecular level, the paper dissects how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic pathways, and modulate immune responses including cytokine profiles and T-cell activity, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The review further evaluates regulatory-approved agents and recent clinical trial findings, while identifying key barriers to clinical translation such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery, and regulatory challenges. The authors conclude that integrating molecular understanding with clinical advances positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative noninvasive strategy for a wide spectrum of diseases.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines new approach methodologies (NAMs) as alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which has long been hampered by high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-based, organoid-based, and computational approaches that now cover the full drug-discovery continuum, from disease modeling and drug design through efficacy testing. The review highlights progress in identifying therapeutic candidates, developing novel experimental models and technologies, and even exploring NAMs themselves as potential treatments in preclinical and clinical settings. The authors also assess the biological, technical, and regulatory obstacles that must be overcome for these methods to achieve robust translational adoption. They conclude by outlining future human-centric drug-discovery pipelines and the societal considerations necessary for the responsible integration of NAMs into mainstream pharmaceutical development.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examined candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that ranks among the most significant hospital-acquired infections due to its high mortality and healthcare burden. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature synthesis covering the epidemiology and species distribution of candidemia, the shortcomings of conventional diagnostic methods, and the challenges of optimizing antifungal treatment in the context of emerging resistance. The review evaluated both established and emerging diagnostic technologies, as well as therapeutic strategies ranging from empiric and targeted antifungal regimens to combination therapies and the management of mixed infections. The authors also assessed the pipeline of novel antifungal agents targeting new fungal pathways and explored future directions including the application of artificial intelligence to diagnostics and the development of vaccine-based prophylaxis. Overall, the review argues that advances in rapid diagnostics, susceptibility-guided therapy, and innovative treatment approaches are essential to improving patient outcomes and addressing the evolving challenges of candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines antimicrobial resistance as a major global public health threat, focusing on the bacterial pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesized current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms by which these pathogens resist antibiotics, encompassing reduced membrane permeability, efflux pumps, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic therapies and traditional drug discovery pipelines have proven inadequate against multidrug-resistant organisms, while assessing emerging approaches such as artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds in terms of their pharmacological feasibility and translational barriers. The authors also address practical challenges including toxicity, dosing, resistance emergence, and regulatory obstacles that complicate real-world implementation of these strategies. The review concludes that combating WHO-priority pathogens requires integrated, multidisciplinary efforts spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, and public health, including antimicrobial stewardship and a One Health framework that encompasses human, animal, and environmental sectors.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the IceCube neutrino detector can probe dark matter particles that have been accelerated to relativistic speeds by proton jets in blazars, a process known as blazar boosting. The authors computed the diffuse dark matter flux from a large sample of blazars, using proton spectra inferred from multiwavelength observations and incorporating dark matter spike profiles around the supermassive black holes at their centers, while accounting for propagation and attenuation effects. The dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section was carefully modeled across multiple interaction regimes—elastic scattering, resonant single-pion production, and deep inelastic scattering—to smoothly bridge the transition between low- and high-energy interaction channels. Applying this framework to IceCube data, the authors derived constraints on the dark matter parameter space and found that this approach can exceed the sensitivity of conventional direct-detection experiments for dark matter masses below roughly one GeV. They also found that the signal is dominated by deep inelastic scattering, making it more sensitive to heavier mediators, while resonant pion production modestly suppresses event rates near the detector threshold.
items.citation: Alberto M. Gago, Jaime Hoefken Zink, Joel Jones-Pérez et al.. Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters
items.summary: This paper investigates how cosmic rays accelerated in young massive stellar clusters propagate through their environments and produce the extended very high energy gamma-ray halos detected by observatories such as LHAASO. The authors first develop a theoretical framework showing that magnetic mirror diffusion combined with pitch-angle scattering in turbulent flows suppresses cosmic-ray transport, yielding an energy-dependent diffusion coefficient scaling as the cube root of energy. They then couple three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a young massive stellar cluster with Monte Carlo cosmic-ray propagation calculations, using the cluster W43 as a benchmark case and testing both a central point source and a spherical shell injection geometry. Their results demonstrate that this suppressed diffusion regime, combined with a standard injection spectrum, successfully reproduces the gamma-ray spectra observed by Fermi and LHAASO, whereas conventional stronger energy-dependent diffusion requires an unusually hard injection spectrum to match the data. The study concludes that the observed gamma-ray emission is governed primarily by the diffusion regime rather than the specific location where cosmic rays are injected, and that the relative contributions of leptonic and hadronic emission processes depend sensitively on which diffusion regime operates.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
items.citation: Lucas Barreto-Mota, Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino, Gaetano Di Marco et al.. Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: The paper addresses limitations in existing image editing benchmarks, which are restricted to simple single-image tasks and struggle to differentiate model performance across diverse and complex scenarios. To overcome these shortcomings, the authors developed CPI-Bench, a benchmark comprising three subsets targeting general editing coverage (including multi-image tasks), practical high-frequency user scenarios, and reasoning-intensive editing tasks. The benchmark was used to evaluate mainstream image editing models, revealing meaningful performance distinctions that prior benchmarks could not capture. Ranking analysis showed that CPI-Bench achieves stronger alignment with a human-preference leaderboard than existing benchmarks, suggesting it serves as a reliable proxy for real-world user experience and evaluation.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump
items.summary: The paper describes a GPU-based implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics using a momentum-jump-free theoretical framework. To optimize performance on GPU hardware, the authors eliminated trajectory spawning — a sampling enhancement technique previously used in CPU implementations — because it introduces thread divergence and dynamic memory allocation overhead that are particularly costly on GPUs. This redesign achieved roughly an order-of-magnitude speedup relative to the CPU implementation with spawning, while also delivering linear scaling with the number of sampling trajectories.
items.citation: Koji Ando. GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of restoring degraded images at very high resolutions, where maintaining global structural consistency while recovering fine local details is particularly difficult. The authors introduce MagnifiQ, a framework that progressively upscales and restores images through multiple intermediate resolution stages rather than attempting direct reconstruction at the target resolution. The approach adapts a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model by replacing self-attention layers with convolutional operations to achieve linear rather than quadratic computational scaling with resolution, and incorporates patch-specific text prompts to provide spatially localized semantic guidance that controls content drift during restoration. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world degraded images demonstrate that MagnifiQ outperforms existing diffusion-based restoration methods in perceptual quality and human preference, producing sharper textures and more globally coherent results at high resolution.
items.citation: Mahesh Reddy, Yashesh Savani, Antoine Mercier et al.. MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils
items.summary: This paper addresses the longstanding challenge of determining the biological sex of individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils in prehistoric rock art, a problem complicated by the lack of ground truth, population variation, and image degradation over millennia. The researchers developed an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework that explicitly models and propagates uncertainty throughout the analytical pipeline, combining multiple image processing strategies, contour extraction techniques, and silhouette augmentation to generate numerous plausible realizations of each stencil's boundary. Two ensembles of deep neural networks with different architectures were trained on a large dataset of contemporary hand samples and then applied to the prehistoric stencils, with predictions further validated through unsupervised dimensionality reduction and explainable AI methods to ensure anatomical consistency. On contemporary data the ensembles achieved strong classification accuracy, particularly for older age groups, and when applied to prehistoric stencils the framework produced both sex attributions and quantified confidence measures that distinguish morphologically clear cases from ambiguous ones. The authors argue that by treating uncertainty as a measurable and informative component rather than an obstacle, their approach enables more robust and reproducible archaeological inference about the makers of ancient hand stencils.
items.citation: Karel Becerra, Boris Mederos, Dean Snow et al.. Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils. arXiv. 2026
