items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, noninvasive electronic nose could accurately detect SARS-CoV-2 infection as an alternative to conventional diagnostic methods. The device used an array of commercially available metal oxide gas sensors to analyze volatile organic compounds in both saliva and exhaled breath samples, with multiple machine learning algorithms applied to classify infected versus non-infected individuals. Detection accuracy varied across algorithms for both sample types, with the best performance achieved using the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm, which yielded area under the curve values approaching or exceeding the threshold considered clinically useful. The findings demonstrate proof-of-concept feasibility for this approach in a real-world hospital setting, suggesting that breath and saliva-based electronic nose testing could offer a rapid, comfortable, and affordable point-of-care screening option. The authors conclude that further development of this technology holds promise for improving early-stage SARS-CoV-2 detection.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.
items.summary: This study investigated the fungal microbiome (mycobiome) across multiple body compartments in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), a condition previously linked to bacterial dysbiosis but poorly characterized in terms of fungal communities. Using ITS1 amplicon sequencing of saliva, sputum, and stool samples from adults with CVID and healthy controls, the researchers analyzed fungal diversity, composition, and differential abundance, and applied machine learning to identify potential biomarkers. They found that mycobiome composition differed significantly between CVID patients and controls across all three niches, with reduced fungal richness and evenness particularly in respiratory and oral samples. A consistent enrichment of opportunistic yeasts, especially *Candida albicans*, was observed in CVID patients regardless of whether they had immune dysregulation or infectious-only manifestations, accompanied by depletion of commensal and environmental taxa. Fungal community profiles showed strong discriminatory power for distinguishing CVID from healthy controls, suggesting that mycobiome signatures hold promise as non-invasive biomarkers and that *C. albicans* expansion may play a pathobiont role in this immunodeficiency.
items.citation: Cabanero-Navalon MD, Carda-Diéguez M, Mira A et al.. Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.. Frontiers in immunology. 2026

items.title: Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether tuberculosis could be diagnosed using *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* DNA extracted from exosomes in saliva, offering a non-sputum-based alternative for detecting paucibacillary disease. The researchers developed a method called ExoNA-based saliva tuberculosis diagnostic, which integrates salivary exosome enrichment, nucleic acid extraction, and dual-target quantitative PCR melting curve analysis, reducing turnaround time substantially compared to conventional approaches. In a pilot clinical study enrolling adults with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis, the majority of whom had negative smear microscopy, the assay demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity against both standard and extended microbiological reference standards. Salivary exosomal DNA was found to be the predominant detectable form of *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* DNA in saliva, and diagnostic performance was maintained in the smear-negative subgroup. The authors conclude that this non-invasive, rapid assay holds promise for tuberculosis diagnosis but requires multicenter validation in more diverse populations before clinical implementation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Ma J, Zheng X, He Y et al.. Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that allow long-term wear and seamless integration with the body, alongside multimodal sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. It also explores how artificial intelligence contributes to signal processing and the generation of predictive health insights. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs, framing these as key obstacles to broader adoption.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles, with particular focus on the exosome subtype, covering their biological origins, functions, and emerging clinical applications. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how these membrane-bound particles are produced through the endosomal pathway, how they mediate intercellular communication by transporting diverse molecular cargoes, and how they can be isolated from biological fluids and cell cultures using methods such as ultracentrifugation, size-exclusion chromatography, and immunoaffinity capture. The review also surveys characterization techniques including nanoparticle tracking analysis, electron microscopy, and flow cytometry, which assess vesicle size, morphology, and surface markers. The authors highlight the therapeutic promise of extracellular vesicles as diagnostic biomarkers, drug delivery vehicles, and tools in regenerative medicine, while acknowledging persistent challenges in standardizing production, purification, and drug loading. They conclude that resolving these technical hurdles through robust, scalable protocols will be essential before extracellular vesicles can be successfully translated into routine clinical use.
items.citation: Madison Schank, Juan Zhao, L Wang et al.. Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential. Biomedicines. 2026

items.title: An integrated electrochemical platform for low-volume biosensing
items.summary: This paper describes the development of a fully integrated electrochemical sensing platform designed to overcome limitations of conventional screen-printed electrode workflows in low-volume biosensing applications. The system combines a custom three-dimensional-printed flow cell, a microfluidic pumping module, and a graphical user interface that synchronizes instrument control, data acquisition, and on-board analysis. Using double-stranded DNA as a model analyte, the platform was evaluated through chronoamperometry under continuous flow, demonstrating a linear calibration range and comparable signal quality to manual pipette-based delivery while improving reproducibility and reducing baseline drift and hands-on time. The platform also supported limited electrode reuse through an electrochemical regeneration step, with signal quality diminishing progressively over successive cycles. The authors conclude that the system provides a compact, programmable chassis suitable for low-volume assays with potential adaptation to point-of-care and field-deployable contexts.
items.citation: Fatma Kurul, Damla Aydoğan, Dogukan Topcu et al.. An integrated electrochemical platform for low-volume biosensing. npj Biosensing. 2026

items.title: Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions
items.summary: This review examines the role of biomaterials in drug delivery, focusing on how advances in polymers, metals, ceramics, composites, and nanostructured carriers have transformed therapeutic design toward personalized medicine. The authors surveyed how tunable physicochemical properties—including degradation kinetics, surface chemistry, and mechanical stability—enable controlled drug release, protection of sensitive therapeutics, and targeted accumulation at disease sites through diffusion-controlled, degradation-mediated, or stimulus-responsive mechanisms. Nanostructured platforms such as liposomes, micelles, and dendrimers were highlighted for their capacity to improve drug solubility, cellular uptake, and site-specific delivery through surface functionalization and ligand-mediated targeting. The review identifies persistent barriers to clinical translation, including immune–biomaterial interactions, batch-to-batch manufacturing variability, unpredictable long-term biodegradation, and regulatory scalability constraints. The authors conclude that future progress requires precision fabrication methods, manufacturing-practice-compatible production, and biologically informed design strategies that accommodate patient-specific variability to realize the full potential of personalized drug delivery.
items.citation: Adna Hrapović, Nadia Islam, Asmaa Al Bourghli et al.. Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions. PeerJ. 2026

items.title: Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application
items.summary: This review examined how polymer-based biosensors perform analytically when applied to complex real-world samples across food, environmental, and clinical contexts. The authors conducted a meta-trend analysis of nearly a hundred original research articles spanning a decade, evaluating four distinct polymer classes—conductive polymers, redox-mediator polymers, hydrogels, and molecularly imprinted polymers—against criteria including matrix interference, precision, stability, and validation completeness. Electrochemical detection was found to dominate the field, with each polymer class offering specific advantages, such as hydrogels preserving enzyme kinetics in protein-rich matrices and molecularly imprinted polymers enabling trace-level detection in harsh environments. However, the review identified serious validation gaps, as the vast majority of studies omitted limits of quantification and substantial fractions lacked reproducibility or precision reporting. The authors conclude that maintaining calibration integrity across different hostile sample matrices remains the central obstacle to commercial deployment, while emerging architectures such as nanocapsulation and microneedle-integrated systems present promising avenues to improve fouling resistance and operational stability.
items.citation: Marcello Mascini, Sara Palmieri, Fabiola Eugelio et al.. Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review
items.summary: This systematic review examined the scope and impact of artificial intelligence integration in medical devices, with a focus on how AI enables personalized, precision health care. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of peer-reviewed articles, industry analyses, and regulatory advisories published over a seven-year period, analyzing current applications, implementation barriers, and strategies to overcome them. The review found substantial advances in AI-driven diagnostics, treatment personalization, wearable health monitoring, and smart prosthetics, with some diagnostic tools demonstrating high classification accuracy across disease categories. Key challenges identified include data security vulnerabilities, algorithmic bias, patient privacy concerns, and difficulties integrating AI systems into existing health care infrastructures, though strategies such as improved data validation, updated regulatory frameworks, and ethical guidelines were found to help mitigate these issues. The authors conclude that while AI-driven personalization holds transformative potential for patient-centered medicine, realizing this potential requires coordinated technical, ethical, and regulatory progress, with emerging technologies like quantum computing and blockchain-based data management identified as promising future directions.
items.citation: Hemanth Ponnambalath Mohanadas, A Manikandan, Ahmad Fauzi Ismail et al.. Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitations of existing image editing benchmarks, which are confined to simple single-image tasks with narrow coverage and poor ability to distinguish between models. The authors propose CPI-Bench, a new benchmark comprising three subsets designed to evaluate general editing across diverse tasks including multi-image editing, practical high-frequency real-user application scenarios, and demanding reasoning-based editing capabilities. The benchmark was used to evaluate mainstream image editing models, revealing meaningful performance differentiation that prior benchmarks failed to capture. The results provide quantification of gaps across general, practical, and reasoning-based editing dimensions, offering guidance for future model optimization. Notably, the benchmark's rankings showed the strongest alignment with a human preference leaderboard among evaluated benchmarks, suggesting it faithfully reflects real-world user experience and serves as a robust proxy for human perceptual judgment.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump
items.summary: The paper describes a GPU-based implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics using a momentum-jump-free theoretical framework. To optimize performance on the GPU architecture, the authors eliminated trajectory spawning, which had been used on CPU implementations to enhance sampling but would introduce costly thread divergence and dynamic memory allocation on parallel hardware. The resulting implementation achieved roughly an order-of-magnitude speedup compared to the CPU approach with spawning, while also exhibiting linear scaling with the number of sampling trajectories.
items.citation: Koji Ando. GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of restoring high-resolution images, particularly at 4K resolution, where diffusion-based methods suffer from computational expense and texture inconsistencies. The authors developed MagnifiQ, a framework that progressively upscales degraded images through multiple intermediate resolution stages rather than attempting direct restoration at the target resolution. Their approach adapts a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model by replacing self-attention layers with convolutional operations that scale linearly with resolution, and incorporates patch-specific text prompts to provide spatially localized semantic guidance during restoration. Testing on both synthetic and real-world degraded images demonstrated that MagnifiQ outperforms prior diffusion-based restoration methods in perceptual quality and human preference, producing sharper textures and more globally coherent results at 4K resolution.
items.citation: Mahesh Reddy, Yashesh Savani, Antoine Mercier et al.. MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils
items.summary: This study addresses the long-standing challenge of determining the biological sex of individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils in ancient rock art, a problem complicated by the lack of ground truth, population variation, and image degradation over time. The researchers developed an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework that models and propagates uncertainty throughout the entire analytical pipeline, combining dual image processing, contour extraction, silhouette augmentation, and ensembles of two distinct deep neural network architectures trained on thousands of contemporary hand samples. Each prehistoric stencil was rendered into multiple plausible silhouette realizations to capture boundary ambiguity, and predictions were validated through a triangulated scheme incorporating unsupervised manifold mapping and explainable AI spatial attribution methods to ensure anatomical consistency. On contemporary hand data the ensemble models achieved strong classification accuracy, particularly in older age groups, and when applied to prehistoric stencils the framework produced sex attributions alongside confidence measures that distinguish morphologically stable cases from ambiguous ones. The authors conclude that uncertainty itself can be treated as a measurable and informative component of archaeological inference, enabling more robust and reproducible analysis of ancient rock art.
items.citation: Karel Becerra, Boris Mederos, Dean Snow et al.. Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Joint Estimation of Sparse Multilayer Networks via Graph Limits
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of jointly modeling multilayer network data, where multiple types of interactions occur among the same set of individuals. The authors represent multiplex networks using a nonparametric framework based on graph limits called scaled graphons, and develop a joint estimator called the multi-network histogram using blockmodel approximations that accounts for each layer's varying sparsity through shared latent variables. They derive theoretical guarantees for this estimator, including an upper bound on the weighted mean integrated squared error and the optimal bandwidth that minimizes it. A key finding is that jointly modeling layers reduces estimation error and allows for a smaller optimal bandwidth compared to single-layer approaches, enabling finer-resolution estimation even in sparser network layers. The method's practical value is demonstrated through simulations and an application to socioeconomic multiplex networks from an Indian village.
items.citation: Youngseok Song, Sofia C. Olhede. Joint Estimation of Sparse Multilayer Networks via Graph Limits. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting software vulnerabilities through static analysis, arguing that traditional rule-based approaches rely too heavily on syntactic patterns while neglecting the semantic meaning embedded in code. The authors propose SETYPE, a semantics-aware type system in which types are derived from the natural language meanings of variable and function names, with both type inference and type checking performed by large language models. A failed type check in this framework signals a potential vulnerability, enabling detection without manually encoded security rules. The approach was prototyped for Python web applications and evaluated on real-world software, achieving high precision and accuracy. The system successfully identified numerous previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities, the majority of which were subsequently confirmed by developers.
items.citation: Ruizhe Wang, Meng Xu, N. Asokan. Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for rapid, decentralized testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors surveyed a broad range of platforms—including lateral flow assays, biochips, and biosensors—organized around the three core operational steps of nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches such as magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods with an emphasis on simplicity and equipment-free operation. Amplification strategies reviewed include both thermocycling methods like PCR and isothermal alternatives such as LAMP, RPA, and NASBA, all adapted for portable and low-power use. On the detection side, the review spans colorimetric and fluorescent assays through to advanced biosensor platforms exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a syndromic molecular panel for central nervous system infections by comparing it against conventional cerebrospinal fluid culture at a national reference center over three years. Using a large dataset of paired molecular and culture results, the researchers calculated measures of diagnostic concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values across the full sample set and within the subset of pathogens specifically targeted by the panel. The syndromic panel demonstrated high specificity and a strong negative predictive value when restricted to its included bacterial targets, but its overall sensitivity was substantially lower, reflecting the limitations of its fixed pathogen coverage. Critically, conventional culture identified clinically important organisms not included in the panel, such as certain staphylococcal and streptococcal species as well as rare environmental pathogens, underscoring that the syndromic panel cannot serve as a standalone diagnostic tool. The authors conclude that optimal management of central nervous system infections requires systematic integration of both approaches, and advocate for next-generation multiplex platforms with broader target coverage guided by real-world epidemiological data.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Sberna G, D'Arezzo S, Valli MB et al.. Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.
items.summary: This study evaluated a rapid molecular diagnostic tool for detecting Group A *Streptococcus* (*Streptococcus pyogenes*) from pediatric pleural fluids, a clinical setting where accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and public health contact tracing. The researchers compared the performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A, a quantitative real-time PCR assay originally designed for throat swabs, against bacterial culture and a laboratory-developed PCR assay targeting a different gene, using a composite reference standard. Testing a convenience sample of pediatric pleural fluid specimens that included both positive and negative cases, the Xpert assay achieved perfect agreement with the composite reference standard and the laboratory-developed PCR, detecting all positive specimens, while culture alone identified only a minority of those same positive cases. The findings demonstrate that the Xpert assay is substantially more sensitive than culture for recovering *S. pyogenes* from pleural fluid, likely because many patients had received antibiotics prior to sample collection. The authors conclude that Xpert offers a rapid and highly accurate alternative for diagnosing invasive Group A streptococcal disease from sterile site specimens in pediatric patients, with faster turnaround times supporting timely clinical and public health decision-making.
items.citation: Amaral G, Gadkar VJ, Almodahka A et al.. Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a versatile and sustainable platform for addressing challenges across energy, environmental, and healthcare sectors. The authors survey the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies of graphene oxide, highlighting how its layered architecture enables surface functionalization, tunable band gap, high surface area, and adjustable hydrophobic or hydrophilic character across structural configurations ranging from zero to three dimensions. The review covers a broad range of applications, including adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, carbon dioxide photoreduction, photocatalytic hydrogen production, battery technologies, ultra-sensitive molecular detection via surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and healthcare platforms. The authors emphasize that graphene oxide can function effectively as a standalone material rather than solely as a composite component, underscoring its transformative and multifunctional potential. However, the review also acknowledges persistent challenges surrounding scalability, long-term stability, reproducibility, and health concerns, and proposes possible solutions to enable sustainable real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance with a focus on bacterial pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these pathogens evade existing antibiotics, including reduced membrane permeability, efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic discovery pipelines have failed to keep pace with resistance and assesses a range of emerging therapeutic strategies—such as artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds—while addressing their translational, regulatory, and clinical obstacles. The authors also emphasize that delivery challenges, toxicity, dosing optimization, and the risk of resistance emergence remain significant barriers for next-generation approaches. They conclude that combating priority-resistant pathogens will require integrated, multidisciplinary efforts spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, antimicrobial stewardship, and a One Health framework that connects human, animal, and environmental health sectors.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry
items.summary: Researchers investigated chitosan–eugenol carbon dots as a multifunctional nanomaterial platform for dental applications, motivated by the need for materials that simultaneously control infection and support tissue regeneration. The carbon dots were synthesized from biocompatible chitosan and eugenol, then characterized for their physical and chemical properties using electron microscopy and elemental analysis, while their biological performance was assessed through antibacterial assays against the caries-associated pathogen Streptococcus mutans and cytocompatibility testing with fibroblast cell cultures. The resulting nanoparticles were spherical and nanoscale in size, with elemental analysis confirming successful incorporation of heteroatoms and surface functionalization. The material demonstrated concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans and showed strong biocompatibility, with fibroblast cells maintaining viability, normal morphology, and enhanced migratory behavior indicative of wound-healing potential. The authors conclude that combining chitosan and eugenol within a carbon dot framework yields a promising multifunctional nanoplatform capable of addressing both oral infection control and tissue repair in dental therapeutic contexts.
items.citation: N. Narayanan, Aruchamy Mohanprasanth, Natesan Thirumalaivasan. Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances
items.summary: This review examines bacterial biofilms — structured microbial communities encased in a self-produced extracellular polymeric substance matrix — focusing on their biology, clinical significance, and the therapeutic challenges they pose. The authors synthesize current knowledge on biofilm development stages, matrix composition, and the physiological heterogeneity that emerges during maturation, alongside the multiple resistance mechanisms that make biofilms difficult to eradicate, including restricted antibiotic diffusion, enzymatic inactivation, efflux pump upregulation, persister cell formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review maps the clinical contexts in which biofilms are implicated, spanning cystic fibrosis, chronic wounds, osteomyelitis, implant-associated infections, and breast implant illness, where persistent biofilms are hypothesized to drive local and systemic inflammatory manifestations. Conventional and emerging detection methods, including real-time monitoring approaches, are also discussed alongside treatment strategies that pair antibiotics with matrix-disrupting enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, bacteriophages, metabolic reactivators, and nanotechnology-based delivery systems. The authors conclude that effective management of biofilm-associated infections requires integrated strategies combining accurate detection with multifaceted therapies, and that advances in multi-omics and systems-level modeling will be critical for developing next-generation preventive and therapeutic approaches.
items.citation: Pranay Amruth Maroju, Angad S. Sidhu, Amogh R. Motaganahalli et al.. Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the IceCube neutrino detector can probe dark matter that has been accelerated to relativistic speeds by blazar jets, a mechanism that circumvents the usual sensitivity limitations of direct-detection experiments for light dark matter. The researchers computed the diffuse flux of boosted dark matter from a large sample of blazars, using proton spectra inferred from multiwavelength observations and conservative dark matter spike profiles around central supermassive black holes, while carefully accounting for propagation and attenuation effects. The dark matter–nucleon scattering cross section was modeled to include elastic, resonant single-pion production, and deep inelastic scattering contributions, with particular attention paid to smoothly bridging the transition between elastic and deep inelastic regimes. Applying this framework to IceCube neutrino data, the authors derived constraints on model parameter space and found that this approach can surpass conventional direct-detection experiments for dark matter masses below approximately one GeV. They further found that the signal is dominated by deep inelastic scattering and is therefore most sensitive to heavier mediators, while resonance processes moderately suppress the event rate near the detection threshold.
items.citation: Alberto M. Gago, Jaime Hoefken Zink, Joel Jones-Pérez et al.. Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters
items.summary: This paper investigates the origin of very high energy gamma-ray emission from young massive stellar clusters, focusing on how cosmic rays escape their acceleration sites and propagate through the surrounding medium. The authors developed a theoretical framework showing that mirror diffusion combined with pitch-angle scattering in turbulent magnetic fields produces an energy-dependent diffusion coefficient proportional to the cube root of energy, which suppresses cosmic-ray transport compared to standard diffusion. They coupled three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a young massive stellar cluster with Monte Carlo cosmic-ray propagation calculations, using the cluster W43 as a benchmark and testing both a central point source and a spherical shell injection geometry. They found that this suppressed diffusion regime, combined with a standard cosmic-ray injection spectrum, successfully reproduces the gamma-ray spectra observed by Fermi and LHAASO, whereas stronger energy-dependent diffusion requires an unusually hard injection spectrum to match the data. A key conclusion is that the observed gamma-ray emission is determined primarily by the diffusive propagation regime rather than by where within the cluster the cosmic rays are injected, with the relative contributions of leptonic and hadronic emission processes also depending sensitively on the diffusion model.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
items.citation: Lucas Barreto-Mota, Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino, Gaetano Di Marco et al.. Cosmic Ray Diffusion and the Origin of Very High Energy Gamma-Ray Emission in Young Massive Stellar Clusters. arXiv. 2026

This redesign achieved a speedup of an order of magnitude relative to CPU calculations that include spawning, and the approach scales linearly with the number of sampling trajectories.

items.title: MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of restoring high-resolution images, particularly at 4K resolution, where diffusion-based methods suffer from computational expense and tend to produce repeated or inconsistent textures. The approach adapts a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model by replacing self-attention layers with convolutional operations that scale linearly with image resolution, and incorporates patch-specific text prompts to provide spatially localized semantic guidance that controls content drift during restoration. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world degraded images demonstrate that MagnifiQ outperforms prior diffusion-based restoration methods in perceptual quality and human preference, yielding sharper textures and more globally coherent 4K outputs while offering favorable speed–quality trade-offs.

items.title: A remark on the full support property
items.summary: The paper studies stability conditions on projective schemes over a field, focusing on the support property, which is a key technical condition in the theory of Bridgeland stability conditions. The authors prove that a mass-upper-bound condition called a mass-Hom bound for a numerical pre-stability condition implies the support property with respect to the full numerical Grothendieck group, rather than just a quotient of it. By combining this result with recent constructions of stability conditions on projective schemes, they establish the existence of stability conditions satisfying the full support property on every projective scheme over a field, and extend this to a uniform statement in the relative setting. Additionally, they show that the distinguished connected component of the full numerical stability manifold does not depend on the choice of polarization, yielding a canonical component intrinsic to the scheme.
items.citation: Yiran Cheng. A remark on the full support property. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils
items.summary: This paper addresses the longstanding challenge of determining the biological sex of individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils in prehistoric rock art, a problem complicated by the lack of ground truth, population variation, and image degradation over time. The researchers developed an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework that combines dual image processing, contour extraction, silhouette augmentation, and ensembles of two different neural network architectures trained on a large dataset of contemporary hand samples. The pipeline generates multiple silhouette realizations per stencil to capture boundary uncertainties, and integrates ensemble predictions with unsupervised dimensionality reduction and explainable AI techniques to validate anatomical consistency. Applied to contemporary data, the ensemble models achieved strong classification accuracy, particularly in older age groups, and when deployed on prehistoric stencils the framework produced both sex attributions and quantified confidence measures that distinguish morphologically stable from ambiguous cases. The authors conclude that uncertainty can be treated as a measurable and informative component of archaeological inference, enabling more robust and reproducible analysis of ancient rock art.
items.citation: Karel Becerra, Boris Mederos, Dean Snow et al.. Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.
items.summary: This study investigated whether synthetic peptide epitopes derived from *Streptococcus agalactiae* surface proteins could serve as the basis for an ELISA-based immunodiagnostic test for Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women. Three epitopes from the bacterial proteins GroEL, enolase, and EF-Tu were selected and tested against serum samples from GBS-positive and GBS-negative individuals using IgG, IgM, and IgA antibody detection. All three peptides, whether used individually or in combination, significantly distinguished between GBS-positive and GBS-negative sera, with the enolase- and EF-Tu-derived epitopes performing best as individual candidates due to their higher immunoreactivity at lower concentrations. Combining epitopes in various mixtures further enhanced immunoreactivity compared to single-peptide assays. The authors conclude that this epitope-based ELISA represents a promising and potentially pioneering alternative to the current culture-based gold standard, which is slow and can yield ambiguous results.
items.citation: Brzychczy-Włoch M, Dobrut A, Drożdż K et al.. Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.. Applied microbiology and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the LIAISON PLEX Gram-Positive Blood Culture Assay, a multiplexed molecular test designed to rapidly identify gram-positive bacterial pathogens and antibiotic resistance markers directly from positive blood culture bottles. The assay was assessed across prospective, pre-selected, and contrived blood culture samples in a multisite design, testing its ability to detect and differentiate thirteen gram-positive bacterial targets and four antibiotic resistance markers. The assay demonstrated a very high valid rate and achieved strong overall sensitivity and specificity across all targets, with robust inclusivity results and minimal cross-reactivity among off-panel species. Performance was maintained in the presence of potential interfering substances, in polymicrobial infection scenarios, and across blood culture bottles from multiple manufacturers. The authors conclude that the assay offers fast, accurate, and reliable detection of gram-positive organisms and their resistance genes, with potential to support antibiotic optimization and patient management in bloodstream infection care.
items.citation: Chow S-K, Stevig C, Granato P et al.. Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for faster and simpler detection of Group B Streptococcus colonization in pregnant women, a key risk factor for neonatal infections and preterm stillbirth. The researchers developed and validated an in-house rapid diagnostic assay combining CRISPR/Cas12a technology with recombinase polymerase amplification, an isothermal method that does not require thermocycling equipment. Specificity was tested against other common reproductive tract pathogens, and the detection limit was established using serially diluted plasmids, with clinical performance evaluated using vaginal-rectal swabs from pregnant women compared against a commercial quantitative real-time PCR method. The assay completed detection within one hour, with results readable either visually via colloidal gold test strips or through a fluorescence reader, and it accurately distinguished Group B Streptococcus from non-target pathogens. Clinical evaluation demonstrated that the rapid assay results correlated closely with conventional PCR, supporting its potential as a high-sensitivity, high-specificity alternative for point-of-care prenatal screening.
items.venue: International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM
items.citation: Hu S, Xie J, Liu L et al.. Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.. International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM. 2026

items.title: Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the real-world diagnostic performance and clinical utility of multiplex polymerase chain reaction panels designed to detect multiple pathogens simultaneously from cerebrospinal fluid in patients with suspected meningitis or encephalitis. Researchers retrospectively reviewed five years of testing data at a tertiary care hospital, examining pathogen detection rates, co-detection frequencies, repeat testing yield, and whether positive results led to documented changes in diagnosis or treatment. Viral pathogens dominated the positive findings, with bacterial detections also present, and co-detections occurred in a notable proportion of positive cases. Despite the technology's capacity for rapid, broad pathogen identification, fewer than half of positive results were associated with a clinically meaningful action, and repeat testing after an initial negative result offered little additional diagnostic value. The authors conclude that while these panels hold genuine diagnostic potential for central nervous system infections, their clinical impact is undermined by inappropriate test ordering and insufficient clinician familiarity with panel content, calling for clearer testing criteria and better-targeted use.
items.venue: The Indian journal of medical research
items.citation: Gürler M, Karaoğlu Ç, Yurtcu EE et al.. Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.. The Indian journal of medical research. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviewed advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from roughly the first half of the 2020s, synthesizing evidence to inform updated WHO policy guidance on detection of tuberculosis disease and drug resistance. The review covers a broad range of technologies and approaches, including digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool, expanded deployment of rapid molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, novel specimen types including tongue swabs and stool, and emerging near point-of-care platforms. Molecular drug-resistance testing has also advanced, with targeted next-generation sequencing now recognized for comprehensive drug-susceptibility profiling at reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays improve diagnostic yield in people with HIV and advanced disease despite performance limitations. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarker signatures show promise for triage and prognosis but no candidate has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The authors conclude that despite meaningful progress, substantial gaps in performance, implementation, and equity remain, underscoring ongoing developmental priorities.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of a centrifugal microfluidic platform designed for simultaneous point-of-care detection of multiple respiratory pathogens, including influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. The system integrates lyophilized reagents into independent reaction chambers on a chip, paired with a portable analyzer that automates sample handling, isothermal amplification, and real-time fluorescence detection in a two-step workflow. The platform achieved extremely low limits of detection with no cross-reactivity against a broad panel of non-target pathogens, and clinical validation using a large set of positive samples demonstrated complete agreement with quantitative PCR. The entire detection process is completed within fifteen minutes using very small reaction volumes, making the system well suited for decentralized testing environments.
items.citation: He P, Feng Y, Zhou X et al.. Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Development and evaluation of a rapid duplex qPCR assay for Treponema pallidum using the GeneSoC microfluidic platform.
items.summary: The paper studied the development and evaluation of a rapid molecular diagnostic assay for detecting Treponema pallidum, the causative agent of syphilis, with an emphasis on suitability for point-of-care testing. The researchers designed a duplex quantitative PCR assay targeting two genomic regions and implemented it on the GeneSoC microfluidic platform, testing it against DNA standards, a reference strain, and clinical specimens including lesion swabs and urine, both with and without prior DNA extraction. The assay demonstrated good linearity and amplification efficiency across the tested concentration range, with no cross-reactivity against other pathogens and qualitative agreement with a conventional comparator assay. A key finding was that detection could be completed within fifteen minutes directly from clinical specimens without DNA extraction, substantially faster than the comparator system, owing to the microfluidic platform's superior thermal cycling speed. The authors note that while extraction-free testing is feasible, DNA extraction may enhance sensitivity when target DNA is present in low quantities.
items.citation: Kawahata T, Banno F, Hama M. Development and evaluation of a rapid duplex qPCR assay for Treponema pallidum using the GeneSoC microfluidic platform.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing modalities. The paper systematically organizes the field around three core operational steps: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection, covering a wide range of platforms including lateral flow devices, biochips, and biosensors. Extraction strategies discussed include magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches, with emphasis on simplicity and equipment-free operation, while amplification methods such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP are reviewed for their adaptation to portable and low-power conditions. Detection platforms are surveyed from conventional colorimetric and fluorescent assays to advanced biosensors incorporating CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, which provide highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition. The review concludes that these combined technological advances are driving point-of-care diagnostics toward sensitive, selective, and economically viable infectious disease testing outside traditional laboratory settings.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical nucleic acid amplification test that combines isothermal amplification with real-time voltammetric detection for diagnosing infectious diseases at the point of care. The approach works by monitoring the proton release that accompanies nucleic acid amplification using a pH-sensing redox compound, addressing optical detection limitations common to existing isothermal methods like LAMP. The system was evaluated against RT-qPCR across multiple respiratory pathogens including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, and RSV A, achieving high concordance with the reference method in purified RNA from clinical samples. A proof-of-concept extraction-free workflow using equine nasal swabs correctly classified all samples for a equine herpesvirus relative to qPCR. The authors conclude that real-time voltammetric LAMP is feasible across diverse sample types and pathogens, though further validation in additional sample matrices and prospective cohorts is needed.
items.citation: Munita R, Lyttleton R, Danefur E et al.. A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.. ACS omega. 2026

items.title: Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.
items.summary: This review paper examined isothermal nucleic acid amplification methods as alternatives to conventional PCR-based diagnostics. The authors surveyed the principles, detection strategies, and applications of the most widely used techniques, including loop-mediated isothermal amplification, helicase-dependent amplification, rolling circle amplification, strand displacement amplification, nucleic acid sequence-based amplification, and recombinase polymerase amplification. Unlike PCR, these methods operate at a constant temperature and do not require thermal cycling equipment, making them particularly suited to resource-limited settings that demand rapid, affordable, and simple diagnostic tools. The review synthesizes information on reaction mechanisms, product detection approaches, and disease diagnostic applications into a single comprehensive resource, addressing a gap in the existing literature where no unified overview had previously covered all these aspects together. The authors also discuss the future prospects of isothermal amplification methods and their potential to broaden access to genomic testing across research and clinical contexts.
items.citation: Amare Amdiyee A, Sisay Tessema T. Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques: A comprehensive overview on their principle & applications as alternative to PCR.. Practical laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection
items.citation: Michelle N. Vu, R. Elias Alvarado, Dorothea R. Morris et al.. Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines biosensing technologies designed for the rapid and accurate detection of priority foodborne pathogens, with a focus on their relevance to both food safety and clinical healthcare settings. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, exploring how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor systems to enable intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing, effectively transforming conventional detection devices into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically assesses current challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward next-generation, regulation-ready food safety monitoring platforms.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey
items.summary: This survey examines the intersection of foundation models and computational healthcare through a data-centric lens, focusing on how these AI systems can address longstanding challenges in clinical data acquisition, quality, and processing. The authors review a broad range of data-centric approaches spanning the full lifecycle of foundation models—from pre-training through inference—and how these approaches can improve healthcare workflows. The survey addresses critical concerns including data annotation, patient privacy, ethical considerations, and AI security, as well as the alignment of these models with human values. The authors find that the interactive, instruction-guided nature of foundation models represents a paradigm shift toward emphasizing data quality and scale rather than model architecture alone, offering new opportunities for clinical applications. The survey concludes with an optimistic outlook on the potential of foundation model-based analytics to enhance patient outcomes and streamline clinical workflows.
items.citation: Yunkun Zhang, Jin Gao, Zheling Tan et al.. Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey. ACM Computing Surveys. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a major cause of hospital-acquired bloodstream infections characterized by high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning epidemiology, species distribution, and infection origins, while critically evaluating the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods that contribute to harmful delays in appropriate treatment. The review surveys emerging diagnostic technologies alongside therapeutic strategies that include both empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, addressing mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance. Combination therapy and novel agents currently in clinical trials targeting new fungal pathways are highlighted as promising approaches to overcoming resistance. Looking ahead, the authors identify artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment strategies as directions likely to shape future candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language model agents can reliably modernize legacy Fortran scientific software while preserving not just nominal behavior but also fault-response characteristics. The authors developed a differential fault-injection validation framework that instruments a shared computational driver and applies identical, deterministic faults to both original and modernized code, allowing the two implementations to be compared under stress conditions rather than only under normal execution. Testing was conducted on the self-consistent-field driver of a quantum chemistry package, targeting integral kernels converted by the language model, across thousands of injection runs covering transient faults, persistent perturbations, and reduced-precision scenarios. The experiments revealed phase-dependent parallel deadlocks and false convergence under reduced precision, while demonstrating that the modernized kernels behaved identically to the originals across all paired injection trials. The work establishes differential fault injection as a principled complement to nominal testing for validating LLM-driven code modernization, and shows that additional synchronization fixes compose cleanly with the modernization without introducing divergence.
items.citation: Evan Coleman, Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina et al.. Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive lecture course on entropy spanning both classical and quantum settings, aimed at readers with backgrounds in mathematics and theoretical physics. The classical treatment develops entropy through large deviation theory, connecting foundational results to both Boltzmannian and Gibbsian statistical mechanics. On the quantum side, the course traces how quantum entropies relate to their classical counterparts both formally and more deeply through their role in statistical hypothesis testing, covering the Kullback-Leibler relative entropy, its quantum generalization due to Umegaki, and Rényi deformations within this unified framework. The course then addresses the substantially harder problem of defining relative entropy for states on subsystems described by von Neumann algebras, requiring modular theory and Haagerup's noncommutative function spaces to recover and extend the constructions of Araki and Uhlmann. Finally, the course introduces a quantum analogue of the Kolmogorov-Sinai dynamical entropy in the von Neumann algebraic setting, with the entire treatment motivated by potential relevance to black hole thermodynamics while remaining mathematically rigorous throughout.
items.citation: Klaas Landsman. The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of identifying and tracking roles that network nodes play as graph structure evolves over time. The authors developed a dynamic role discovery method based on temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization, which enforces consistency in role definitions across time steps and penalizes abrupt changes in role membership to improve robustness against noise. Unlike prior approaches, the method produces a single unified set of roles valid across all time periods alongside a universal transition matrix describing the likelihood of moving between roles. The approach was evaluated on multiple real-world and synthetic datasets using both engineered and automatically generated node features, demonstrating reduced role prediction errors compared to competing techniques. Analysis of the transition matrices further showed that the learned system is more stable, with nodes tending to remain in their roles rather than switching arbitrarily, and the method scales efficiently to large, sparse graphs.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
items.summary: This paper introduces Twin (Test-time World-model Inference), a system designed to play unknown grid games by having a frontier coding agent construct an executable world model purely through simulation and interaction, without any hand-engineered task-specific designs. The system works by requiring that a world model accurately reproduce every previously observed game transition before any action is taken, using mismatches between predictions and actual outcomes as counterexamples to iteratively repair the model. Twin was evaluated on a continual learning benchmark of grid games and achieved near-complete success, clearing the vast majority of levels with efficiency exceeding that of first-time human players on most of them. A key finding was that the system could infer the game's goal before receiving any reward signal on the majority of cleared levels, with the remaining cases handled through automated search. The authors conclude that constructing a usable world model is more tractable than anticipated, while inferring the correct goal representation emerges as the more challenging subproblem.
items.citation: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano et al.. Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational complexity of deciding whether two tournaments are isomorphic, a problem recognized as a key bottleneck in the broader graph isomorphism problem. The authors focus on tournaments of bounded VC dimension, a class of combinatorial structures for which neither hardness nor polynomial-time algorithms were previously known, and resolve an open problem by providing a quasi-polynomial algorithm whose running time is polynomial in the exponent with respect to the VC dimension parameter. To achieve this, they develop an isomorphism-invariant decomposition method for tournaments, introduce the concept of patched tournaments to enable recursion, and exploit the structure of near twins to balance the size and number of decomposed pieces. As a complementary result, they also establish that tournament isomorphism is polynomial-time decidable for tournaments of bounded chromatic number, addressing the class that characterizes unbounded VC dimension in hereditary tournament families. Together, these results significantly advance the understanding of tractable cases for tournament isomorphism.
items.citation: Simon Raßmann, Pascal Schweitzer. Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Geometry-Conforming Finite Element Methods for Interface Problems on Fitted and Unfitted Meshes
items.summary: This paper develops a geometry-conforming finite element framework for solving elliptic boundary value and interface problems on two-dimensional curved domains. The approach uses the Frenet–Serret transformation to represent curved boundaries and interfaces exactly, generating nonpolynomial local shape functions in physical coordinates that conform to the prescribed geometry without approximation. For meshes that do not align with interfaces, the framework couples geometry-conforming spaces on curved-boundary elements with geometry-conforming immersed finite element spaces on interface-cut elements. The authors establish rigorous theoretical results including optimal approximation, inverse, and trace estimates, as well as well-posedness and optimal energy and norm error estimates for a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin discretization on fitted meshes. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate that the method avoids the geometric variational crime inherent in conventional curved-geometry approximation, achieving accuracy comparable to isoparametric finite elements while yielding smaller interface trace errors in reported tests.
items.citation: Yuanhui Lin, Tao Lin, Xu Zhang et al.. Geometry-Conforming Finite Element Methods for Interface Problems on Fitted and Unfitted Meshes. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.
items.summary: This study examined whether multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests, capable of detecting multiple respiratory viruses simultaneously, could be feasibly integrated into routine primary care in New Zealand. A prospective mixed-methods pilot was conducted across seven primary care clinics during winter, combining electronic medical record audits with surveys, interviews, and focus groups involving both patients and clinicians. The tests were administered to patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms as a broader alternative to COVID-19-only testing, and outcomes related to acceptability and clinical utility were assessed. Both clinicians and patients responded positively to the tests, with all clinicians finding them useful in practice and a majority reporting that results influenced antibiotic prescribing decisions. The authors conclude that these tests were readily incorporated into primary care workflows and may improve management of common respiratory illnesses while encouraging patients who test positive to adopt transmission-reducing behaviours.
items.citation: Bibby S, Marsh S, Dowell A et al.. Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.. BJGP open. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.
items.summary: This study evaluated a lateral flow immunoassay-based antigen rapid diagnostic test capable of simultaneously detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus from nasopharyngeal swab specimens. The test's performance was assessed against real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction as a reference standard using archived specimens, and cross-reactivity was examined against a panel of respiratory viral and bacterial pathogens. The test demonstrated high sensitivity across all four viral targets in specimens with high viral loads and achieved perfect specificity with no cross-reactivity observed against any of the tested microorganisms. Sensitivity was reduced in specimens with low viral loads, leading the authors to conclude that the test is reliable as a rapid screening and initial differentiation tool but should complement rather than replace molecular testing.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kang M, Yu HJ et al.. Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients
items.summary: This study investigated the disease burden of respiratory syncytial virus infection in adult patients at a Japanese clinic by testing nasopharyngeal swabs collected from individuals presenting with acute respiratory infection symptoms. Samples were analyzed using rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests capable of detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, and RSV simultaneously. While cases of SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A were detected with reasonable frequency and one influenza B case was identified, no RSV-positive cases were found among the patients tested. Comparison with prior studies that employed polymerase chain reaction testing revealed a statistically significant difference in RSV detection rates, with PCR identifying RSV in a notable proportion of adult patients. The authors conclude that rapid immunochromatographic antigen testing has limited utility for diagnosing RSV infections in Japanese adults, likely due to insufficient sensitivity compared to PCR-based methods.
items.citation: Kajiwara N, Tsunetoshi Y, Shiode S. No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients. 2026

items.title: Performance of an antigen test for detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus-a prospective study.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multiplex rapid antigen test capable of simultaneously detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus in patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms. Using a prospective design, symptomatic patients including children were tested with both the nasal swab antigen test and a separately collected nasopharyngeal PCR sample, with antigen test analysis performed by emergency department staff and PCR conducted in a central laboratory. The test demonstrated high sensitivity for all four viral targets when using a PCR cycle threshold cutoff intended to reflect infectious viral loads, along with perfect specificity across all agents and age groups. A notable finding was that nasal swabs absorbed less viral RNA than nasopharyngeal swabs, a difference that reached statistical significance for influenza A in the broader patient population but not in children. The authors conclude that the test's performance supports its potential utility as a marker of infectiousness in acute clinical care settings.
items.venue: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the long-standing question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper contrasted the generally accepted benefits of regular moderate-intensity exercise for immune defense with the high infection burden reported among elite athletes and military personnel performing arduous physical activity. Opposing expert groups debated key contested issues, including whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently drives increased infection risk apart from confounding factors such as sleep disruption, anxiety, nutritional deficits, and travel, and whether current biomarkers and study designs are adequate to address these questions. Both groups agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but could not resolve whether exercise per se is a direct causative factor in elevated infection risk among those performing high-intensity training. The authors conclude that the debate highlights a need for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from the many coexisting variables in these populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple databases to gather existing evidence from patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations with spinal cord injury. Spinal cord injury disrupts autonomic function and alters catecholamine concentrations at rest and following exercise, which likely directly suppresses immune cells given that the vast majority of lymphoid cells express adrenergic receptors, with these effects being especially pronounced in individuals with tetraplegia. However, some immune responses to exercise, such as increases in natural killer cell cytotoxicity and mucosal immunity changes in those with tetraplegia, appear independent of catecholamine alterations and may resemble responses seen in able-bodied individuals, suggesting compensatory mechanisms such as sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or neuroendocrine adjustments may offset injury-related immune deficits. The authors conclude that exercise and rehabilitation therapy show promise as tools to maintain or improve immune and autonomic function following spinal cord injury, and call for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and their implications for infection susceptibility.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria L. Goosey‐Tolfrey, Nicolette C. Bishop. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026
