items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper examined graft-versus-host disease, a serious multi-systemic complication arising from allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in which donor lymphocytes attack host tissues, causing substantial morbidity and reduced physical capacity in long-term survivors. The authors reviewed the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease, with particular attention to its chronic form, alongside available evidence from both animal and human studies on the effects of exercise as an adjunct therapy. Their review found that exercise training shows promise for improving physical fitness and potentially immune function while reducing fatigue in affected patients, though the evidence base remains limited. The authors conclude that more randomized controlled trials specifically targeting patients with graft-versus-host disease are needed before firm recommendations can be made.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with the goal of identifying more effective therapeutic targets. The authors synthesized current knowledge on nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system, as well as pathological changes in bone and cartilage driven by inflammatory cytokines and organelle dysfunction. They highlight three key intracellular processes that drive disease progression: mitochondrial dysfunction with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization leading to chondrocyte apoptosis, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress that exacerbates cartilage degradation. Based on these mechanistic insights, the review proposes a multimodal therapeutic framework targeting inflammatory cascades, organelle homeostasis restoration through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and nociceptive signaling attenuation. The authors also emphasize the potential of organelle-targeted drug delivery systems to improve the efficacy and stability of these emerging treatments.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Bispecific T cell engagers for treatment-refractory autoimmune connective tissue diseases
items.summary: This study investigated the use of bispecific T cell engager (TCE) therapies in patients with severe, treatment-refractory autoimmune connective tissue diseases, specifically antisynthetase syndrome and systemic sclerosis. Under compassionate use, patients with antisynthetase syndrome received the CD19×CD3 TCE blinatumomab, while patients with systemic sclerosis received the BCMA×CD3 TCE teclistamab, with both groups subsequently receiving rituximab as maintenance therapy to inhibit B cell redifferentiation. Both TCEs reduced their respective target cells in affected tissues and lowered autoantibody titers, with blinatumomab producing clinical, serological, and histological improvements in myositis and stabilization of interstitial lung disease, and teclistamab improving skin fibrosis, stabilizing interstitial lung disease, and resolving tendon friction rubs. Notably, maintenance rituximab achieved prolonged disease control even in patients who had previously failed rituximab therapy alone. Treatment was associated with adverse events including cytokine release syndrome up to grade 3 and respiratory infections, though no neurotoxicity syndrome was observed, suggesting these agents may serve as potential rescue therapies for refractory disease.
items.citation: Christina Düsing, Andrea‐Hermina Györfi, Ayla Nadja Stütz et al.. Bispecific T cell engagers for treatment-refractory autoimmune connective tissue diseases. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: This paper addresses the limitations of existing image editing benchmarks, which are restricted to simple single-image tasks and fail to distinguish performance across diverse models in complex, real-world settings. The authors developed CPI-Bench, a new benchmark comprising three subsets targeting general editing diversity (including multi-image tasks), high-frequency practical user scenarios, and reasoning-intensive editing instructions. Evaluations of mainstream image editing models using this benchmark demonstrated improved differentiation between models across general, practical, and reasoning-based editing capabilities. Ranking analysis further showed that CPI-Bench achieves the strongest alignment with a human-preference leaderboard, suggesting it reliably reflects real-world user judgments and can serve as a robust proxy for human perceptual evaluation.
items.citation: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du et al.. CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language model agents can reliably modernize legacy Fortran scientific software while preserving not just nominal behavior but also fault tolerance and numerical robustness. The researchers developed a differential fault-injection validation framework that applies identical, deterministic perturbations to both original and LLM-modernized code at multiple instrumentation sites within a shared computational driver, isolating the converted components for comparison. Testing focused on integral kernels within a quantum chemistry software package, examining responses to transient faults, persistent perturbations, and reduced floating-point precision across thousands of runs. The fault injection campaigns revealed phase-dependent parallel deadlocks and false convergence under reduced precision, while also producing quantitative models of how fault absorption costs scale with the number of corrupted bits. The original and modernized kernels agreed across all paired injection experiments, and a synchronization fix motivated by the campaign's findings also composed correctly with the modernization, supporting the method's utility for validating LLM-driven code transformations beyond simple correctness checks.
items.citation: Evan Coleman, Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina et al.. Validating LLM-Modernized Scientific Software Through Differential Fault Injection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy
items.summary: This paper presents a set of lecture notes providing a comprehensive treatment of entropy in both classical and quantum settings, aimed at bridging mathematical rigor with physical intuition. The classical theory is developed through the lens of large deviation theory, connecting foundational results to Boltzmannian and Gibbsian statistical physics, while quantum entropies are motivated through their deep role in statistical hypothesis testing. The treatment covers a progression from familiar Kullback-Leibler and Umegaki relative entropies to their Rényi deformations, and then to the more abstract setting of von Neumann algebras where Araki and Uhlmann relative entropies are defined using modular theory. Haagerup's noncommutative spaces are introduced to make these abstract quantum entropies tractable in terms of density operators and traces, and the Connes-Størmer-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy is presented as a quantum analogue of the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from ergodic theory. The course was motivated by connections to black hole thermodynamics, though that application itself is not covered, and it is designed to be accessible to readers with backgrounds in probability theory, functional analysis, and quantum theory.
items.citation: Klaas Landsman. The Okinawa Lectures on Entropy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of discovering and tracking roles that network nodes occupy as graph structures evolve over time. The authors developed a dynamic role detection method based on temporally regularized Non-negative Matrix Factorization, which enforces consistency of role definitions across time periods and penalizes abrupt changes in role membership to handle real-world noise. A key contribution is the derivation of a universal transition matrix describing the probability of nodes moving between roles over time, rather than producing role sets that vary independently at each time step. The method was evaluated on multiple real-world and synthetic datasets using both engineered and automatically generated node features. Results show that appropriate regularization reduces prediction error compared to competing techniques, and transition matrix analysis confirms that the approach produces more stable role assignments with fewer arbitrary node transitions.
items.citation: Emily J Evans, Weihong Guo, Carlotta Domenicon. RegRole: Regularized Role Detection and Prediction in Temporal Dynamic Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
items.summary: This paper introduces Twin, a Test-time World-model Inference system designed to play unknown grid games by constructing an executable world model entirely from simulation and interaction, without any hand-engineered rules. A frontier coding agent writes and continuously repairs this world model, enforcing that it correctly reproduces every previously observed game transition before any action is taken, with mismatches used as counterexamples to refine the model. The system was evaluated on a continual learning benchmark of grid games similar to ARC-AGI-3, where the rules and goals are hidden from the player. Twin successfully cleared nearly all levels with high action efficiency compared to human players, and was able to infer the correct goal before receiving any reward on the majority of levels it completed. The authors conclude that constructing a usable world model is more tractable than expected, but that inferring the correct goal from interaction alone represents the harder and more fundamental challenge.
items.citation: Alexy Skoutnev, Kirill Acharya, Gaston Longhitano et al.. Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational complexity of determining whether two tournaments (complete directed graphs) are isomorphic, a problem that has resisted classification for decades and represents a key bottleneck in graph isomorphism research. The authors resolve an open problem by proving that tournament isomorphism can be decided in quasi-polynomial time when the tournaments have bounded VC dimension, a central measure of combinatorial complexity. To achieve this, they develop a new isomorphism-invariant decomposition method for tournaments, introduce the concept of a "patched tournament" to enable recursion, and design a recursive algorithm that exploits near-twin structure while balancing piece size against piece count. As a consequence, automorphism groups of tournaments with bounded VC dimension can be computed in polynomial time. In a complementary result, the authors also establish that tournament isomorphism is polynomial-time decidable for tournaments of bounded chromatic number, addressing the class of tournaments that characterizes unbounded VC dimension via hereditary closure.
items.citation: Simon Raßmann, Pascal Schweitzer. Isomorphism of tournaments with bounded VC dimension. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future trajectory of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with an emphasis on platforms suitable for clinical and field deployment. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, exploring how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional instruments into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent obstacles such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, summarizing how emerging evidence has shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. The review covers developments across screening, diagnosis, and drug-resistance testing, including the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a frontline screening tool and the diversification of molecular diagnostic platforms enabling more decentralised testing. Progress in testing non-sputum specimen types such as stool, gastric aspirate, nasopharyngeal samples, and tongue swabs has improved bacteriological confirmation in children and other populations unable to produce sputum, while advances in rapid molecular drug-resistance testing and next-generation sequencing have strengthened reference laboratory capacity. Urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic benefits for people living with HIV who have advanced disease, though performance limitations restrict broader application. Despite these gains, the review identifies persistent performance, implementation, and equity gaps, and notes that while host transcriptomic and other biomarker signatures show promise for prognosis and triage, no biomarker yet meets WHO criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing tuberculosis infection from disease, including subclinical forms.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis, motivated by the urgent diagnostic demands exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases and synthesized evidence on molecular assays, antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suited to decentralized settings, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening despite variable performance depending on viral load and circulating variants. Antibody-based assays were identified as more appropriate for seroprevalence and retrospective applications than for acute infection detection, and emerging biosensor and AI tools showed promise but remain largely at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical evidence. The review concludes that no single testing modality is universally optimal, and that complementary deployment of these approaches, alongside advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient design, will be essential for both COVID-19 management and broader pandemic preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped the landscape of research combining artificial intelligence with point-of-care and rapid diagnostic technologies for infectious diseases in resource-limited settings. Following established scoping review methodology, the authors searched five major databases covering publications from early 2015 through early 2026, screening over a thousand records and ultimately including more than two hundred studies. The field showed exponential growth in publication volume, with the majority of work concentrated on COVID-19, malaria, and tuberculosis, while neglected tropical diseases were markedly underrepresented, and convolutional neural networks were the dominant analytical approach across imaging-based modalities such as microscopy and biosensors. Geographically, research was heavily concentrated in East Africa and South Asia, leaving West Africa and Latin America largely understudied. The authors identified a critical gap in research rigour, finding that the vast majority of studies lacked prospective field validation, and they call for future work to prioritise real-world validation, broaden disease coverage beyond the dominant triad, and meaningfully involve end-user communities from the earliest stages of development.
items.venue: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
items.citation: Farquhar H. AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.. Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for rapid multiplexed detection of respiratory pathogens at the point of care. The system integrates CRISPR/Cas13a chemistry with lyophilized reagents pre-loaded onto a spinning disc and a portable fluorescence analyzer, enabling automated processing after sample loading, along with a novel resin-based method to purify and concentrate nucleic acids from throat swabs. The platform can simultaneously screen six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples in under an hour, achieving single-copy analytical sensitivity without cross-reactivity between targets. Clinical validation using retrospective patient throat swabs demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity, supporting the platform's accuracy for decentralized testing. The authors conclude that iCARD represents a robust and high-throughput molecular diagnostic tool suitable for point-of-care deployment and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.
items.summary: This review examines point-of-care testing technologies for infectious diseases, focusing on their role in early screening, epidemic surveillance, and public health prevention. The authors systematically surveyed recent advances across molecular diagnostics, microfluidic systems, biosensing technologies, and artificial intelligence as applied to rapid diagnostic platforms. They also analyzed the quality assessment frameworks used to evaluate these technologies, including key performance indicators such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, stability, and field applicability. Particular emphasis is placed on deployment strategies for resource-limited settings, addressing technical optimization, resource allocation models, and local support infrastructure. The review concludes by identifying current challenges and proposing future development directions to guide further research and implementation of infectious disease point-of-care testing.
items.citation: Zhang YX, Ru JF. Point-of-care testing (POCT) for Infectious diseases: technological innovation, effectiveness evaluation, and application strategies in resource-limited regions.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Strongyloides screening, diagnostics, therapeutics, and management.
items.summary: The paper reviews recent advances in the screening, diagnosis, treatment, and management of strongyloidiasis, a parasitic infection that remains widely underdiagnosed despite its potentially fatal consequences in immunocompromised individuals. On the diagnostic front, molecular methods using nucleic acid amplification have superseded traditional parasitologic approaches, and new rapid diagnostic tests based on recombinant antigens have improved point-of-care serologic screening compared to standard immunoglobulin-based assays. Treatment options are expanding, with moxidectin demonstrating non-inferiority to the established standard ivermectin, and emodepside showing promising cure rates in early trials through a mechanistically distinct mode of action. The World Health Organization has conditionally recommended mass drug administration of ivermectin in highly endemic communities, and updated screening recommendations now reflect a broader understanding of which immunosuppressed populations face the greatest risk of severe hyperinfection. The authors conclude that while diagnostic and therapeutic tools are improving, harmonized screening algorithms and prospective studies in high-risk groups remain critical priorities given limited data in severe disease and special populations.
items.citation: Clark EH, Nutman TB. Recent advances in Strongyloides screening, diagnostics, therapeutics, and management.. Current opinion in infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents the updated recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for managing rheumatoid arthritis using synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. An international task force conducted systematic literature reviews on the efficacy and safety of these therapies, then used a structured voting process to revise and consolidate guidance from the previous update. The resulting framework was streamlined to fewer recommendations organized around overarching principles covering conventional synthetic, biological, and targeted synthetic agents, including Janus kinase inhibitors. The recommendations endorse starting with methotrexate combined with short-term glucocorticoids, escalating to a biologic agent after an inadequate response, and considering Janus kinase inhibitors with careful attention to risks such as major cardiovascular events, malignancies, and thromboembolic events. Guidance is also provided on treat-to-target strategies, sequencing after treatment failure, and cautious tapering in sustained remission, with high levels of evidence and agreement supporting most recommendations.
items.citation: Josef S. Smolen, Christopher J. Edwards, Victoria Konzett et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in support of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that allow long-term wear and seamless integration with the body, alongside multimodal sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also assessed. Despite notable progress, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. The authors synthesize findings across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to provide a comprehensive overview of the field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the anticipated trajectory of the food and medicine homology field as it transitions from traditional empirical knowledge toward contemporary scientific frameworks. The authors outline a vision centered on scientific rigor, mechanistic understanding, precision medicine principles, and modernization of the industrial chain through advanced technologies. Key research directions identified include active component identification, multisystem interaction mechanisms involving gut microbiota, and emerging biological processes such as phase separation and immunometabolic reprogramming. Applications are expected to shift toward dynamic, personalized health management using multidimensional data and artificial intelligence to address chronic diseases and aging populations. The paper also anticipates industrial transformation through synthetic biology, intelligent delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing practices to create a more transparent and evidence-based ecosystem.
items.citation: Mengyao Li, Gui-Fen Wu, Feng Lu et al.. Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026. Food & medicine homology.. 2026

items.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
items.summary: The paper argues that systems using language models to draw conclusions from multiple sources make a design error by conflating two fundamentally distinct operations: interpreting individual sources and aggregating those interpretations into a final decision. The authors propose separating these operations and define a structured four-field evidence tuple as the interface between them, which they argue fully determines the design of both components. They identify a failure mode they term count-scale drift, wherein summing unnormalized weights causes the effective decision threshold to shift with the number of sources consulted, and show that the vote rule and posterior ordering diverge when source reliabilities differ, with no single threshold able to reconcile them. Pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios is presented as an arithmetic rather than architectural fix that resolves both problems and generalizes beyond language models to any score-summing system. The framework is validated on a longitudinal corpus in both retrospective and prospective settings, where the proposed separation yields strong predictive performance on a survival task, and the authors explicitly enumerate falsifiable predictions, negative results, and remaining confounds.
items.citation: Zhelun Wu. Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of embedding constrained optimization solvers into end-to-end learned systems, where fixed-depth unrolling forces difficult trade-offs among solution quality, feasibility, and computational cost. The authors propose Residual-Controlled Douglas–Rachford Splitting, a differentiable solver layer for conic linear programs that treats the unrolled solver as a feedback-controlled dynamical system, using a causal controller to adaptively tune relaxation and objective-drive parameters while preserving the projection-splitting structure of Douglas–Rachford splitting. Theoretically, they establish that each admissible block remains an averaged relaxed operator and admits finite-step fixed-point residual bounds, and they analyze time-varying rollouts as summable perturbations of a limiting averaged operator to recover primal-dual diagnostics from the final solver state. Experiments on mixed-cone benchmarks and engineering applications demonstrate that the proposed method improves solution quality, feasibility, and downstream decision performance compared to fixed-depth unrolling approaches.
items.citation: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu. Residual-Controlled Douglas--Rachford Splitting for Differentiable Solver Layers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate whether self-evolving AI agents can adapt code-based physical designs when the underlying physics of their environment changes. The benchmark consists of source-to-target adaptation pairs spanning six physics domains, where a design that succeeds under source conditions must be iteratively revised to work under mutated target conditions using sandbox feedback within a limited attempt budget. Ten self-evolving methods representing four paradigms were compared, revealing that the benchmark is far from solved and that simulator-grounded reflection outperforms unverified self-revision, while memory mechanisms anchor agents to early designs and broad tree search fails to converge. Notably, providing agents with exact information about the physical changes did not substantially raise performance, suggesting that the core challenge is mechanism redesign rather than parameter inference. These findings highlight fundamental limitations in current self-evolving agents when faced with dynamic environmental conditions requiring structural adaptation rather than incremental refinement.
items.citation: Yuhao Zhan, Bingxiang He, Zecong Tang et al.. PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations
items.summary: This paper investigates how intrinsic dimensionality, a common measure of representational complexity in language models, is affected by properties of datasets rather than language itself. The researchers focused specifically on lexical diversity, defined as the number of unique final tokens in a dataset, and examined how it influences intrinsic dimensionality estimates across different scales. They discovered a scale-dependent transition between two distinct regimes: at low lexical diversity, fewer unique final words paradoxically yield higher intrinsic dimensionality, while at high lexical diversity this relationship reverses. The researchers derived an exact, parameter-free formula that accurately predicts the transition point between these two regimes at every scale tested. Their findings caution against straightforward interpretation of intrinsic dimensionality as a reflection of representational complexity, while also revealing a general organizational principle governing how linguistic data is structured within language model representations.
items.citation: Arwa Osman, Marco Baroni, Iuri Macocco. Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: TRIAGE: Risk-Controlled Pseudo-Label Admission for Annotation-Efficient Semi-Supervised Retinal OCT Classification
items.summary: TRIAGE addresses the challenge of automating retinal disease diagnosis from optical coherence tomography scans, where annotation costs are high because labeling requires specialist expertise. The paper proposes a semi-supervised learning framework that departs from conventional confidence-based pseudo-label selection by incorporating an asymmetric cost matrix that treats different types of classification errors unequally, reflecting the clinical reality that under-grading disease severity is more dangerous than over-grading. The framework combines a hierarchical classifier that can accommodate partial supervision of disease subtypes, a patient-grouped conformal risk controller using primal-dual optimization for coverage guarantees, and a context-aware Transformer teacher that performs cross-slice verification across volumetric scans. Evaluated on a hospital-derived dataset with unseen test patients, TRIAGE achieves strong scan-level accuracy and macro-level classification metrics using only a small fraction of labeled data, substantially reducing under-grading rates compared to fixed-threshold semi-supervised baselines. The framework generalizes to additional multi-class OCT datasets, maintaining high accuracy even when labeled data is reduced to as little as one percent.
items.citation: Md Ashraful Hossen Akash, Shyla Afroge, Abdullah Al Mamun et al.. TRIAGE: Risk-Controlled Pseudo-Label Admission for Annotation-Efficient Semi-Supervised Retinal OCT Classification. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AppleScab-LT: A Longitudinal Real-Field Apple Scab Dataset for Temporal Disease Progression Analysis
items.summary: This paper introduces AppleScab-LT, a longitudinal dataset designed to capture the temporal progression of apple scab disease under natural field conditions, addressing the lack of time-series data in existing plant disease image repositories. The researchers conducted systematic orchard monitoring, repeatedly tracking and photographing individually identified infected leaves across multiple observation points, then applied expert-guided disease verification, polygon-based annotation, and rigorous quality assurance protocols throughout dataset curation. The resulting dataset comprises longitudinal leaf sequences, thousands of high-resolution images, and progressive temporal samples that capture variability in disease severity accumulation, progression rates, and inter-leaf differences. Quantitative disease descriptors based on pixel severity, color-intensity severity, and normalized relative severity are included to provide standardized measurements for temporal analysis. The authors position AppleScab-LT as a foundational resource for disease progression modelling, temporal disease intelligence, and precision agriculture applications.
items.citation: Aamir Hilal, Shabir Ahmad Sofi, Neeraj Goel. AppleScab-LT: A Longitudinal Real-Field Apple Scab Dataset for Temporal Disease Progression Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An expanded codebook of human transcription factor DNA-binding specificity
items.summary: This paper investigated the DNA-binding specificities of hundreds of poorly characterized or previously unstudied human transcription factors, aiming to expand the known vocabulary of sequence recognition in the human genome. The researchers conducted a large systematic effort involving thousands of independent experiments using multiple in vitro and in vivo assays to determine binding motifs for these transcription factors. Motifs were successfully identified for roughly half of the transcription factors tested, the majority of which were associated with a single protein, extending the known repertoire of human transcription factor binding specificities by over a hundred distinct motifs. The study demonstrated that motifs identified through in vitro methods are strongly enriched at cellular binding sites, validating their biological relevance. Collectively, the findings reveal tens of thousands of previously unknown conserved transcription factor binding sites across the human genome, particularly concentrated in promoter regions where they are predictive of gene expression.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it substantially expands the catalog of how human transcription factors recognize DNA, uncovering more than 100 previously unknown binding motifs. By employing multiple complementary assays that capture different dimensions of DNA sequence specificity, it provides a richer resource for characterizing transcription factors whose functions were not yet well understood.
items.citation: Arttu Jolma, Kaitlin U. Laverty, Ali Fathi et al.. An expanded codebook of human transcription factor DNA-binding specificity. Nature. 2026

items.title: Ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities driving plasma mixing on the Sun
items.summary: Using the world's first four-meter class solar telescope, researchers obtained high-spatial-resolution observations of the solar photosphere to investigate the interaction between magnetic fields and turbulent convection at scales previously beyond observational reach. They examined time sequences of images focusing on the edges of magnetic flux concentrations in a magnetically active region of the photosphere. The observations revealed ubiquitous magnetized Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities at the boundaries of these flux concentrations, providing the first experimental confirmation of a long-standing theoretical prediction. These instabilities, which could be reproduced by high-resolution numerical simulations, drive plasma mixing and have implications for understanding magnetic field creation and dissipation, flux braiding through vortex motion, and the transport of mass, energy, momentum, and magnetic flux in magnetohydrodynamic systems. The findings also support theoretical models in which disjoint magnetic field concentrations beneath the solar surface connect to the monolithic flux structures visible in the photosphere.
items.why_notable: The work is drawing attention because new high-spatial-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal that Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities—previously considered rare or localized—are in fact ubiquitous drivers of plasma mixing on the Sun, painting a far more complex and dynamic picture of solar surface activity than had been seen before.
items.citation: D. Kuridze, Friedrich Wöger, M. van Noort et al.. Ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities driving plasma mixing on the Sun. Nature. 2026

items.title: ZFP36L2 orchestrates stress-adaptive plasticity in regeneration and cancer
items.summary: This paper investigated the molecular mechanisms controlling phenotypic plasticity during intestinal regeneration and colorectal cancer metastasis, focusing on how differentiated cells can revert to an intestinal stem cell state. The researchers examined the RNA-binding protein ZFP36L2, which is mutated in a subset of colorectal cancers, using mouse colon regeneration models and human colorectal cancer systems. They found that ZFP36L2 acts as a stress-responsive molecular switch that binds AU-rich sequences in stress-associated messenger RNAs and promotes the formation of biomolecular condensates linked to mRNA degradation, thereby terminating the stress response and enabling cellular dedifferentiation. Loss of ZFP36L2 impaired intestinal regeneration and stem cell gene expression in mice, while in human colorectal cancer it blocked canonical metastatic outgrowth from the LGR5-positive stem cell state and instead promoted non-canonical lineage plasticity into heterogeneous, poorly differentiated cell states associated with worse clinical outcomes. The work identifies ZFP36L2 as a pivotal coupler of stress sensing and cell-fate reprogramming that is essential for both wound healing and metastatic progression.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a single RNA-binding protein as a key orchestrator of how cells adapt to stress during both normal tissue regeneration and the spread of colorectal cancer, suggesting a shared molecular mechanism linking these two processes.
items.citation: Qingwen Jiang, Manisha Raghavan, Aileen M. Rodriguez et al.. ZFP36L2 orchestrates stress-adaptive plasticity in regeneration and cancer. Nature. 2026

items.title: In situ particle-to-fibre transformation of hydrogels for 3D printing

items.title: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours
items.summary: This study investigated how amygdala astrocytes contribute to stress-related behavioural changes, with a particular focus on their primary cilia and associated signalling mechanisms. The researchers examined astrocyte alterations during stress at the protein and gene expression level, finding that stress reduces expression of cilia-related molecules and results in morphologically shorter primary cilia in amygdala astrocytes. Using chemogenetics and targeted activation of the native G protein-coupled receptor sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1, the researchers were able to restore primary cilia length, correct molecular disruptions, and improve stress-related behaviours in mice. Selective genetic disruption of amygdala astrocyte primary cilia in mice independently altered stress-related behaviours and gene expression across multiple cell types, confirming a functional role for astrocytic cilia in this brain region. The authors also found that cilia-related genes and the target receptor are abundantly expressed in human amygdala astrocytes and show disrupted expression in stress-related brain disorders, suggesting that astrocyte primary cilia mechanisms may represent a novel therapeutic avenue for stress-related conditions.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it identifies a previously underappreciated cellular structure — primary cilia on amygdala astrocytes — as a key player in stress-related behavior, showing that disruption of these cilia occurs during stress and that restoring them can improve stress behaviors in mice.
items.citation: Sara G. Pelaz, Katsukuni Mitsui, Natalia Kołosowska et al.. Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours. Nature. 2026

items.title: A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models
items.summary: This paper investigated how next-generation three-dimensional cancer models, specifically organoids and spheroids, could expand the Cancer Dependency Map by addressing limitations of traditional two-dimensional cell lines in capturing cancer diversity and biology. The researchers conducted genome-scale CRISPR screens alongside multi-omic profiling across a large collection of these next-generation models spanning multiple cancer types. They found that these models cover previously underrepresented genomic and molecular cancer subtypes, preserve transcriptional programs that are silenced in conventional cell lines, and reveal gene dependencies linked to those preserved programs. The study also demonstrated that growth format and culture medium independently influence gene essentiality, highlighting how experimental context shapes dependency profiles. The combined dataset from traditional and next-generation models was integrated into the DepMap portal, offering an expanded resource for identifying cancer vulnerabilities and potential therapeutic targets.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it expands a key resource for understanding cancer vulnerabilities by integrating CRISPR screening data from more advanced, next-generation cancer models alongside traditional cell lines, thereby broadening coverage of tumour subtypes and genomic alterations in The Cancer Dependency Map.
items.citation: James Neiswender, Samuel Maffa, Lisa Brenan et al.. A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models. Nature. 2026

items.title: An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of reducing hardware overhead in quantum error correction by engineering qubits whose most frequent errors are also the easiest to correct. The researchers designed and experimentally realized a two-qubit entangling gate for dual-rail cavity qubits, a type of erasure qubit encoded in pairs of superconducting microwave cavities. Their gate is fast and demonstrates very low erasure rates, residual Pauli errors well below the erasure rate, and an extreme bias toward dephasing over bit-flip errors, thereby preserving the desired error hierarchy throughout gate operation. Surface code simulations were used to support the claim that this hierarchy translates into substantially improved fault-tolerant performance and faster suppression of errors as systems scale. The results represent a concrete experimental step toward practical quantum error-corrected systems with reduced resource overhead.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates a fast, low-error entangling gate that maintains a strong error hierarchy in dual-rail cavity erasure qubits, a property considered important for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
items.citation: Nitish Mehta, James D. Teoh, Taewan Noh et al.. An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits. Nature. 2026

items.title: A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
items.summary: This paper describes the creation of a large international repository of laboratory cancer models intended to better represent the diversity of human cancers for preclinical research. The Human Cancer Models Initiative generated hundreds of next-generation models, including tumor organoids, derived from thousands of donors spanning a wide range of cancer types, including rare cancers and donors of non-European ancestry. To assess whether these models faithfully capture the properties of the original patient tumors, the researchers performed comprehensive multi-omic analyses—including whole genome, exome, methylome, transcriptome, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing—on matched tumor-model pairs. They found high genetic and epigenetic concordance between tumors and their derived models, while also identifying factors associated with discordance and showing that certain culture conditions can meaningfully shift cellular states. The resource, which includes molecular profiling data, clinical information, and integrative software tools, is being made publicly available to support investigation of cancer mechanisms, therapeutic resistance, and treatment response.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it provides a large-scale, publicly available collection of next-generation cancer models spanning a wide range of cancer types, paired with multi-omic characterization linking each model back to the donor tumor. Such a comprehensive resource is expected to serve as a foundational reference for cancer research and drug discovery communities worldwide.
items.citation: Dina ElHarouni, Mushriq Al‐Jazrawe, Seongmin Choi et al.. A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers. Nature. 2026

items.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
items.summary: This paper introduces Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model designed to address the computational challenges posed by spatial proteomics technologies applied to cancer tissue analysis. The core problem is that existing methods are typically tailored to single cohorts using specific marker panels and protocols, making it difficult to transfer knowledge across studies or robustly identify biomarkers. VirTues learns multi-scale representations spanning proteins, cells, niches, and whole tissues directly from multiplex imaging data, enabling a single pretrained model to perform diverse tasks including marker reconstruction, cell segmentation, niche annotation, and zero-shot annotation across heterogeneous datasets. Applied to triple-negative breast cancer, the model's derived biomarkers successfully predicted patient response to anti-PD-L1 chemo-immunotherapy and stratified disease-free survival in an independent cohort. VirTues outperformed both state-of-the-art computational biomarkers derived from the same datasets and current clinical stratification approaches, demonstrating the value of a generalist foundation model for spatial proteomics.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because a single foundation model can analyze tissue organization across multiple biological scales simultaneously, performing a wide range of tasks—from reconstructing missing markers to stratifying patients—across diverse datasets and experimental panels. Its broad versatility in spatial proteomics positions it as a potentially transformative tool for both basic research and clinical applications.
items.citation: Johann Wenckstern, Eeshaan Jain, Benedikt von Querfurth et al.. The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales. Nature. 2026

items.title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
items.summary: This study investigated whether latent viruses reactivate during acute COVID-19 infection and whether such reactivation is associated with long COVID outcomes. Using longitudinal multi-omic data from a large cohort of hospitalized COVID-19 patients, the researchers tracked reactivation of Herpesviridae and Anelloviridae families over time, characterizing immune, transcriptomic, and metabolomic signatures associated with these events. The findings revealed that viral reactivation was common, correlated with disease severity and clinical outcomes, and notably occurred in immunocompetent individuals during severe illness rather than being restricted to immunosuppressed patients. Reactivation was associated with heightened systemic inflammation, and viral shedding persisted into convalescence, with Anelloviridae reactivation specifically linked to long COVID. These results challenge the assumption that latent viral reactivation requires an immunocompromised host and suggest it may play a role in shaping COVID-19 trajectories and post-acute sequelae.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it links the chronic reactivation of specific latent viruses during COVID-19 to disease severity, inflammation, and clinical outcomes. The findings suggest these reactivation patterns carry immune signatures that could help predict patient prognosis in both acute and long COVID-19.
items.citation: Cole Maguire, Jing Chen, Nadine Rouphael et al.. Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19. Nature. 2026

items.title: A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies
items.summary: This study established a large biobank of clinically annotated tumour organoids derived directly from patient tissue across five gastrointestinal and gynaecological cancer types, generating renewable and genetically stable three-dimensional models that better capture tumour diversity than traditional cell lines. Each model was extensively characterized using whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing, and genome-wide CRISPR–Cas9 screens were performed across a substantial subset to systematically map gene dependencies. Integrative analyses identified genomic and clinical markers associated with specific dependencies, including organoid-specific essential genes and targetable vulnerabilities revealed by comparing paired pre- and post-treatment samples to track tumour evolution. In colorectal cancer, functional and pharmacological interrogation of the EGFR–RAS–MAPK signalling axis demonstrated that different KRAS variant alleles produce distinct biological effects. The resulting resource is publicly available and is intended to broaden model diversity and deepen mechanistic understanding in support of precision oncology.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it creates a large, clinically annotated organoid resource derived directly from patient tumours that links molecular profiles to gene dependencies across multiple cancer types. By revealing subtype-specific vulnerabilities and treatment-driven changes, it offers new tools and mechanistic insights to advance precision oncology.
items.citation: C. Herranz-Ors, Shriram G. Bhosle, A. E. Beck et al.. A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies. Nature. 2026

items.title: DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation
items.summary: This paper developed an unbiased, broadly applicable platform for discovering molecular glue degraders across diverse E3 ligases using multiplexed mass spectrometry-based chemical screening. The researchers identified a compound called M12, which functions as a prodrug that is activated through glutathione S-transferase-mediated glutathionylation, after which the glutathione moiety binds to an evolutionarily conserved site on the E3 ligase DCAF11. This activation reprograms DCAF11 to recruit and degrade the neo-substrate DDX18 via the ubiquitin proteasome system. The study further demonstrated that this glutathione-dependent mechanism can be broadly applied to achieve targeted degradation of a range of proteins beyond DDX18. These findings establish that metabolically activated compounds can redirect E3 ligase function, expanding the scope of targeted protein degradation and chemically induced proximity approaches.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it describes a molecular glue degrader that is activated by a cellular metabolic process—glutathionylation—to recruit diverse target proteins for destruction, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism for expanding targeted protein degradation.
items.citation: Hojong Yoon, Franziska Wachter, Katharine A. Barrett et al.. DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation. Nature. 2026

items.why_notable: Observations of a magnetar's polarized X-ray emission have provided strong evidence for vacuum birefringence—a prediction of quantum electrodynamics in which extreme magnetic fields alter how light propagates through empty space. This offers a rare direct observational test of quantum electrodynamics under conditions far beyond what can be achieved in laboratories.

items.title: An ancient mitochondrial program tunes translation to haem availability
items.summary: This paper investigated how cells sense and respond to haem deficiency, a key problem underlying anaemia and haemoglobin disorders. The researchers discovered that haem scarcity is detected within mitochondria via an OMA1–DELE1 signalling axis, whereby low haem triggers OMA1-dependent release of DELE1 into the cytosol. Once in the cytosol, DELE1 displaces inhibitory haem from the kinase HRI, enabling HRI activation and consequent translational regulation during erythroid differentiation. This pathway is conserved across human tissues and even in bloodless invertebrates, indicating it evolved long before haemoglobin-based oxygen transport emerged. Pharmacological manipulation of the system was shown to boost fetal globin expression, suggesting therapeutic relevance for haemoglobinopathies such as thalassaemia and sickle cell disease.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it uncovers an ancient, evolutionarily conserved mechanism by which mitochondria sense haem availability to regulate translation, predating haemoglobin-based oxygen transport. Its potential therapeutic relevance to iron deficiency disorders adds significant biomedical interest.
items.citation: Xiang Zhang, Max-Hinderk Schuler, Gonca Çetin et al.. An ancient mitochondrial program tunes translation to haem availability. Nature. 2026

items.title: Maps of chromosomal regions crucial for cell division reveal high diversity
items.summary: The study investigated centromeres, the chromosomal regions essential for cell division, by comprehensively sequencing and characterizing them across a genetically diverse group of individuals. This large-scale sequencing effort produced detailed maps of centromeric regions that had previously been difficult to resolve. The findings reveal that centromere sequences undergo dynamic and rapid mutational change, evolving quickly both between generations and over longer evolutionary timescales spanning hundreds of thousands of years. This high diversity and rapid evolution provides new insights into how centromeres function and how they have changed throughout human evolutionary history.
items.why_notable: The work is attracting attention because it provides the first complete sequence maps of centromeres—chromosomal regions essential for cell division—across a diverse set of individuals, revealing unexpectedly rapid and dynamic mutational change. These findings offer new insight into how centromeres evolve and carry out their critical function in cell division.

items.title: Switching off the FNIP1 gene protects against metabolic disease
items.summary: The paper investigated whether naturally occurring genetic variants that disrupt the FNIP1 gene have consequences for metabolic health in humans. Using a very large population dataset, researchers identified rare loss-of-function variants in FNIP1 and found they are associated with a markedly reduced risk of cardiometabolic disease and a broadly favorable metabolic profile. To explore the underlying mechanisms, the team silenced genes in the FNIP1 pathway in mice and observed enhanced fat breakdown along with metabolic improvements that mirrored those seen in human carriers of the variants. The findings suggest that the FNIP1 pathway plays a meaningful role in regulating metabolism and represents a potential therapeutic target for cardiometabolic disease.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a genetic variant that substantially lowers the risk of cardiometabolic disease in humans, and demonstrates in animal models that silencing the same biological pathway replicates those protective metabolic effects, suggesting a promising therapeutic target.
items.citation: Switching off the FNIP1 gene protects against metabolic disease. Nature. 2026
